Details: Unused in stock: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 7 of 8 (index 6 of FFF8CDB0), which is masked: bit 6 of cal 0x1B97D is set (0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off for every slot). 0x0E51E4 (read) then writes a fixed ratio for the channel instead of 256 x measured/reference, and the reference ref_6 (the only place this step enters, statics FFF84AB4..FFF84AD0 read only by 0x0E51E4, ram_xref) is not used; the reference copies FFF8C130.. have no reader. So editing it has no effect unless that cal bit is cleared, which would make the channel count (then this would be the background step for FFF8C190[6] when FFF8A7C3 changes; overlap flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F). Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 0 everywhere. Confidence: read.

table.name: Timing Retard High Load (1st Gear)
table.description:
Timing pulled at high load in 1st gear (by rpm and load), used only above about 2800 rpm and 0.84 g/rev (65 % load) and not in neutral. Raising values adds retard. Not used if knock control is switched off. Stock up to about 2.1 degrees.
Details: When used: 0x0DF3EC (called from 0x0DF0B8, args read): FFF8A779 = -(cal 0x2FE3E (23) x value >> 7) half-degrees, a retard term in the final timing sum FFF8A744 of 0x0D9E40 (read). Normal path: the table for the current gear FFF8A621 (1-5; gear 6 and 0 give 0) is used only while rpm FFF8CD54 >= cal 0x2FE44 (2800 rpm, hysteresis cal 0x2FE46 = 100 rpm) and load FFF8ADE4 >= cal 0x2FE40 (65 %, hysteresis cal 0x2FE42 = 15 %), and is forced to 0 while FFF88ADA bit 6 (neutral switch, discrete input FFF8A29E bit 5 = pin PH5, Phase 16) is set (read). Fault path: while FFF88E2B bit 1 (set by the failed status of U0073/U0101/U0122/U0140/U0402/U0416/U0422/U0423/U0155 = CAN communication faults, 0x080B96 area, read) or (manual coding FFF886AB bit 7 and FFF88E28 bit 0 = P0500/P2158 vehicle-speed faults) is set, the 3rd-gear table is used at every gear, rpm and load. All of it is 0 while cal 0x56EE7 bit 7 (knock control off) is set (read). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (2000-5600 rpm, 80-160 %). Scaling assumes cal 0x2FE3E = 23. Stock 0-23 counts = up to 2.1 degrees. Gear meaning of FFF8A621 inferred. p16 (read): confirmed - FFF88E2B bit 1 is the OR of the test-failed bits FFF81315 b0-b6 / FFF8131E b2-b3 (0x080B96) = U0422/U0140/U0402/U0101/U0416/U0122/U0073/U0423/U0155. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Start (Below 200 km/h)
table.description:
Delay, in 10 ms steps after a sudden throttle opening (tip-in), before the tip-in timing retard starts, by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Stock 0, so the retard starts immediately.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 below cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h), latched on the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears. First 10 ms pass of the retard window (retard applies from this pass count up to the End table), by rpm FFF8CD5C (x25) (read). Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). On the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (Tip-In Timing Retard End) are latched by rpm/25. FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes < end, engine state 3, rpm within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA and speed below 200 km/h or 200-250 km/h; amount = code cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) (stock 0/0/20/20 for codes 1-4) + Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder. Afterwards FFF8A772 falls each pass by min(255, decay table(rpm/25) x FFF8A760), FFF8A760 = combustion events since the previous pass (0x0DC7E8 on the per-event counter FFF8A780, 0x0DFEF8), i.e. by the table value per combustion event. 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 (0.5-degree units) from the timing request FFF8A76A (read). Stock 0 (retard from the first pass). Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (Below 200 km/h)
table.description:
How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used below 200 km/h. Larger values give timing back faster. Stock 1 degree per event (a 10 degree retard is gone in 10 events).
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 below cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h), every pass (looked up by rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, R5 at 0x0DDDBE, read); acts once the retard window has ended or its conditions fail. Ramp-out of the tip-in retard in degrees per combustion event. Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). On the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (Tip-In Timing Retard End) are latched by rpm/25. FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes < end, engine state 3, rpm within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA and speed below 200 km/h or 200-250 km/h; amount = code cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) (stock 0/0/20/20 for codes 1-4) + Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder. Afterwards FFF8A772 falls each pass by min(255, decay table(rpm/25) x FFF8A760), FFF8A760 = combustion events since the previous pass (0x0DC7E8 on the per-event counter FFF8A780, 0x0DFEF8), i.e. by the table value per combustion event. 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 (0.5-degree units) from the timing request FFF8A76A (read). Stock 1.0 degree per combustion event at all rpm (10 degrees gone in 10 events). Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Decay (From 200 km/h)
table.description:
How fast the tip-in timing retard is removed once its window ends, in degrees per combustion event by rpm; used at 200 km/h and above. Larger values give timing back faster. Stock 1 degree per event.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 at or above cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h), every pass (looked up by rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, R5 at 0x0DDDBE, read); acts once the retard window has ended or its conditions fail. Ramp-out of the tip-in retard in degrees per combustion event. Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). On the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (Tip-In Timing Retard End) are latched by rpm/25. FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes < end, engine state 3, rpm within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA and speed below 200 km/h or 200-250 km/h; amount = code cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) (stock 0/0/20/20 for codes 1-4) + Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder. Afterwards FFF8A772 falls each pass by min(255, decay table(rpm/25) x FFF8A760), FFF8A760 = combustion events since the previous pass (0x0DC7E8 on the per-event counter FFF8A780, 0x0DFEF8), i.e. by the table value per combustion event. 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 (0.5-degree units) from the timing request FFF8A76A (read). Stock 1.0 degree per combustion event at all rpm (10 degrees gone in 10 events). Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (Below 200 km/h)
table.description:
How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used below 200 km/h between about 3900 and 6375 rpm. Stock retard is 10 degrees for the stronger tip-in classes. Stock 0.30 s, 0.50 s from 6000 rpm.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 below cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h). End of the tip-in retard window, in 10 ms passes since the tip-in code FFF8A619 appeared, by rpm FFF8CD5C (x25). 0x0DDD94 (called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args read: engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, pedal released FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, FFF888CF, FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C, outputs FFF8A772/A773/A771). On the pass where FFF8A619 becomes non-zero the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (05BB68 / 05BB74) are looked up by rpm/25; the second table of each pair is used when speed >= cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h). FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes since the code appeared < end, with engine state 3, pedal not fully released, rpm FFF8CE9C within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA (20..255) and speed within cal 0x37EF5..0x37EFC; afterwards it decays by 05BB8C/05BB80(rpm/25) x FFF8A760 per pass. Amount = cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) by code 1-4 (stock 0 / 0 / 20 / 20) + 05BB44(FFF888CF) (stock 0) (read). 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 from the timing request FFF8A76A (0.5-degree units), which reaches the base timing sum through FFF8A76D (0x0DD760, 0x0DA600) (read). So stock gives 10 degrees of retard for codes 3 and 4 (read). FFF8A619 (0x0B86A0 via 0x0B8618, read) is a tip-in code: active while the pedal is off its released position and the throttle byte FFF8CD74>>2 has risen by >= cal 0x3497C (6 counts, about 3.4 %) over the last 40 ms (5-deep 10 ms history FFF8CD78..CD7C); 0x40 = from below 0594A8(rpm) to above 0594B4(rpm) with a rise >= cal 0x3497F (8); 0x30 / 0x20 = peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5); else 0x10 (read). It clears when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Unit: passes of the 10 ms module (read). Stock 30 passes (0.30 s), 50 (0.50 s) at 6000 rpm and above; start table 05BB50 is 0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard End (From 200 km/h)
table.description:
How long the tip-in timing retard lasts after a sudden throttle opening, in 10 ms steps by rpm; used from 200 to 250 km/h, between about 3900 and 6375 rpm. Stock retard is 10 degrees for the stronger tip-in classes. Stock 0.30 s, 0.50 s from 6000 rpm.
Details: When used: speed FFF99835 at or above cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h; up to cal 0x37EFC = 250 km/h). End of the tip-in retard window, in 10 ms passes since the tip-in code FFF8A619 appeared, by rpm FFF8CD5C (x25). 0x0DDD94 (called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args read: engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, pedal released FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, FFF888CF, FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C, outputs FFF8A772/A773/A771). On the pass where FFF8A619 becomes non-zero the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (05BB68 / 05BB74) are looked up by rpm/25; the second table of each pair is used when speed >= cal 0x37EF4 (200 km/h). FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes since the code appeared < end, with engine state 3, pedal not fully released, rpm FFF8CE9C within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA (20..255) and speed within cal 0x37EF5..0x37EFC; afterwards it decays by 05BB8C/05BB80(rpm/25) x FFF8A760 per pass. Amount = cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) by code 1-4 (stock 0 / 0 / 20 / 20) + 05BB44(FFF888CF) (stock 0) (read). 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 from the timing request FFF8A76A (0.5-degree units), which reaches the base timing sum through FFF8A76D (0x0DD760, 0x0DA600) (read). So stock gives 10 degrees of retard for codes 3 and 4 (read). FFF8A619 (0x0B86A0 via 0x0B8618, read) is a tip-in code: active while the pedal is off its released position and the throttle byte FFF8CD74>>2 has risen by >= cal 0x3497C (6 counts, about 3.4 %) over the last 40 ms (5-deep 10 ms history FFF8CD78..CD7C); 0x40 = from below 0594A8(rpm) to above 0594B4(rpm) with a rise >= cal 0x3497F (8); 0x30 / 0x20 = peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5); else 0x10 (read). It clears when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Unit: passes of the 10 ms module (read). Stock 30 passes (0.30 s), 50 (0.50 s) at 6000 rpm and above; start table 05BB5C is 0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder
table.description:
Extra tip-in timing retard added by intake air temperature (from what is probably the second intake air temperature sensor). Stock 0 at all temperatures, so stock tip-in retard comes only from the fixed per-class amounts (10 degrees for the stronger classes).
Details: When used: on every pass with a tip-in code, added to the code amount (0x0DDD94: FFF8A771 = this(FFF888CF), FFF8A7EC = code cal + this, capped at 255; argument s8 = FFF888CF passed in the delay slot at 0x0DDE3C, read). FFF888CF is the second intake air temperature (degC + 50 from Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, 0x06B304; sensor identity inferred). Tip-in timing retard 0x0DDD94 (10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; args engine state FFF8866C, speed FFF99835, FFF886AB bit 5, rpm/25 FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF8CD65, tip-in code FFF8A619, second intake temperature FFF888CF, events-per-pass FFF8A760, rpm FFF8CE9C; stack args checked at 0x0DDDA0..0x0DDDB2: s0 coolant, s4 code, s8 FFF888CF, s12 FFF8A760, s16 rpm, read). On the pass where the tip-in code FFF8A619 appears the window start (05BB50 / 05BB5C) and end (Tip-In Timing Retard End) are latched by rpm/25. FFF8A772 = amount while start <= passes < end, engine state 3, rpm within cal 0x37EF8..0x37EF6 (3900-6375 rpm), coolant FFF8CD65 within cal 0x37EFB..0x37EFA and speed below 200 km/h or 200-250 km/h; amount = code cal 0x37EFD..0x37F00 (below 200 km/h) or 0x37F01..0x37F04 (200-250 km/h) (stock 0/0/20/20 for codes 1-4) + Tip-In Timing Retard Temperature Adder. Afterwards FFF8A772 falls each pass by min(255, decay table(rpm/25) x FFF8A760), FFF8A760 = combustion events since the previous pass (0x0DC7E8 on the per-event counter FFF8A780, 0x0DFEF8), i.e. by the table value per combustion event. 0x0DD568 subtracts FFF8A772 (0.5-degree units) from the timing request FFF8A76A (read). Stock 0 at all temperatures, so stock retard comes only from the code cals (10 degrees for codes 3/4). Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum
table.description:
Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle before the stab must be below this. Together with Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum it defines a big low-to-high throttle jump. Stock 5.1 % at idle rising to 30 % from 5600 rpm.
Details: When used: during a tip-in event (0x0B86A0, read): class 4 needs the throttle before the event (held FFF8CD77) below this(rpm FFF8CE9C). Stock 5.1 % up to 800 rpm rising to 30 % from 5600 rpm. Tip-in classifier 0x0B86A0 (called by 0x0B8618, read): active while running (FFF8906B = 3), accelerator not released, throttle rising (CD7C < CD78) and FFF8CD77 - its value 40 ms earlier (CD7B) >= cal 0x3497C (6 = 3.4 %); it ends when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Class FFF8A619: 0x40 if the throttle before the event < Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum, the peak 40 ms rise >= cal 0x3497F (8) and the throttle now >= Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum; else 0x30 / 0x20 for a peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5) unless frozen (see Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle); else 0x10. 0x0DDD94 (read) turns class n into the retard FFF8A772 = cal 0x37EFC+n (or 0x37F00+n by speed) + 05BB44(FFF888CF), subtracted from FFF8A76A in 0x0DD568; stock classes 3/4 get 20 (10 deg), 1/2 get 0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum
table.description:
Tip-in classification by rpm: for the strongest tip-in class (4), the throttle after the stab must be at or above this. Stock 20.4 % at idle, 44-65 % at 1600-4000 rpm, 94 % from 4800 rpm.
Details: When used: during a tip-in event (0x0B86A0, read): class 4 needs the current throttle FFF8CD77 at or above this(rpm FFF8CE9C). Stock 20.4 % up to 800 rpm, 44-65 % in 1600-4000 rpm, 74 % at 4400 rpm, 94 % from 4800 rpm. Tip-in classifier 0x0B86A0 (called by 0x0B8618, read): active while running (FFF8906B = 3), accelerator not released, throttle rising (CD7C < CD78) and FFF8CD77 - its value 40 ms earlier (CD7B) >= cal 0x3497C (6 = 3.4 %); it ends when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Class FFF8A619: 0x40 if the throttle before the event < Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum, the peak 40 ms rise >= cal 0x3497F (8) and the throttle now >= Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum; else 0x30 / 0x20 for a peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5) unless frozen (see Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle); else 0x10. 0x0DDD94 (read) turns class n into the retard FFF8A772 = cal 0x37EFC+n (or 0x37F00+n by speed) + 05BB44(FFF888CF), subtracted from FFF8A76A in 0x0DD568; stock classes 3/4 get 20 (10 deg), 1/2 get 0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle
table.description:
Tip-in classification by rpm: once the pedal has been pressed for a short while and throttle is at or above this, the tip-in class is held rather than reassigned to classes 2/3 or dropped back to 1. Stock 13 % at 0 rpm rising to 38 % from 4000 rpm.
Details: When used: during a tip-in event (0x0B86A0, read): once the accelerator has been pressed for more than 10 passes and the current throttle FFF8CD77 is at or above this(rpm FFF8CE9C), classes 2/3 are no longer assigned and the class keeps its last value instead of falling back to 1. Stock 13 % at 0 rpm rising to 38 % from 4000 rpm. Tip-in classifier 0x0B86A0 (called by 0x0B8618, read): active while running (FFF8906B = 3), accelerator not released, throttle rising (CD7C < CD78) and FFF8CD77 - its value 40 ms earlier (CD7B) >= cal 0x3497C (6 = 3.4 %); it ends when the throttle closes by cal 0x34980 (4) or the pedal is released. Class FFF8A619: 0x40 if the throttle before the event < Tip-In Retard Class 4 Start Throttle Maximum, the peak 40 ms rise >= cal 0x3497F (8) and the throttle now >= Tip-In Retard Class 4 Throttle Minimum; else 0x30 / 0x20 for a peak rise >= cal 0x3497E (10) / 0x3497D (5) unless frozen (see Tip-In Retard Class Hold Throttle); else 0x10. 0x0DDD94 (read) turns class n into the retard FFF8A772 = cal 0x37EFC+n (or 0x37F00+n by speed) + 05BB44(FFF888CF), subtracted from FFF8A76A in 0x0DD568; stock classes 3/4 get 20 (10 deg), 1/2 get 0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Tip-Out Timing Retard
table.description:
Timing pulled, by gear and manifold pressure, when rpm rises shortly after lifting off the pedal on a warm engine above walking speed; probably damps driveline shunt or coasting downshift jolts. Latched on the event and removed at once afterwards. Stock 0 at low manifold pressure, up to 30 degrees at high pressure.
Details: When used: within cal 0x1B8F0 (100 passes of the 10 ms task = 1 s, inferred) after the accelerator is released, once the trigger FFF8A774 bit 5 sets. Bit 5 (0x0E0F3C) is set while: pedal released, rpm rate FFF8CEA6 >= cal 0x1B8E6 (26), rpm FFF8CE9C <= cal 0x1B8E8 (6600 rpm, hyst. cal 0x1B8EA), coolant FFF88A44 >= cal 0x1B8EC (158 F / 70 C), vehicle speed FFF88BE8 >= cal 0x1B8EE (178 = 10 km/h) and FFF8A8AE bit 7 and FFF88E62 bit 0 (not identified) (0x0E0F3C, read); bit 4 (0x0E0EA8, read) passes bit 5 on only within cal 0x1B8F0 passes of the pedal release and while rpm FFF8CE9C >= cal 0x1B8F2 (0, no floor in stock). 0x0DDB2C (read): on the rising edge of FFF8A774 bit 4 this table (gear FFF8A621 x manifold pressure FFF88A34) is latched into FFF8A76F and held while the bit stays set; when it clears the value decays by cal 0x1B8F4 (51200 = 200 half-degrees per pass, i.e. at once). FFF8A76F is subtracted from the final timing sum FFF8A744 (0x0D9E40, read). So a retard when the rpm rises right after a lift-off (driveline shunt / coasting downshift damping, inferred). Stock 0 at 4.4 psia (30 kPa), up to 30 degrees at high manifold pressure. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out
table.description:
Limits how fast the timing request may climb back to the closed-pedal target just after the pedal is released, by rpm. Lower values give a softer return. Stock 0.5 degree per step at low rpm, 5 degrees at 3000 rpm, unlimited from 3500 rpm.
Details: When used: 0x0E0A30 (read): while the accelerator is released (FFF8A774 bit 0), for the first part of the release (counter FFF8484C, incremented by FFF8A760 per pass, below cal 0x30FD0 = 3072) and while the closed-pedal target is more than cal 0x30FD2 - 32 (20 half-degrees) above the current request, the timing request FFF8B10E may rise by at most (this - 32) half-degrees per pass (rpm FFF8CDC2 axis); otherwise it follows the target at once. FFF8B10E feeds FFF8A789 (0x0E0910) and the spark target FFF8A72A. Stock 0.5 degree/pass at low rpm, 5 degrees at 3000 rpm, unlimited (65534) from 3500 rpm. Confidence: read.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard
table.description:
Short timing retard by coolant temperature, applied for a few combustion events when fuel comes back after decel fuel cut because rpm fell to the resume point with the pedal still closed; then ramped out. Softens the fuel-return bump. 128 = no change. Stock 0 when cold, up to -25 degrees from 50 C.
Details: When used: 0x0DAFD4 (called per combustion event from 0x0DF02C <- 0x07D0E0, the crank-synchronous task; args read: accelerator released FFF88C64 bit 5, FFF8A774 bit 3, MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, FFF88ADA bit 6, engine stopped FFF88A2D bit 0). Event (read): with the pedal released, the engine running and the rpm change per event FFF8CEA6 >= cal 0x2FF56 (s16 -154 = -30 rpm per event; signed CMP/GE at 0x0DB000), an event starts when FFF8A774 bit 3 is set and rpm FFF8CE9C/128 (rpm/25) is below FFF8A62E. After cal 0x2FF50 (1) event with no change, FFF8B0DA = this table(coolant FFF88A44) << 7 for cal 0x2FF4F (10) combustion events; afterwards B0DA ramps back toward 0x4000 (no change) by cal 0x2FF58 - 0x4000 = 179/16384 per event (0.7 degrees per event). Pressing the pedal or a fast rpm drop cancels it (B0DA = 0x4000) (read). 0x0DB374: FFF8A753 = min(B0DA, B0DC) >> 7, the more retarding of this term and the 0x0DB21C term (05B718/05B724), and A753 is added in the 128-offset half-degree frame to the final timing sum (0x0D9E40, read). Trigger meaning: FFF8A774 bit 3 is set by 0x0E1628 when the limit state FFF8A638 steps from 8 to 9 while cylinders were cut on the previous pass (FFF8A643 != 0), and cleared by FFF8A78E (read). 0x0BD684 enters state 8 while FFF8A63D bit 0 holds past the 059D44 hold count and goes to 9 when it drops (read). FFF8A63D bit 0 comes from bit 2, which 0x0C06F0 clears when the pedal is released and rpm/25 >= FFF8A62E (plus start-time and fault conditions) (read). So state 8 is the deceleration fuel cut and FFF8A62E its rpm threshold in 25 rpm units (inferred from the cut-cylinder count and the closed-pedal rpm test), and this table is a short retard when fuel returns because rpm fell to that threshold with the pedal still closed (read in Phase 19: limit state 8 is the staged decel fuel cut, A63D bit 0 held for 059D44 passes). 128 = no change, one count = 0.5 degree, negative = retard. Stock 0 up to 0 C (32 F), -8 at 10 C, -12 at 20 C, -16 at 30 C, -18 at 40 C, -25 degrees from 50 C (122 F). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Closed-Pedal Resume)
table.description:
How fast, in degrees per combustion event by rpm, the -5 degree decel-fuel-cut timing offset is removed after the cut ends with the pedal still released. Stock 5 degrees per event at all rpm, so the offset is gone on the first event.
Details: When used: state 2 after a cut that ended with the pedal still released or rpm/25 below the resume threshold FFF8A62E (latch FFF84762 = FFF8A78D, set on the falling edge of FFF8A64C bit 2 in that case, read). Decel fuel cut timing offset FFF8B0DC, 0x0DB21C (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8 <- 0x07D0E0; args A64C bit 2, FFF88C64 bit 5, read). State FFF8A76E (0x0DD7E8, 10 ms): 3 while cylinders are cut (FFF8A64C bit 2 = cut active in limit state 8, 0x0C5170), 4 once the cut has lasted cal 0x2FF48 (1 s) with coolant >= cal 0x2FF4A (70 C), load FFF8A616 < cal 0x2FF4E (77 %), rpm FFF8CD54 < cal 0x2FF4C (2500 rpm), combustion mode 4 and FFF8881E < cal 0x2FF46; after the cut 1 (hold) while those conditions last, at most cal 0x2FF44 (3 s), then 2. B0DC = 0x4000 (no change) in state 3, cal 0x2FF12 << 7 (118: -5 degrees) in state 4, held in state 1, and in state 2 it climbs back to 0x4000 by (table(rpm FFF8CD54) - 0x4000) per event. FFF8A753 = min(Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard term B0DA, B0DC) >> 7 is added to the final timing sum (0x0DB374, 0x0D9E40), 128 = no change (read). Stock 17664 = 5.0 degrees per event at all rpm, so the -5 degree offset is gone on the first event. Confidence: read.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Recovery Timing Ramp (Pedal Resume)
table.description:
How fast, in degrees per combustion event by rpm, the -5 degree decel-fuel-cut timing offset is removed after the cut ends because the pedal was pressed. Stock 5 degrees per event at all rpm, so it is gone at once.
Details: When used: state 2 after a cut that ended with the pedal pressed and rpm/25 at or above the resume threshold FFF8A62E (latch FFF84762 clear, read). Decel fuel cut timing offset FFF8B0DC, 0x0DB21C (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8 <- 0x07D0E0; args A64C bit 2, FFF88C64 bit 5, read). State FFF8A76E (0x0DD7E8, 10 ms): 3 while cylinders are cut (FFF8A64C bit 2 = cut active in limit state 8, 0x0C5170), 4 once the cut has lasted cal 0x2FF48 (1 s) with coolant >= cal 0x2FF4A (70 C), load FFF8A616 < cal 0x2FF4E (77 %), rpm FFF8CD54 < cal 0x2FF4C (2500 rpm), combustion mode 4 and FFF8881E < cal 0x2FF46; after the cut 1 (hold) while those conditions last, at most cal 0x2FF44 (3 s), then 2. B0DC = 0x4000 (no change) in state 3, cal 0x2FF12 << 7 (118: -5 degrees) in state 4, held in state 1, and in state 2 it climbs back to 0x4000 by (table(rpm FFF8CD54) - 0x4000) per event. FFF8A753 = min(Decel Fuel Cut Resume Timing Retard term B0DA, B0DC) >> 7 is added to the final timing sum (0x0DB374, 0x0D9E40), 128 = no change (read). Stock 17664 = 5.0 degrees per event at all rpm. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Hold (RPM)
table.description:
When the A/C compressor switches off near standstill, the ECU retards timing 5 degrees for this many combustion events (one per 180 degrees of crank rotation), by rpm, then ramps the retard out. Probably smooths the idle load change. Stock 12 events from 650 to 1200 rpm (about 0.45 s at 800 rpm), 0 at 1400 rpm.
Details: When used: 0x0D8E3C (called from 0x0DF02C, args read): on the falling edge of FFF8A9A2 bit 6 (A/C compressor engaged, inferred in my research notes) while FFF88A3C < cal 0x2FE88, vehicle speed FFF99835 < cal 0x2FE90 (4 km/h), rpm FFF8CE9C within cal 0x2FE8E..0x2FE8C (500 rpm..max) and coolant >= cal 0x2FE8A, a hold counter FFF8A75D is loaded from this table (by rpm FFF8CE9C) and counted down per pass. While it runs, FFF8B0CC = cal 0x2FE82 (2560 = 10 half-degrees = 5 degrees); afterwards B0CC decays by cal 0x2FE84 (51) per pass. B0CC >> 8 is subtracted from the final timing sum FFF8A744 (0x0D9E40, read). Off while FFF88A2D bit 0 (engine stopped) or FFF8A65F bit 7. The alternate per-step table 05B410 (by FFF8A8C7) replaces cal 0x2FE82 only with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set (0 in stock). Stock 12 passes from 650 to 1200 rpm, 0 at 1400 rpm. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1)
table.description:
Manual transmission, gear 1: timing correction (negative = retard) by the size of the throttle-flow change after a throttle step, scaled by the surge phase, coolant and mode factors. Appears to damp driveline surge (shuffle) by retarding while rpm swings up.

table.name: Surge Damping Timing Coolant Factor
table.description:
Scales the surge damping timing correction by coolant temperature on this manual-transmission car. Stock 0.30 at -10 C and below, full from 0 C.
Details: When used: MT coding (FFF88ADA bit 7 set, always in this ROM): 0x0DE0BC writes FFF8A75C = this(coolant FFF88A44) (read). Multiplier x/255 on the surge damping term; stock 0.30 up to -10 C (14 F), 1.0 from 0 C (32 F). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping (inferred from the structure; the stock odd-count-only factors fit it). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Surge Damping Throttle Flow Map
table.description:
Converts throttle opening and rpm into a flow fraction (probably how much the throttle limits airflow); how fast this value changes is what triggers and sizes the surge damping timing retard. Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers surge damping. Stock 0 at closed throttle, reaching full by 28-37 % throttle.
Details: When used: every 10 ms pass of 0x0DE0E0: 0x0DC838 looks this up by throttle opening FFF88A3A (rows) and rpm FFF8CE9C (columns) into FFF8B114, and FFF8B0EE = |B114 - B114 two passes ago| is the input of the Surge Damping Timing Curves and of the trigger (read). FFF8B114 has no other reader (read). Stock 0 at closed throttle, rising steeply and reaching 32768 by 28-37 % throttle depending on rpm (800-5000 rpm columns): a throttle-limited flow fraction (inferred). Changing it changes how strongly a throttle step triggers the surge damping retard. Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping (inferred from the structure; the stock odd-count-only factors fit it). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic) (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Alternate A/C-switch timing retard amount, by an unidentified input. It has no effect on a stock car: it is only read when a calibration switch is set, which is off in stock (stock uses a fixed 5 degree retard instead). Stock 0, 5 and 10 degrees across the axis.
Details: When used: never in stock. 0x0D8E3C (called from 0x0DF02C; args read: FFF88A2D bit 0, cal 0x1D0AE bit 0, FFF8A9A3 bit 0, FFF8A9A2 bit 6, FFF8A65F bit 7) loads FFF8B0CC with this table (by FFF8A8C7) instead of cal 0x2FE82 (2560 = 5 degrees) only when its second argument, the calibration bit 0x1D0AE bit 0, is set; it is 0 in stock, so the table is never read (read). With that bit set the trigger also changes from the A/C engagement edge (FFF8A9A2 bit 6) to FFF8A9A3 bit 0. B0CC >> 8 is subtracted from the final timing sum (0x0D9E40) while the A/C Cut Timing Retard Hold counter runs, then decays (read). Axis FFF8A8C7 is not identified: 0x116034 writes it as a latched copy of FFF8A8C6 (latch conditions involve FFF88B8B bit 0 and FFF8A9A3 bit 1; not worked out in detail), and FFF8A8C6 comes from 0x115F80, which takes it from FFF88B91 (a received input byte, meaning not identified); FFF8A8C6 is read by several other functions together with the same cal bit 0x1D0AE bit 0 (read). Stock 0, 5, 10 degrees at axis 0 / 8 / 15 and above. Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Reduction Spark Retard
table.description:
Turns a torque or efficiency shortfall back into spark retard on base timing. Besides torque reduction, it is how the ECU pulls fired timing down to Primary Ignition (or the closed-pedal target) plus knock correction advance where that is below Base Timing, so it must stay the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard; don't edit one without the other. Not used in the rev/overboost-cut states.
Details: When used: on the FFF8A76A spark path (normal fuel mode; the catalyst-heating paths FFF8A76B / FFF8A76C use the sibling Catalyst Heating Spark Retard tables, inferred), except in limit states 0x0B / 0x0C / 0x19 / 0x1A with their Limit-State Spark bits set (stock) and in state 0x1B. 0x0DD568 (read): spark angle FFF8A76A = base timing FFF8A645 - this(max(FFF8A64B, cal 0x2FDE4 = 102) x 128) + per-cylinder trim - tip-in retard FFF8A772, capped at cal 0x1B83C (120); FFF8A76A then rate-limits into the fired timing (0x0DD760 -> 0x0DA600 -> FFF8A744). FFF8A64B (0x0C39DC) is the torque cap over the air torque times the request efficiency, the share of torque the spark must still deliver (inferred), so this is the torque-reduction (and efficiency) retard. Same form as Catalyst Heating Spark Retard (0x0DD4EC). Stock 0 at 100 %, 4 degrees per 1/16 step down to 60 degrees at 12.6 %; the floor 102 limits it to about 34 degrees (inferred). Not used by the rev limiter. The floor applies only on the normal path: when FFF8866C = 3 and either FFF8A649 != -128 or (param 5 = FFF88C64 bit 5 set and the state is not 2), outside state 0x18 with A649 = -128, the input is FFF8AF22 >> 7 instead (no floor, read). FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4, read) = Ignition Efficiency vs Retard(max(0, FFF8A645 - (FFF8A789 - 32 [+ 0.3516 deg x (KCA FFF8A791 + FLKC FFF8A7A7) in combustion modes 3/4]))), the efficiency of the timing request relative to base timing, and 0x0C39DC builds FFF8A64B = min(255, torque-cap ratio x AF22 / 128). This table is the exact inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard (axis and data mirrored), so on both paths FFF8A76A = min(base timing, timing request + KCA + FLKC) less the torque-cap retard: this is the mechanism by which Primary Ignition (or Closed-Pedal Timing Target) and the knock correction advance limit the fired timing (read; min() form computed). Keep it the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard. Because FFF8A64B is capped at 255, the pedal-pressed path always takes at least 1 count (0.5 degree) from this table even at full torque (255 x 128 = 32640 -> 1 by the truncating lookup 0x1AB8BC; computed), and the input is always capped at 256 = 100 % (read). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections), and in stock the target is far lower, so raising this map at idle or when coasting does nothing.
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0, see Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)), TGVs not forced closed. From 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 clear (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. In stock the request at idle (about 6-8 degrees at 500-900 rpm, warm) is far below this map (19-28 degrees at 400-1000 rpm, 0.13-0.39 g/rev (10-30 % load)), and it stays below it when coasting (17 vs 34 degrees at 2000 rpm), so idle and coast timing are set by Closed-Pedal Timing Target and raising this map there has no effect (computed from stock data); lowering it below the target does take effect. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-closed side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm.
Details: 0x0D9E40 (read): final timing FFF8A744 = min(max(timing sum, floor), cap). The cap is this table x (1 - TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8) + Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open) x FFF8B3E8 (rpm FFF8CE9C x load FFF8A616), used only while the accelerator is fully released (FFF886AB bit 5), the latch FFF8A774 bit 6 is set (set by FFF8A7E0 bit 4, cleared while the engine is stopped, 0x0E1258, read) and vehicle speed FFF88BE8 <= cal 0x32DF2 (17778 = 1000 km/h, i.e. always); otherwise the cap is cal 0x2FC66 (120 = 60 degrees, no cap). So it is a closed-pedal (deceleration / idle) cap; it never limits timing with the pedal pressed. The rpm axis ends at 4,000 rpm. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description:
Maximum timing allowed with the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration), by rpm and load, TGV-open side; blended with Ignition Timing Cap (Pedal Released, TGV Closed) by how far the TGVs are open. Never limits timing with the pedal pressed.
Details: TGV-open partner of Ignition Timing Cap (TGV Closed), blended by the TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 (0x0D9E40, read). Same activation condition. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Target
table.description:
Ignition timing target by rpm with the pedal released (idle and coasting) on this manual car; coolant, intake-air and post-start corrections are added. The ECU fires the lower of this and the Pedal Released Base Timing map, and in stock this target is the lower one, so it sets idle and coast timing; it is also fired directly during a scan-tool timing check. Stock 6 degrees at 500-700 rpm rising to 17 degrees from 2000 rpm.
Details: When used: on the manual-transmission coding (FFF886AB bit 7 forces FFF8CE63 = 0, 0x06B68C, so the debounced state FFF8A7D9 is 0; read). 0x0D948C: FFF8A72F = this(FFF8CD5C = rpm/25) (the rpm x load table 05B48C replaces it only below cal 0x23834 = 0 rpm, i.e. never). FFF8A72F is the base of the pedal-released timing target in 0x0E0A30 (FFF8A72F + A788 + A782 + A755, blended with the pedal-pressed request by FFF8A72E; its rise after tip-out is limited by Timing Request Recovery Rate After Tip-Out) (read). That request FFF8A789 reaches the fired timing in normal running, not only in the scan-tool mode: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 = Ignition Efficiency vs Retard(max(0, FFF8A645 - (FFF8A789 - 32 + KCA + FLKC))) (0x0C13B4); the two tables are inverses, so the fired base is min(Base Timing (Pedal Released) + comps, this target + comps + KCA + FLKC), followed by 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and the fired sum 0x0D9E40 (read; min() form computed). In stock the target (6-9 degrees at 500-1000 rpm) is far below Base Timing (Pedal Released) (19-28 degrees), and 17 vs 34 degrees at 2000 rpm, so this table sets idle and coast timing (KCA Max is 0 at idle loads; computed from stock data). In addition, in 0x0D9E40 the final timing FFF8A744 is set to FFF8A72F - 32 directly while FFF99845 bit 5 (a scan-tool control, cleared by 0x1CE6DE when the pedal is pressed, FFF8A787 > 0 or rpm > 2000) is set (read). The (x - 32)/2 frame follows from that use. Stock 6 degrees at 500-700 rpm rising to 17 degrees at 2000 rpm and above. Confidence: read.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation
table.description:
Timing added with the pedal released on a cold engine, by coolant temperature, scaled by Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier. Adds to the pedal-released base timing and the closed-pedal target. Stock 13 degrees at -10 C and below, 7 at 20-60 C, 0 from 80 C.
Details: When used: 0x0E07F4 (read): while the accelerator is released (FFF8A774 bit 0) FFF8A788 = this(coolant FFF88A44) x Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier(FFF8CD62 = rpm/12.5) / 128 + 05BD4C(coolant; 0 in stock, only above load cal 0x239A8), 0 when FFF8866C = 1. FFF8A788 is added to the pedal-released base timing (0x0C2C08, E/F path) and to the closed-pedal timing target in 0x0E0A30 (A72F + A788 + A782 + A755) (read). Stock 13 degrees up to -10 C, 10 at 0-10 C, 7 at 20-60 C, 4 at 70 C, 0 from 80 C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
table.description:
Scales Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation by rpm (1.0 = full amount). Stock 0.5 up to 700 rpm, 0.29 at 800-900 rpm, almost full from 1000 rpm.
Details: When used: 0x0E07F4 (read): while the accelerator is released (FFF8A774 bit 0) FFF8A788 = this(coolant FFF88A44) x Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier(FFF8CD62 = rpm/12.5) / 128 + 05BD4C(coolant; 0 in stock, only above load cal 0x239A8), 0 when FFF8866C = 1. FFF8A788 is added to the pedal-released base timing (0x0C2C08, E/F path) and to the closed-pedal timing target in 0x0E0A30 (A72F + A788 + A782 + A755) (read). FFF8CD62 = sat8(FFF8CD54 >> 6) = rpm/12.5 (0x06B3B8, read). Stock 0.5 up to 700 rpm, 0.29 at 800-900 rpm, 0.99 from 1000 rpm. Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
table.description:
Extra closed-pedal timing for the first moments after a start (stationary, pedal released, low rpm), by the coolant temperature at start, then ramped out. It raises the closed-pedal timing target, which sets the fired idle timing in stock, so it does advance the spark (up to the Pedal Released Base Timing map). Not applied below about -3 C start coolant; stock 8 degrees at 0 C rising to 15 degrees at 60 C, 0 from 80 C.
Details: When used: 0x0DB71C (read): while the car is stationary (FFF88BE8 <= 18), within cal 0x31468 (30 counts of FFF88A76 = 0.3 s since start; 10 ms per count, p16) and at or below cal 0x31466 (1000 rpm), FFF8A756 = this(coolant at start FFF88A46) x 05B76C(baro; 255 in stock)/256; afterwards it decays by cal 0x31464 (-12.8 half-degrees per pass; 0x0DB71C runs from 0x0DF0B8 in the crank-synchronous task, so one pass = one combustion event, inferred from the call chain), limited to cal 0x31462..0x31463 (0..30). 0 when the start coolant is below cal 0x3146A (-3 C). Start type FFF8A6E7 = 3 uses 05B760 (all 0). FFF8A755 = FFF8A756 is added to the pedal-released timing target in 0x0E0A30 (read). That target is the request side of the closed-pedal timing limit, so this advance reaches the fired timing whenever the target is below Base Timing (Pedal Released), as it is at idle in stock: fired base = min(Base Timing (Pedal Released) + comps, Closed-Pedal Timing Target + comps + this + KCA + FLKC) via 0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0DD568 (read; min() form computed). It is not part of the scan-tool fixed timing in 0x0D9E40 (FFF8A72F - 32 only). Stock 8 degrees at 0 C rising to 15 degrees at 60 C start, 0 from 80 C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Boost
table.description:
Boost target in absolute pressure, by rpm and the ECU's target torque (the driver's request after the torque limits). Corrected for barometric pressure and intake temperature, then the wastegate control chases it. Raise with Boost Limit. Stock peaks at 211 kPa absolute (about 16 psi gauge) near 5,200 rpm.
Details: Target Torque axis (FFF8AECA): the torque the ECU is aiming for, i.e. the driver's request from the Requested Torque tables (pedal x rpm, set chosen by drive mode) after the Maximum Torque (IAT) and (DAM) limits, the external (CAN) torque limit and the gear/rpm rate shaping (torque module 0x0BE694, read). It is a request, not a measured torque; 16000 = 0 ft-lb. 0x108678 -> FFF8B3AC, the boost target before compensation: rpm (FFF8CD54) x target torque FFF8AECA (Nm). Target pressure = this, scaled about absolute zero by the baro and IAT compensations. Stock peaks at 211 kPa abs (about 16 psi gauge) near 5,200 rpm; the 0 ft-lb column sits below atmospheric. cal 0x290A8 = 1 would replace it with cal 0x290A6 (0 in stock). Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Units: see the scaling note (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Initial
table.description:
Base (feed-forward) wastegate duty by rpm and target torque, before boost feedback is added. Higher duty = more boost. It is scaled by the wastegate duty baro and IAT compensations and the total is capped by Wastegate Duty Maximum. Faults force 0 % duty.
Details: Target Torque axis (FFF8AECA): the torque the ECU is aiming for, i.e. the driver's request from the Requested Torque tables (pedal x rpm, set chosen by drive mode) after the Maximum Torque (IAT) and (DAM) limits, the external (CAN) torque limit and the gear/rpm rate shaping (torque module 0x0BE694, read). It is a request, not a measured torque; 16000 = 0 ft-lb. 0x107D3C -> FFF8B38C: base duty on rpm x target torque FFF8AECA (Nm). Output FFF8B3A8 = min(this x FFF8B3B6/32768 + P + I, Maximum x FFF8B3B6/32768) (0x108098, read), where FFF8B3B6 = Wastegate Duty Baro Compensation x Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Higher duty = more boost: faults force 0 % (0x1088B4, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Maximum
table.description:
Ceiling on wastegate duty (Initial plus feedback) by rpm and target torque, scaled by the same baro and IAT compensations. Also stops the boost integral from growing once duty reaches it. Raise it if feedback runs out of authority.
Details: Target Torque axis (FFF8AECA): the torque the ECU is aiming for, i.e. the driver's request from the Requested Torque tables (pedal x rpm, set chosen by drive mode) after the Maximum Torque (IAT) and (DAM) limits, the external (CAN) torque limit and the gear/rpm rate shaping (torque module 0x0BE694, read). It is a request, not a measured torque; 16000 = 0 ft-lb. 0x107F24 -> FFF8B39E raw, FFF8B39C = this x FFF8B3B6/32768: the cap on Initial + feedback (0x108098) and the limit that stops the positive integral (0x1080E4) (read). Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Boost Baro Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Target Boost (and Boost Limit) by rpm and barometric pressure (1.0 = no change). Stock pulls the target down to 0.6 at altitude between 4,000 and 6,000 rpm.
Details: 0x10865C -> FFF8A84C: rpm x barometric pressure FFF88668 (kPa x 256 absolute), 128 = x1.0. Multiplies the absolute target together with the IAT compensation (0x108778: B3B2 = 2 x A84C x IAT comp x A84B, 32768 = x1). Stock pulls the target down to 0.6 at altitude between 4,000 and 6,000 rpm. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Wastegate Duty Baro Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Wastegate Duty Initial and Maximum by rpm and barometric pressure (1.0 = no change). Edit together with Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation, which it is combined with.
Details: 0x108890 -> FFF8B3B4 = this << 8: rpm x barometric pressure FFF88668, 128 = x1.0. With Wastegate Duty IAT Compensation it forms FFF8B3B6, which multiplies Wastegate Duty Initial and Maximum (0x108098, 0x107F24). Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Boost Proportional
table.description:
Proportional wastegate duty added by boost error (target minus actual; positive = under target), scaled by Boost Proportional IAT Gain. Larger values react harder to error. Zero while boost feedback is inactive.
Details: 0x1080E4: P term FFF8B3A4 = this(boost error) x Boost Proportional IAT Gain / 128; boost error = target FFF8B3B0 - measured FFF89264 (positive = under target). Zero while feedback is inactive. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Boost Integral Step (Positive Error)
table.description:
How fast the boost integral adds duty when boost is under target, by boost error; added every 20 ms, scaled by Boost Integral Positive IAT Gain. Only grows above Boost Integral Positive Error Deadband and while duty is below Wastegate Duty Maximum; capped by Boost Integral Maximum.
Details: 0x1080E4: while the error is >= Boost Integral Positive Error Deadband and the output duty FFF8B3B8 is below the maximum FFF8B39C, the integral FFF85370 grows each pass by this(error) x Boost Integral Positive IAT Gain / 128, capped at Boost Integral Maximum. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). p16 (read): 0x1080E4 runs in the 20 ms OS task (0x107654 <- 0x1E0AE8): the step is added once per 20 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: Boost Integral Step (Negative Error)
table.description:
How fast the boost integral removes duty when boost is over target, by boost error; applied every 20 ms while duty is at least 5 %, scaled by Boost Integral Negative IAT Gain. Floored at Boost Integral Minimum.
Details: 0x1080E4: while the error is below cal 0x28FCC (0) and the output duty is at least cal 0x28FD0 (5 %), the integral FFF85370 changes each pass by this(error) x Boost Integral Negative IAT Gain / 128 (negative), floored at Boost Integral Minimum. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). p16 (read): 0x1080E4 runs in the 20 ms OS task (0x107654 <- 0x1E0AE8): the step is added once per 20 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: Boost Integral Positive Error Deadband
table.description:
The boost integral only adds duty while boost is under target by at least this much, to avoid creeping on tiny errors. Stock about 0.66 kPa (0.1 psi).
Details: 0x1080E4: the integral only grows while the boost error is at least this (read). Stock 170 = 0.66 kPa (0.1 psi). Confidence: read.

table.name: Boost Feedback Activation Threshold
table.description:
Boost feedback (proportional and integral) only runs while the boost target is above atmospheric by more than this, by rpm; otherwise feedback is zero and the integral is reset. Stock -6.6 kPa below 2,800 rpm (feedback runs from slightly below atmospheric, but not at light load where the target is far below it), about 28 kPa (4.1 psi) above.
Details: 0x1080E4: feedback (P and I) runs only while target minus barometric pressure (FFF8B3AE, gauge) is above this(rpm) (hysteresis cal 0x29828, 6.7 kPa) and rpm is above Boost Feedback Minimum RPM, and the boost state FFF8A842 is 0 or 2; otherwise P = 0 and the integral is reset to 0. Stock: -6.6 kPa below 2,800 rpm, +28 kPa (4.1 psi) above. Chain (0x107654, read): Target Boost(rpm, target torque FFF8AECA) -> FFF8B3AC; FFF8B3B0 = (B3AC + 3404.8) x f - 3404 with f = Baro Comp x IAT Comp x A84B (128 = x1 each); error = B3B0 - measured FFF89264; PI terms from the step tables; duty = min(Initial x Duty Comp + P + I, Maximum x Duty Comp), then the state/fault overrides in 0x107D1C/0x1088B4 and the PWM output FFF8B3B8 (0x1E417C, channel E11). Confidence: read.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, Monitor)
table.description:
Safety-monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default), probably read by the electronic throttle torque monitor. Keep it identical to the main table: change both together or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault.
Details: When used: Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default); keep identical. Byte-for-byte copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) (data and axes) in separate storage, read by a second module (0x1873C4/0x1874BC/0x1875BC/0x1876BC, rpm x FFF88FE2, same A-then-B lookup order and weight structure, into FFF8BBAE/BBB2/BBB6/BBBA). Almost certainly the electronic-throttle torque monitor: change it together with the primary map or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault (inferred). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Accelerator Pedal Scaling
table.description:
Shapes the accelerator pedal position before it goes into the Requested Torque maps (role inferred). Stock is 1:1 apart from a small dead band near closed. Editing this also changes the second pedal channel, which reads the same data.
Details: Shapes the pedal position FFF88C54 (0x09E800, read) into FFF88A5E, the pedal input of the requested-torque maps (role inferred). Stock is 1:1 except a small dead band near closed. Table 065C8C reads the same data (with its own, identical axis) for the second pedal channel FFF88C52, so editing this edits both. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Accelerator Pedal Span
table.description:
Pedal sensor voltage travel that counts as 100 % pedal. Normally leave alone; change only for a different pedal sensor.
Details: Pedal voltage travel that equals 100 % (0x09EE9E, read); cal 0x573BC is used instead under flag FFF88B7B bit 2 (same value in stock). Volts assume the 65536 = 5 V sensor scale. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description:
Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother. Stock 0.2-0.5 ft-lb (0.25-0.65 Nm) per step.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4, FFF88ADA bit 7 set (always in stock) or FFF8AE0A below cal 0x1FC96. Step1, by gear x rpm, before the gear and pedal factors. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. A second shaping path (Path B) exists but is off in stock (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Stock 0.2-0.5 ft-lb (0.25-0.65 Nm) per pass. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F6B0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal)
table.description:
Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: the smoothing only acts when the request is below it. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm), 111-148 ft-lb (150-200 Nm) in gears 2-4 above 2000 rpm.
Details: When used: when the torque request drops (tip-out). Ceiling (Normal set). table.name: Target Torque Rise Path B Coolant Rise (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Part of the condition that lets Path B tip-in smoothing act, based on how much the coolant has warmed since start. Has no effect on a stock car because Path B is switched off (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). Stock 0.
Details: When used: only matters with Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B set (clear in stock). Gate of Path B (0x0BBA32..0x0BBA90, read): the warm condition is FFF80B96 >= cal 0x22A0C (16384 = 0 degC) and coolant at start FFF89224 >= cal 0x22A0A (50 = 0 degC, degC + 50 unit); while it holds, Path B stays available if clamp(FFF80B96 - FFF89224) < this(FFF89224). FFF80B96 is a copy of coolant FFF88A44 taken by 0x082F7E / 0x082FB0 under start/state conditions (read); which moment it captures is not identified. Data = coolant difference in the 409.6-per-degC unit offset by 0x4000 (40 degC) (read). Stock 16384 = 0 everywhere (a temperature difference: 0 degC = 0 degF; no +32 offset applies to a difference). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set (clear in stock, byte 0x01), FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04 (0 in stock, so never while running; hysteresis 0x22A06), and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <= ...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >= ...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) (1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B, Off in Stock)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = FFF8AEC6: if prev + Step2B >= Path B Stage 2 Torque the shaped value becomes prev + Step2B; then, if prev + Step1B < Path B Stage 2 Torque, it becomes max(Path B Start Torque, prev + Step1B); otherwise the main path's value stands. Whenever the cal bit is set, a request below Path B Start Torque also passes unshaped. Tables are selected by drive mode FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4, other = 1) and, for the step tables, by AT/CVT Coding as in the main path. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes and is passed the same cal bit, so it stays consistent. Stock: every Path B step and torque table is 16000 (0 ft-lb, 0 ft-lb per 10 ms); set them all before enabling the bit. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05FA54), so it stays consistent. Confidence: inferred.

AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Path B, Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp, AT/CVT Coding, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Path B tip-in smoothing for drive mode 4 with AT/CVT coding: allowed torque rise per 10 ms in Path B's fast stage. Has no effect on a stock car: Path B is switched off (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B clear, rpm limit 0). Stock 0; fill the whole Path B set before enabling it.
Details: When used: never in stock (Path B off). Drive mode 4 with AT/CVT Coding. Step2B of Path B, by gear x rpm (0-4000 rpm), before the Path B gear and pedal factors; looked up into FFF84100..FFF8410E (0x0BBE42..0x0BBF6E). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Path B (read, 0x0BB958 0x0BCEFE..0x0BCF96): a second rise-shaping path evaluated after the main one. It acts only while Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B (cal 0x23704 bit 6) is set (clear in stock, byte 0x01), FFF88BAA >= cal 0x22A08 (80; hysteresis 0x22A09), rpm FFF8CD54 <= cal 0x22A04 (0 in stock, so never while running; hysteresis 0x22A06), and the Path B gate is open. The gate is open unless all three hold: FFF8AE64 <= Target Torque Rise Path B Pedal-Released Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), FFF8AF1C <= ...Path B Low-Speed Time(FFF88BAA), and (the warm condition is false or FFF80B96 - coolant at start FFF89224 >= ...Path B Coolant Rise(FFF89224)). Step1B = (Path B Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear cal 0x229F0 + 2(g-1) (1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier (Path B, Off in Stock)(FFF8AF00) / 65025; Step2B the same with cal 0x229FA.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Path B Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; gear cals apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set. With prev = FFF8AEC6: if prev + Step2B >= Path B Stage 2 Torque the shaped value becomes prev + Step2B; then, if prev + Step1B < Path B Stage 2 Torque, it becomes max(Path B Start Torque, prev + Step1B); otherwise the main path's value stands. Whenever the cal bit is set, a request below Path B Start Torque also passes unshaped. Tables are selected by drive mode FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4, other = 1) and, for the step tables, by AT/CVT Coding as in the main path. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes and is passed the same cal bit, so it stays consistent. Stock: every Path B step and torque table is 16000 (0 ft-lb, 0 ft-lb per 10 ms); set them all before enabling the bit. AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.description:
Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target. Stock 258 ft-lb (350 Nm) warm from about 2000 rpm; less at low rpm, with very cold intake air below about 3000 rpm, and above about 6000 rpm with intake air at or below 32 F (148-170 ft-lb, 200-230 Nm, back to full by 50 F).
Details: 0x0BD078 -> FFF8AEC8: the limited target FFF8AEC2 = min(FFF8AEA6, this(rpm FFF8CD54, IAT FFF88A48), Maximum Torque (DAM), FFF8AF0C, FFF8AE5A) (read). Stock 258 ft-lb (350 Nm) warm; reduced with very cold intake air and below about 2,800 rpm. Target-torque chain (0x0BE694, read): Requested Torque sets -> drive-mode select (0x0BDBD8) -> FFF8AEFC -> + additive torque (0x0BB53C) -> external/fault limit (0x0BB1AC) -> FFF8AEA6 -> min with Maximum Torque (IAT), Maximum Torque (DAM) and two other limits (0x0BD078) -> FFF8AEC2 -> gear-dependent rate shaping (0x0BB958) -> FFF8AEBE -> max with a floor (0x0BD3F0) -> FFF8AEC6 -> max with idle/cruise floors (0x0BB4A8) -> FFF8AEAA -> + 059D18 offset (0x0BD404) -> FFF8AECA, the target-torque axis of Target Boost and the wastegate duty tables. Confidence: read.

table.name: Maximum Torque (DAM)
table.description:
Maximum target torque by DAM (knock learning) and rpm, in the same lowest-wins limit as Maximum Torque (IAT). Losing DAM lowers the torque target and so the boost target. Stock 258 ft-lb (350 Nm) to about 4000 rpm, tapering to 181 ft-lb (246 Nm) (full DAM) or 148 ft-lb (200 Nm) (DAM 0) above 6000 rpm.
Details: 0x0BD078 -> FFF8AEDE: second limit in the same min() (read). Row input FFF8A637 = FFF811AE copied by 0x0BD67C, the DAM-like knock value (x16); columns rpm. Stock 258 ft-lb (350 Nm) to about 4,000 rpm, tapering to 181 ft-lb (246 Nm) at full DAM and 148 ft-lb (200 Nm) at DAM 0 above 6,000 rpm: lost DAM lowers the torque target and so the boost target. Target-torque chain (0x0BE694, read): Requested Torque sets -> drive-mode select (0x0BDBD8) -> FFF8AEFC -> + additive torque (0x0BB53C) -> external/fault limit (0x0BB1AC) -> FFF8AEA6 -> min with Maximum Torque (IAT), Maximum Torque (DAM) and two other limits (0x0BD078) -> FFF8AEC2 -> gear-dependent rate shaping (0x0BB958) -> FFF8AEBE -> max with a floor (0x0BD3F0) -> FFF8AEC6 -> max with idle/cruise floors (0x0BB4A8) -> FFF8AEAA -> + 059D18 offset (0x0BD404) -> FFF8AECA, the target-torque axis of Target Boost and the wastegate duty tables. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base)
table.description:
Throttle-side torque cap by rpm used only during the rev or overboost cut when neither stage applies. It does not limit torque in normal driving, so raising it gives no extra power. Stock about 165 ft-lb (224 Nm) near the limiter, 108-207 ft-lb (146-280 Nm) lower down.
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0B while neither stage cap is on: in stock after a rev cut between Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and Rev Limit Reset RPM, and during an overboost cut below 256 kPa abs. Throttle-side torque cap by rpm FFF8CD54 (part 5); it is not a general torque limit: outside state 0x0B the request passes uncapped (0x0BDA84, read), so raising it gives no extra torque in normal driving (the normal-driving caps are Maximum Torque (IAT) / (DAM)). It limits the throttle only, not fuel or spark. Stock 108 ft-lb (146 Nm) at 1,200 rpm, 207 ft-lb (280 Nm) at 2,000 rpm, about 192 ft-lb (260 Nm) at 2,800-3,600 rpm, 184 ft-lb (250 Nm) at 4,400-6,000 rpm and 165 ft-lb (224 Nm) from 6,800 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: read.

Second throttle-side cap of the rev/overboost cut. Its thresholds equal stage 1's, so it is never used in stock (no effect in stock). Stock 52 ft-lb (70 Nm) flat.

The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Confidence: read.
