table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
table.description:
Base exhaust temperature by rpm and load for the A/F sensor's exhaust model, which probably decides when it is safe to heat the front A/F sensor fully (water condensation check). Does not affect fuel or timing. Stock about 400-520 C at idle to about 1000 C at 6800 rpm.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): base exhaust temperature from rpm FFF8CD54 and load FFF8BAC4 (= FFF8ADE4, or cal 0x42E7E under FFF88E2A bit 1). Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Stock 397-522 degC at 600 rpm, ~780 degC at 2400 rpm mid load, 975-1038 degC at 6800 rpm. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
table.description:
Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for ignition timing (later timing = hotter exhaust). Does not affect fuel or timing. Stock 1.21 at -20 degrees to 1.0 from 15 degrees.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): multiplies the base exhaust temperature by this(final timing FFF8A744)/128. Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Stock 1.21 at -20 deg falling to 1.0 from 15 deg BTDC (later timing, hotter exhaust). Both factors multiply the absolute temperature (base table + 223.15 K, i.e. Kelvin), not the degC/degF value shown: x1.10 on 800 C (1073 K) gives 907 C. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor
table.description:
Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for knock-related retard. Does not affect fuel or timing. Stock 1.0 at no retard to 1.10 at 30 degrees retard.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read, input checked in the assembly): multiplies the base by (this + 128)/256, input = FFF8A735 + FFF8A7A5 x 180/256 - 32 - FFF8A744 clamped to s8, i.e. base timing plus the maximum knock advance minus final timing (retard below the knock-free maximum, inferred), in half degrees. Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Stock 1.0 at 0 deg rising to 1.10 at 30 deg retard. Both factors multiply the absolute temperature (base table + 223.15 K, i.e. Kelvin), not the degC/degF value shown: x1.10 on 800 C (1073 K) gives 907 C. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
table.description:
How quickly the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model follows its target, by coolant. Does not affect fuel or timing. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): FFF8BAC8 = (previous x 32768 + target x k/2)/(32768 + k/2) with k = this(coolant FFF8CD65); target = the modelled exhaust temperature while running (engine state 3), else coolant temperature. Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Stock 0.011 per pass at -40/-20 degC and from 60 degC, 0.016 at 0 and 40 degC, 0.026 at 20 degC. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
table.description:
Modelled water in the exhaust at start, by coolant and intake temperature. If it is above the threshold, full A/F sensor heating waits until the model has dried out. Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier.
Details: When used: at ignition on, at the cranking -> running change of FFF8906B, on rising FFF89053 bit 4 and while FFF89053 bit 3 is set (0x1801A4, read). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water (stock 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.2 kPa at 30 C, 94 kPa at 98 C, in kPa x 8192 - read values); 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x1801A4 (read, args checked in the assembly): FFF8C478 = this(coolant FFF8AC8D, IAT FFF8AC8B; both degC + 50 bytes, cal 0x4234E / 0x42344 = -40 C on sensor fault) + FFF81880 (amount carried over from the last run). Above 415645 the A/F sensor heating waits for the model to dry out; below it the sensor takes the fast path (state 5). Stock 808794 at -30/-30 C, 415645 at 0/0 C (exactly the threshold), 0 from coolant 100 C or IAT 100 C. Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
table.description:
Scales how fast water is modelled to condense in the exhaust, by exhaust flow (probably 1.0 = normal); more condensation keeps the front A/F sensor in its protected heating state longer. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: always (module 0x180C20). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water (stock 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.2 kPa at 30 C, 94 kPa at 98 C, in kPa x 8192 - read values); 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x180BE4 / 0x17F4B8 (read): the condensation rate FFF8C448 is proportional to this(exhaust flow FFF8C4B4) x FFF8C4B4 x cal 0x42DA8 x (water partial pressure - saturation pressure at pipe temperature) / total pressure, so this scales condensation linearly (256 = 1.0 assumed; inferred). Stock 0.80 from 0 to 20 g/s, rising to 1.21 at 61 g/s, 0.96 from 113 g/s. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
table.description:
Water vapour pressure versus exhaust pipe temperature for the A/F sensor condensation model, which decides how long the front A/F sensor is kept in protected heating. Stock is the real physical curve; leave alone.
Details: When used: always (exhaust condensation model 0x180C20 behind the A/F sensor heater release, read). 0x17F4B8 (read; axis = pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, LF75404S_table_inputs): saturation = this(pipe temperature); total pressure = max(MAP, baro) in kPa x 8192; water partial pressure = total x cal 0x42333/256 (15 %); the condensation rate FFF8C448 = flow FFF8C4B4 x Condensation Flow Factor x cal 0x42DA8 x (partial - saturation) / total, clamped >= 0, and is integrated (minus evaporation) into the condensate amount that holds the A/F sensor in its protected heating state (see A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start). Stock is the physical saturation vapour pressure of water: 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.25 kPa at 30 C, 95 kPa at 98 C, 1509 kPa at 196 C; the last point (899 C) is 4294946604 (near the u32 maximum), so above 196 C no condensation is possible. Raising the curve lowers the modelled condensation (shorter heater protection), lowering it lengthens it; the physics argues for leaving it. Confidence: read.

table.name: High Pedal Entry Threshold
table.description:
Accelerator position, by barometric pressure, at or above which the ECU switches to the high-pedal cam targets (set 2), provided vehicle speed is steady. Lowering it uses the high-pedal cams earlier. Stock 90 % everywhere. Other functions also read this high-pedal flag.
Details: High-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (0x10F848 -> FFF8B410, 0x11C15C, read): FFF8B410 counts passes with the accelerator FFF88A5E at or above this threshold (by barometric pressure FFF88A42 = FFF88668) while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 changes by less than cal 0x35B16... per pass (by gear FFF888A0) and FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear. The bit sets once FFF8B410 reaches 05D740 (1 pass) and clears after the pedal stays below cal 0x36518 for cal 0x36516 passes. The AVCS uses the bit to pick cam target set 2; 12 other functions read FFF8A8A4 (not reviewed). Stock 90 % at every pressure. p16 (read): the pass counter FFF8B410 (0x10F848 <- 0x1140BC <- 0x1E1560) runs in the 80 ms OS task (one pass = 80 ms); the latch 0x11C15C runs every 10 ms. Confidence: read.

table.name: High Pedal Tip-In Rate Threshold
table.description:
Pedal-rise rate, by pedal position, that sets the high-pedal flag immediately on a fast stab at the pedal (above about 90 %), for both the high-pedal cam targets and Injection Timing (High Pedal), without waiting for the normal entry delay. Stock never triggers below 89 % pedal.
Details: 0x10F7DC (10 ms task, read): when the pedal rise FFF88C5C (= pedal FFF88A5E - the previous pedal sample FFF88C60, 0x09F234) is at or above this(pedal), FFF8B40E is loaded with 05D410 (6 passes) and otherwise counts down; zero while FFF8A8A5 b0 is clear (0x1194DC: neutral switch and two status flags). With B40E nonzero and the pedal at or above 05D6F0 / 05D6E4 (90 %), 0x119500 / 0x119438 set FFF8A8A5 b2 / FFF8A8A3 b0 after cal 0x35B3C (5) passes, and those set the high-pedal latches FFF8A8A4 b7 (AVCS target set 2, 0x11C15C) and b6 (Injection Timing (High Pedal), 0x11C0C4) without waiting for the 80 ms counter of High Pedal Entry Threshold (read). Stock 100 % (never) below 89 % pedal and 6 % per sample at 90 % and above. The sample interval of FFF88C5C was not settled. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description:
Minimum engine speed for intake cam control by oil temperature. Below it the cams are held at rest and ignition fades to the AVCS Inactive timing tables. Stock 365 rpm at 90 degC rising to 855 rpm at 140 degC (probably because hot, thin oil needs more rpm for pressure).
Details: When used: always. 0x15CD4C (read): the intake AVCS may run closed-loop (enable status FFF8AB2E = 0) only while rpm FFF8CE9C >= this(oil temperature FFF8B97C) (hysteresis cal 0x3B888 = 100 rpm), rpm below cal 0x3B880, oil above cal 0x3B884 and time since start >= 05E57C; otherwise the cam state FFF8AB2C becomes 4 (held at default) and Primary Ignition fades to the AVCS Inactive tables (my research notes). Stock 365 rpm at 90 degC rising to 855 rpm at 140 degC (hot, thin oil needs more rpm for oil pressure, inferred). FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp)
table.description:
Minimum engine speed for exhaust cam control by oil temperature; works like Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp). Stock identical to the intake table (365-855 rpm between 90 and 140 degC oil).
Details: When used: always. 0x16144C, the exhaust twin of 0x15CD4C (read): exhaust AVCS status FFF8AB20 / state FFF8AB1E, same logic as Intake AVCS Minimum RPM (Oil Temp). Stock identical to 05E570 (365-855 rpm over 90-140 degC). FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start
table.description:
How long after every start the cams are held at their rest position before cam control begins, by coolant temperature at start. Stock is 10 s below -20 degC, 2.8 s when warm and 3.7 s when hot. Raise for a longer hold, lower to start cam control sooner.
Details: When used: after every start. 0x15B59C (intake) and 0x15F7C0 (exhaust, descriptor 05E770, same data 0x03AD6A) (read): while FFF88A76 / 2 is below this(coolant at start FFF88A46) the AVCS request FFF8AB2D / FFF8AB1F is 4 (hold at the default position, no closed-loop cam control). FFF88A76 counts 10 ms passes since the engine left cranking (0x07E1AC: +1 per call, saturating at 65535, reset while FFF88A27 bit 0 is set; called once per pass from 0x07D3E4 in the 10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read), so one table count = 20 ms. Stock 10 s (raw 500) below -20 degC, 8 s at -10, 5 s at 0, 3.5 s at 10, 2.8 s at 20-60 degC, 3.7 s from 70 degC. A second table (05E414) can only shorten it once the delay has run out (read), which has no effect in stock (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description:
Minimum oil temperature before cam control is allowed, by intake air temperature at start (a proxy for how cold the engine was). Below it the cams stay at rest. Stock: 80 degC oil after a -40 degC start, 25 degC after a 0 degC start, no limit from 5 degC up.
Details: When used: always. 0x15B59C (intake) and 0x15F7C0 (exhaust, descriptor 05E788, same data 0x03AD8A) (read): the active-control request (FFF8AB2D = 1) needs oil temperature FFF8B97C >= this(FFF8CEE6) plus the rpm / pedal windows; otherwise the request is 9 (FFF8AB28 bit 5 / FFF8AB24 bit 5 clear). FFF8CEE6 = intake air temperature latched at start, (IAT + 50 - 10) x 65536/160 (0x06AF58, read), the iat_409 scale. Stock 80 degC oil for a start at -40 degC, 25 degC at 0 degC, no limit from 5 degC up. FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start
table.description:
Appears to set how long after a start (by coolant at start) the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty instead of closed-loop control. Only matters if longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start; in stock it never is, so it probably has no effect on a stock car.
Details: When used: every pass while running; only matters if it is longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start. Time after start (A76/2, 20 ms counts) during which the intake OCV duty is held at the fixed 52 % (cal 0x3CE52) instead of closed-loop cam control, when the oil-temperature condition (Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp) also holds. Stock 10 s at -40..-20 degC coolant at start, 8 s at -10, 5 s at 0, 3.5 s at 10, 2.8 s at 20-50, 2 s from 60 degC; this is never longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start (equal up to 50 degC, shorter from 60 degC), so in stock the window ends before closed-loop control starts (inferred). Its own data block (0x3D066), not the one of AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second, Unused) (0x3D088); the two hold the same stock values (read). 0x15B59C (intake AVCS request, read; arguments mapped from the call at seg_0x150000.c:7959 and the stack offsets at 0x15B5BC-0x15B68C): 05E420 and 05E414 / 05E408 are read with coolant at start FFF88A46 (R14 at 0x15B664-0x15B674), 05E42C and 05E438 with IAT at start FFF8CEE6 (R12 at 0x15B678-0x15B68C). Output FFF8AB2A bit 3 = 1 unless all of: AVCS enable status FFF8AB2E = 0, FFF88ADA bit 3 clear, FFF8AB27 bit 6 clear, not (rpm CE9C <= cal 0x3AD38 = 450 rpm with FFF88A28 bit 1) and FFF88A76/2 >= Fixed Duty Window. Output FFF8AB2A bit 4 = (Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp(IAT at start) <= oil FFF8B97C x 328 >> 16) and FFF8AB28 bit 7 and FFF8AB27 bit 5 and the rpm/angle windows of cals 0x3AD1A-0x3AD46 (same structure as AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start), which sets FFF8AB28 bit 5). In 0x15DF20 (cam 1) and 0x15E63C (cam 2), when both bits are set the duty B8DE is not feedback + hold but max(min(cal 0x3B8FE, cal 0x3CE52), cal 0x3B8FC) = 1300 = 52 % (read); B8DE becomes the OCV output B8EA only in AVCS states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3, slice D). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description:
Appears to set the oil temperature, by intake air temperature at start, above which the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start instead of closed-loop control. Stock 79 degC after a very cold start, no limit from 5 degC up. Only acts during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start, which in stock ends before cam control starts, so it probably has no effect on a stock car.
Details: When used: every pass while running. Oil temperature above which the intake fixed-duty hold (52 %, cal 0x3CE52) may apply during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start, by IAT at start. Stock 79 degC at IAT -40..-20 degC, 54 degC at -10, 44 at -5, 24 at 0, 0 degC (no limit, byte 64) from +5 degC; close to AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start) except at IAT -20 degC (79 vs 70 degC). 0x15B59C (intake AVCS request, read; arguments mapped from the call at seg_0x150000.c:7959 and the stack offsets at 0x15B5BC-0x15B68C): 05E420 and 05E414 / 05E408 are read with coolant at start FFF88A46 (R14 at 0x15B664-0x15B674), 05E42C and 05E438 with IAT at start FFF8CEE6 (R12 at 0x15B678-0x15B68C). Output FFF8AB2A bit 3 = 1 unless all of: AVCS enable status FFF8AB2E = 0, FFF88ADA bit 3 clear, FFF8AB27 bit 6 clear, not (rpm CE9C <= cal 0x3AD38 = 450 rpm with FFF88A28 bit 1) and FFF88A76/2 >= Fixed Duty Window. Output FFF8AB2A bit 4 = (Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp(IAT at start) <= oil FFF8B97C x 328 >> 16) and FFF8AB28 bit 7 and FFF8AB27 bit 5 and the rpm/angle windows of cals 0x3AD1A-0x3AD46 (same structure as AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start), which sets FFF8AB28 bit 5). In 0x15DF20 (cam 1) and 0x15E63C (cam 2), when both bits are set the duty B8DE is not feedback + hold but max(min(cal 0x3B8FE, cal 0x3CE52), cal 0x3B8FC) = 1300 = 52 % (read); B8DE becomes the OCV output B8EA only in AVCS states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3, slice D). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description:
Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. Stock about -9.5 % to +8 % at the error extremes, 0 at zero error.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard); positive error = the cam must move away from its rest position, and stock duty rises with it. When used: intake cam 1 (0x15DF20, error FFF8B956) at idle / standstill. This is the idle variant, used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF88C64 bit 5) and vehicle speed FFF88BE8 x 9/160 < cal 0x3B904 (4 km/h); otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / cam 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust cam 1 / cam 2), read: duty = learned hold duty (FFF8B8E8 / FFF8B8E6 intake cam 1 / 2, FFF8B8FE / FFF8B8FC exhaust cam 1 / 2) + (P + D) x cal 0x3B90C/100 (exhaust cal 0x3C7E2; both 100 %), clamped 31.9...81.1 % (exhaust 32.1...81.1 %). P = this table (-100 + x/327.68 %) x oil factor/128, used when the cam error (intake FFF8B956 / B954 from 0x15CF8C, exhaust FFF8B916 / B914 from 0x16168C; target - actual) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3B90A intake, 0x3C7E0 exhaust). The feedback duty is the output only in the active states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3 intake, FFF8AB24 bit 3 exhaust). Stock -4.5...-9.5 % at -40 deg error, +3.5...+8 % at +40 deg, 0 at 0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)
table.description:
Proportional part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used. Stock within 0.5 % of the cam 1 table.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard); positive error = the cam must move away from its rest position, and stock duty rises with it. When used: intake cam 2 (0x15E63C, error FFF8B954) at idle / standstill. This is the idle variant, used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF88C64 bit 5) and vehicle speed FFF88BE8 x 9/160 < cal 0x3B904 (4 km/h); otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used. 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / cam 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust cam 1 / cam 2), read: duty = learned hold duty (FFF8B8E8 / FFF8B8E6 intake cam 1 / 2, FFF8B8FE / FFF8B8FC exhaust cam 1 / 2) + (P + D) x cal 0x3B90C/100 (exhaust cal 0x3C7E2; both 100 %), clamped 31.9...81.1 % (exhaust 32.1...81.1 %). P = this table (-100 + x/327.68 %) x oil factor/128, used when the cam error (intake FFF8B956 / B954 from 0x15CF8C, exhaust FFF8B916 / B914 from 0x16168C; target - actual) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3B90A intake, 0x3C7E0 exhaust). The feedback duty is the output only in the active states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3 intake, FFF8AB24 bit 3 exhaust). Stock within 0.5 % of the cam 1 table. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description:
Proportional part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used at idle with the pedal fully released; otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. Larger values correct cam error faster. Stock about -9 % to +7.5 % at the error extremes.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard); positive error = the cam must move away from its rest position, and stock duty rises with it. When used: exhaust cam 1 (0x16269C, error FFF8B916, state FFF8AB1E) at idle. This is the idle variant, used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF88C64 bit 5) and FFF88E7E < cal 0x3B904 x 128 (FFF88E7E not identified; the intake twin uses vehicle speed there); otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / cam 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust cam 1 / cam 2), read: duty = learned hold duty (FFF8B8E8 / FFF8B8E6 intake cam 1 / 2, FFF8B8FE / FFF8B8FC exhaust cam 1 / 2) + (P + D) x cal 0x3B90C/100 (exhaust cal 0x3C7E2; both 100 %), clamped 31.9...81.1 % (exhaust 32.1...81.1 %). P = this table (-100 + x/327.68 %) x oil factor/128, used when the cam error (intake FFF8B956 / B954 from 0x15CF8C, exhaust FFF8B916 / B914 from 0x16168C; target - actual) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3B90A intake, 0x3C7E0 exhaust). The feedback duty is the output only in the active states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3 intake, FFF8AB24 bit 3 exhaust). Stock -8...-9.2 % at -40 deg error, +6.5...+7.5 % at +40 deg. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 2)
table.description:
Proportional part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used at idle with the pedal fully released; otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used. Stock close to cam 1.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard); positive error = the cam must move away from its rest position, and stock duty rises with it. When used: exhaust cam 2 (0x162D18, error FFF8B914) at idle. This is the idle variant, used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF88C64 bit 5) and FFF88E7E < cal 0x3B904 x 128 (FFF88E7E not identified; the intake twin uses vehicle speed there); otherwise Exhaust AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 2) is used. 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / cam 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust cam 1 / cam 2), read: duty = learned hold duty (FFF8B8E8 / FFF8B8E6 intake cam 1 / 2, FFF8B8FE / FFF8B8FC exhaust cam 1 / 2) + (P + D) x cal 0x3B90C/100 (exhaust cal 0x3C7E2; both 100 %), clamped 31.9...81.1 % (exhaust 32.1...81.1 %). P = this table (-100 + x/327.68 %) x oil factor/128, used when the cam error (intake FFF8B956 / B954 from 0x15CF8C, exhaust FFF8B916 / B914 from 0x16168C; target - actual) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3B90A intake, 0x3C7E0 exhaust). The feedback duty is the output only in the active states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3 intake, FFF8AB24 bit 3 exhaust). Stock close to cam 1. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description:
Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control. Stock only acts at 700 rpm, and Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor turns it off from 80 degC oil.
Details: When used: intake cam 1 in active control (0x15DF20). D term (read): when |FFF8B952| (the filtered rate of change of the cam error, 0x15CF8C) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3CCC8), D = (-100 + this(rpm, rate)/327.68 %) x oil factor/128 x 05E5F4(error)/128 (128 = 1.0 in stock), added to the P term. Oil factor Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor (05E590). Stock -10 % / +3 % at the extreme rates at 700 rpm only, 0 elsewhere. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description:
Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control. Stock identical to cam 1.
Details: When used: intake cam 2 in active control (0x15E63C, rate FFF8B950). D term (read): when |FFF8B950| (the filtered rate of change of the cam 2 error, 0x15CF8C) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3CCC8), D = (-100 + this(rpm, rate)/327.68 %) x oil factor/128 x 05E5F4(error)/128 (128 = 1.0 in stock), added to the P term. Stock identical to cam 1. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description:
Damping (derivative) part of the exhaust cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing; added to the proportional term during active cam control. More damping reduces overshoot. Stock about -10 % to +3 % at the extreme rates, 0 near zero rate.
Details: When used: exhaust cam 1 in active control (0x16269C, rate FFF8B912). D term (read): when |FFF8B912| (the filtered rate of change of the cam error) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3CCC6), D = (-100 + this(rpm, rate)/327.68 %) x oil factor/128 x 05E924(error)/128 (128 = 1.0 in stock), added to the P term. Oil factor 05E8C0 (constant 1.0 in stock, not in this set). Stock -10/-6/-3 % and +3/+1.5 % at the extreme rates from 1000 to 5000 rpm, 0 near zero rate. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 2)
table.description:
Damping (derivative) part of the exhaust cam 2 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing; added to the proportional term during active cam control. Stock identical to cam 1.
Details: When used: exhaust cam 2 in active control (0x162D18, rate FFF8B910). D term (read): when |FFF8B910| (the filtered rate of change of the cam error) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3CCC6), D = (-100 + this(rpm, rate)/327.68 %) x oil factor/128 x 05E9A8(error)/128 (128 = 1.0 in stock), added to the P term. Stock identical to cam 1. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor
table.description:
Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the intake cam damping term for both cams. Stock 1.0 up to 70 degC and 0 from 80 degC, so the damping term only acts with cool oil.
Details: When used: intake D term (0x15DF20 cam 1; 05E614 in 0x15E63C cam 2, same data 0x03CE0A) (read): D x this(oil FFF8B97C)/128. Stock 1.0 up to 70 degC oil and 0 from 80 degC, so the rate term only acts with cool oil. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Oil Factor (Normal, Positive Error)
table.description:
Oil-temperature multiplier (128 = 1.0) on the driving intake cam proportional duty when the cam lags its target. Applies to both intake cams. Stock 1.0 up to 100 degC, rising to 1.05 from 120 degC.
Details: When used: intake AVCS active control, normal branch, cam error > 0 (target ahead of actual) (0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C; descriptor 05E620 for cam 2) (read): P = the main P table x this(oil FFF8B97C)/128. table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description:

Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard); positive error = the cam must move away from its rest position, and stock duty rises with it. When used: the main (driving) AVCS proportional duty, used whenever the idle variant is not: the accelerator is applied or vehicle speed is at least 4 km/h (FFF88BE8 x 9/160 >= cal 0x3B904) (read, 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C intake, 0x16269C / 0x162D18 exhaust). Rows rpm, columns cam error (degrees); the duty term is summed with the rate (D) term and scaled by the oil-temperature factor into the OCV duty. 32768 = 0 % (stock about -9 % to +8 %). Same shape and scaling as the idle variant (Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)); stock data differ from it only in the outer cells. Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second, Unused)
table.description:
A second start-delay table that can only shorten the AVCS hold after the hold has already ended, so it never changes anything. Edit AVCS Activation Delay After Start instead.
Details: 0x15B59C (read): the hold threshold is 05E408 while the hold flag FFF86848 is set or the engine is stopped (FFF88A76 = 0, which also clears FFF8683B); only after the hold has ended does it become min(05E408, this). Since FFF88A76 only rises while running and coolant at start FFF88A46 is fixed, min(05E408, this) <= 05E408 <= A76/2 can never set the hold again; a stall resets A76 to 0 and restores 05E408 first. So this table has no effect on the output (read). Stock equals 05E408 up to 50 C, 2.0 s instead of 2.8-3.7 s from 60 C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Current Integral Step (Off in Stock)
table.description:

Read by 0x15ED58 (cam 1) and as 05E71C by 0x15F158 (cam 2), same data 0x03BC50. 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). table.name: Intake OCV Base Duty (Cam 1, Legacy Path, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Base intake cam 1 valve duty by rpm for an older, byte-based cam control path. No effect on a stock car: a calibration switch selects the normal feedback control instead.
Details: When used: never in stock (cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 set). Base term by rpm of the intake cam 1 OCV duty in the legacy byte-based AVCS path: about 49.2-52.0 % duty before the FFF88AA4 factor; the learned and feedback bytes are added around 128 (= 51.2 %). Module (read): seg 0x100000 0x104xxx-0x106xxx is the byte-based cam path; 0x10466C (intake, called at seg_0x100000.c:3516 with rpm CD54, FFF88AA4, learned bytes FFF8147A/147C/147E, feedback bytes FFF8B368, cam errors B956/B954) forms per cam: B352 = this(rpm) x 026EB0/026EC0(FFF88AA4)/128 (stock factor 0.89-1.0); B356 = 147A if the cam error >= cal 0x26E82 (364 = 2.0 deg), 147C if <= cal 0x26E84 (-2.0 deg), else 128; B366 = clamp(B368 + B352 + 147E + B356 - 384, 0, 250). 0x106A0C does the same for the exhaust cams (05CF08/05CF14, factors 0298F4/029904, errors B916/B914, thresholds cal 0x298C6/0x298C8) into B380. The OCV duty routines 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust) set duty B8DE = B366[cam] x 10 (B380 for exhaust) only when cal 0x3CCC4 bit 0 is clear (read). FFF88AA4 = (FFF88AE6 >> 8 - 10) x 1.6 (0x060000 area, read); FFF88AE6 not identified. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

Details: 0x0F2274 (read): one of the minimum idle-speed requests maxed into B246 (value << 6 = 12.5 rpm per count); skipped (0) while FFF88E2B bit5 is set. table.name: Idle Post-Start Mode Exit Coolant
table.description:

Details: When used: idle modes 2/3 (post-start) in the idle mode state machine 0x0F354C (read). Once time since start FFF88A76 >= cal 0x24E92 (200 = 2 s; neither exit happens earlier), the mode goes to 5 (normal idle) when coolant FFF88A44 >= this(coolant at start FFF88A46) or when the vehicle moves (about 2-4 km/h); while the warm-up flag FFF88EA2 bit 1 is set it stays in 2/3 regardless of coolant and goes to mode 7 only once the vehicle moves (0x0F354C, read; my research notes). Stock: 50 degC (122 F) for starts below 75 degC, 120 degC (65535, never) for warmer starts, which then leave the post-start mode only by moving. table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 1 to 2)
table.description:

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Minimum idle speed requested by another module over CAN, by request code. No effect on a stock car: only used when a calibration switch is set, which is off in stock.
Details: When used: never in stock. 0x10EA40 (read; 20 ms task 0x1E0AE8 via 0x113060): while the network variant / frame gate holds (FFF88E0C bit 3 with FFF88621 = 1, bit 4 with FFF88618 = 1, or bit 7 with FFF88618 = 1) and FFF8A9A3 bit 0 is set, FFF8B3FA = this(CAN code FFF8A88A) for cal 0x35534 = 250 passes (5 s), then it falls by cal 0x35532 = 5 counts (1 rpm) per pass; 0 when FFF8A9A3 bit 0 clears. 0x10EB1C takes FFF854E2 = max(B3FA, a second request from FFF8A8D9 = CAN FFF88B90 + 26 scaled by cal 0x3555C, limited to cal 0x35556 = 1500 rpm), optionally remaps it through 05D3C0 / 05D3CC, and stores FFF8B3FC. FFF8B3FC's only reader is 0x0EE338, which passes it to the idle target module 0x0F2274 as stack argument 7 (disassembly at 0x0EF2E4, read); there min(B3FC, 0x1E00) >> 6 (12.5 rpm units) is maxed into a minimum idle-speed request only when param_1 = cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 and FFF8A9A2 bit 6 are both set (0x0F2826 reads @(158,R15) = param_11, read). Cal 0x1D0AE = 0, the same switch that keeps the alternate A/C idle air path and radiator-fan duty tables off, so this request has no effect in stock. Unit: rpm x 5.12 (read from the >> 6 into 12.5 rpm units and the 0x1E00 = 1500 rpm cap). Stock 700 rpm for codes 0-4, 800 rpm for 5-9. Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Alternate, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Remaps the CAN idle speed request before it is applied. No effect on a stock car: the request is only used when a calibration switch is set, which is off in stock. Stock is a straight pass-through.
Details: When used: never in stock (see CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate, Off in Stock): its output FFF8B3FC only acts with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0, which is 0). 0x10EB1C (read, disassembly 0x10EC56-0x10EC7A): the combined request FFF854E2 (input) is passed through this table into FFF8B3FC when FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is set and FFF8A8A1 bit 7 is clear; with both set 05D3CC is used instead; with FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear the request is stored unchanged; with FFF88B8E bit 0 (CAN 0x280) the output is cal 0x3555E (0). FFF8A7E2 bit 0 is always set on the manual coding (brief), so this is the table that would apply. Stock identity (615-923 rpm in = out). Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Flag Set, Alternate, Off in Stock)
table.description:

Details: When used: never in stock (output FFF8B3FC only acts with cal 0x1D0AE bit 0, which is 0). 0x10EB1C (read): used instead of 05D3C0 when FFF8A8A1 bit 7 is also set; FFF8A8A1 bit 7 comes from CAN bits FFF88B95 bits 0/1 via 0x11BBB4 (read, meaning not identified). Input = combined request FFF854E2. Stock identity (615-923 rpm in = out). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial)
table.description:
Extra idle air right after start, by start type (first start, restart, after a stall, remote start; start-type meanings inferred) and coolant. It is held after start, then decays by Post-Start Idle Air Decay once rpm reaches the idle target. Stock large when cold, small from 40 degC.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read; args per call in module 0x0EE338): post-start idle air B20E = max(start air, staged air 05C49C family), added to the idle air at half weight (0x0F0AF8). While the engine is not running (FFF88A27 bit0, cranking) the start air is set from this(start type FFF8A6E7, coolant FFF88A44) (TGVs not forced closed, FFF8A881 bit4 clear); once running it is held, then multiplied by Post-Start Idle Air Decay every 4th pass after rpm has reached the idle target and the time since start FFF88A76 passed 05C5C0. Start type 0 = first start, 1 = restart after key-off, 2 = after a stall, 3 = received start request (my research notes, inferred). Stock 15360 cold -> 640 base-air units at >= 40 degC. p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial, TGV Closed)
table.description:
TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air (Initial): extra idle air right after start by start type and coolant, held and then decayed once rpm reaches the idle target. Stock large when cold, 640 base-air units when warm.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read; args per call in module 0x0EE338): post-start idle air B20E = max(start air, staged air 05C49C family), added to the idle air at half weight (0x0F0AF8). As Post-Start Idle Air (Initial) but used while FFF8A881 bit4 (TGVs closed). Stock 17920 cold -> 640 base-air units. p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay
table.description:
Multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air once rpm has reached the idle target and Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay has passed, by start type and coolant. Smaller = faster fade. Stock 0.97-0.99.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read): every 4th pass (cal 0x257A6) after rpm has once reached the idle target and FFF88A76 (time since start) >= 05C5C0/05C5FC, the post-start air is multiplied by this(start type FFF8A6E8, coolant FFF88A44) (the @025814 coolant table only when FFF88BE8 >= cal 0x257AC = 8889, i.e. never). TGVs not forced closed. Stock 0.97..0.99 per step (smaller = faster decay). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay (TGV Closed)
table.description:
TGV-forced-closed version of Post-Start Idle Air Decay: multiplier applied every 40 ms to the post-start idle air after the decay delay. Smaller = faster fade. Stock 0.97-0.99.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read): every 4th pass (cal 0x257A6) after rpm has once reached the idle target and FFF88A76 (time since start) >= 05C5C0/05C5FC, the post-start air is multiplied by this(start type FFF8A6E8, coolant FFF88A44) (the @025814 coolant table only when FFF88BE8 >= cal 0x257AC = 8889, i.e. never). TGVs closed (FFF8A881 bit4). Stock 0.97..0.99 per step. p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air Decay Delay
table.description:
Time after start, by start type and coolant at start, before the post-start idle air starts to decay (rpm must also have reached the idle target). Longer = extra air held longer. Stock 1.5 s for a cold first start, 0.25-1.5 s when warmer.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read): the post-start air (start air) starts to decay only once FFF88A76 (time since start, counts) reaches this(start type FFF8A6E8, start coolant FFF88A46) and rpm has reached the idle target; it also bounds the stop-start restart window. TGVs not forced closed. Stock 1.5 s for a first start below 0 degC, 0.01 s for restarts there, 0.25..1.5 s above. p16 (read): FFF88A76 (time since start) counts 10 ms passes (0x07E1AC <- 0x07D3E4 <- 0x1DFE3C); stock 150 = 1.5 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air IAT Add
table.description:
Added to Post-Start Staged Air Level by intake air temperature, for the timed post-start air bump. Stock 2560 base-air units at -40 degC only, 0 elsewhere.
Details: 0x0F1270 (read): staged post-start air FFF84E48 (part of B20E = max(start air, staged air), half weight). A pass counter starts once rpm first reaches the idle target after the start (cal 0x257A8 = 0 margin) and runs while the engine runs; every 4th pass (cal 0x257A6): before Start Time the staged air is held (0 after a start), between Start Time and End Time it rises by Ramp Step per check up to Level + IAT Add, after End Time it is multiplied by Decay. The other staged-air tables use start type FFF8A6E8 x coolant FFF88A44; this one only intake air temperature FFF88A48. Stock: active only at -40 degC and from 70 degC up (zeros between = Start/End 0, so the staged air is decayed to 0 at once; checked as real data, the five data blocks are contiguous 160-byte arrays with no overlap) - a hot-restart air bump (inferred). This table: added to the Level by intake air temperature FFF88A48 (stock 2560 base-air units at -40 degC only). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Key-On/Cranking)
table.description:
Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure, used at key-on and while cranking. Stock 1.72 at 58 kPa to 1.0 at 100 kPa. The two Running copies hold the same data: edit all three together.
Details: When used: only at key-on and while cranking (engine state 1/2); in running the copies Idle Air Altitude Factor (Running, ...) 05C61C / 05C628 are used, so edit all three together (read, slice C). 0x0F19E0 -> FFF811D5, multiplies the idle air B1FE (cal 0x1D0BD bit7 = 1). 1.72 at 58 kPa -> 1.0 at 100 kPa. Copies 05C61C/05C628 hold the same data. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Air Altitude Factor (Running, A/C Off)
table.description:
Multiplier on idle air by barometric pressure while running with the A/C off. Stock 1.72 at 58 kPa to 1.0 at 100 kPa, identical to the other two copies: edit all three together.
Details: When used: engine running (FFF8906B not 1/2) and FFF8A7DF bit 5 clear. 0x0F19E0 / 0x0F088C (read): FFF811D5 = Idle Air Altitude Factor 05C610(baro FFF88668) while the engine state FFF8906B is 1 or 2 (key-on / cranking), otherwise 05C61C when FFF8A7DF bit 5 is clear and 05C628 when it is set. FFF811D5 multiplies the idle air B1FE (x/32, cal 0x1D0BD bit 7 = 1 stock; 0x0F0A90, read). FFF8A7DF bit 5 is FFF8CDD2 bit 7 debounced by 0x0F40D4 (cals 0x34ED4/0x34ED5), and CDD2 bit 7 is a copy of FFF8A9A2 bit 6, the A/C-compressor-engaged flag (0x0B7712, read; A/C meaning inferred as in the A/C idle air tables). So this copy is used with the A/C off. Stock: identical data to Idle Air Altitude Factor (05C610), 1.72 at 58 kPa to 1.00 at 100 kPa; edit all three together to change the altitude correction. Confidence: read.
