Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). In recovery state 0 0x182900 (read) raises the limit by max((pedal - limit) / (10 x remaining passes), 05F240 = 1 % per pass) with remaining = this - FFF8BAEE (passes spent in state 0, 0x181AB8); 0x1839F0 ends the recovery (FFF8AC90 bit 7 clear) when FFF8BAEE reaches this, when the limit reaches the pedal, or when the pedal is released. Stock 50, 30, 30, 30 passes = 0.5, 0.3, 0.3, 0.3 s at 10/60/90/120 km/h. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Brake Pressure Threshold
table.description:
Brake pressure, by booster vacuum and vehicle speed, above which the brake counts as applied for brake override. Raise to make override need a firmer brake press. Used while the brake-pressure signal from the stability control unit is valid. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while the VDC brake-pressure signal is valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4, set after cal 0x435D6 = 100 passes with no CAN/VDC fault, 0x181978 / 0x1839B8). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x183178 (read, args checked in the assembly): brake applied FFF8AC90 bit 0 is set when FFF8AC94 >= this(brake booster vacuum FFF8BAFC, speed FFF8AC95) and cleared when FFF8AC94 <= cal 0x43442 (1); without a valid pressure signal the brake switch FFF88E2F bit 3 is used instead. FFF8BAFC = max(0, baro - FFF88D10) with FFF88D10 the filtered analog pressure input FFF88D0C (raw x 29888/65536 + 416, kPa x 256 absolute) while cal 0x57585 bit 5 is set (stock; 0x182B28, read); brake booster vacuum sensor inferred. Axis 1 is that vacuum (0-30 kPa = 0-4.35 psi). Stock 5/9/14/25/35 at 10-30 km/h, falling to 1/4/9/19/31 from 100 km/h (rows 0, 5, 10, 20, 30 kPa vacuum): more booster vacuum or less speed = higher threshold. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Deceleration Threshold (No Pressure Signal)

scaling.units: ms per km/h of speed drop
ms per mph of speed drop

table.description:
Deceleration needed (by pedal and speed) to confirm braking when the brake-pressure signal is not available, so brake override can still act from the brake switch. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: only while the VDC brake-pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear) and the brake was applied over the accelerator (FFF8AC90 bit 6). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x183A9C (read, args checked in the assembly): FFF8AC91 bit 2 (brake confirmed by deceleration) sets when the vehicle is slowing (FFF8AC90 bit 2, FFF8AC96 > 0) and cal 0x435DA (23) < FFF8BB06 < this(pedal, speed); with a valid pressure signal it simply follows brake applied. FFF8AC91 bit 2 replaces the minimum-pedal condition of Brake Override Delay. Stock (ms per km/h; decel = 1000/x km/h/s): 236/130/113/109 at 14 % pedal (4.2-9.2 km/h/s), 2000/260/143/118 at 28 %, 2000/1936/248/134 at 56 % pedal (columns 10/30/70/100 km/h). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: VDC Torque Request Correction
table.description:
Correction, by the gap between the stability control (VDC) torque request and actual engine torque, that sets how tightly the ECU limits target torque during a VDC torque reduction (VDC meaning inferred). Stock opens the limit well above the request when engine torque is below it, and follows the request with a small undershoot otherwise.
Details: When used: every 10 ms (0x117778 from 0x110AAC, task 0x1DFE3C), effective while the VDC torque-reduction flag is active. 0x117778 (read; stack arguments checked in the disassembly: param_5 @36 = IAT FFF88A48, param_8 @48 = FFF8B404, param_9 @52 = FFF88B80 bit 2, param_10 @56 = FFF88DF6): on the active network variant (FFF88E0C bit 4) the request R is FFF888B6 = CAN 0x0D2 bytes 3:2 from the VDC unit (signals_rates_can, read), or the TCM limit FFF88DF6 x 20 + 10000 while FFF88B80 bit 2 (always clear on this MT car). Error e = R - FFF8B404 (the reported engine torque, see CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate) + 10000, floored at cal 0x35AB2 (-148 ft-lb, -200 Nm) -> FFF8B42A. Output FFF8B47C = R x 05D620(IAT)/128 (1.0 stock) + this(e) + an integrator FFF8568C (+0.4 ft-lb, +0.6 Nm per pass while e >= +2.2 ft-lb, +3 Nm, -0.4 ft-lb, -0.6 Nm per pass while e < 0, limited to -111..+111 ft-lb, -150..+150 Nm; cals 0x35AA6-0x35AB0) - offsets, floored at 0 ft-lb (read). The table and the integrator are suppressed (0) on the pass where FFF88B94 bit 0 or FFF88B80 bit 2 rises and while the request has just dropped by more than 7.7 ft-lb (10.4 Nm) (cal 0x35AF4, latch FFF8A89A) (read). FFF8B47C limits the target torque: 0x0BD404 sets FFF8AECA = min(FFF8AEAA, B47C x 8 - 64000) while FFF8A8A2 bit 6, which is FFF88B94 bit 0 (CAN 0x0D2 byte 4, VDC) unless FFF88E0E bit 0 (0x11C028 / 0x11B594, read); FFF8AECA is the boost-target torque (Phase7_Anchors). Meaning 'VDC traction-control torque request' inferred from the VDC frame. Axis: request minus reported engine torque (Nm). Stock, in Nm (1 Nm = 0.738 ft-lb): -18 for errors at or below -42, -9 at -21, 0 at 0, +30 at +21, +88 at +42, +264 at +104, +381 at +146 and above: when the request is above the engine torque the limit is opened well above the request, when it is below the limit follows the request with a small undershoot. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Maximum (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Upper limit, by barometric pressure, of a modelled brake-booster vacuum. No effect on a stock car: a calibration setting makes the ECU use the booster vacuum sensor input instead, so the model output is discarded.
Details: When used: never in stock. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182B28 (read, all stack args checked in the assembly) has three sources for the booster vacuum FFF8BAFC: cal 0x57585 bit 5 set (stock 0x73) = baro - analog pressure input FFF88D10; else bit 6 = fixed cal 0x43402 (50 kPa); else a model from manifold vacuum baro FFF88668 - MAP FFF88A34: while not braking at low manifold vacuum (FFF8AC90 bit 3 clear) the estimate is filtered (cal 0x43406) up towards the manifold vacuum as long as it is below this(baro); during braking it is reduced by 253 x 13/100 per count of brake-pressure rise (FFF8AC93 - FFF8AC92). With bit 5 set the model result is discarded (the output is overwritten), so this table has no effect in stock. Stock 3840/5120/7040/8960/12800 = 15/20/27.5/35/50 kPa (2.2-7.3 psi) at baro 65/71.5/78/84.5/97.5 kPa. Confidence: read.

table.name: Brake Booster Vacuum Model Manifold Threshold (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Manifold-vacuum threshold, by barometric pressure, for a brake-booster vacuum model. No effect on a stock car: stock uses a vacuum sensor input instead, and the model's results are discarded.
Details: When used: never with effect in stock. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x18390C (read): FFF8AC90 bit 3 = brake pressure FFF8AC94 >= cal 0x435BD (1) and FFF88A38 >= this(baro FFF88668) - 12800 (FFF88A38 = (MAP - baro)/2, so MAP - baro >= (this - 12800)/128 kPa), i.e. braking with too little manifold vacuum to recharge the booster. Bit 3 feeds only the brake-pressure latches FFF8AC92 / FFF8AC93 / FFF8BAFE and the manifold-vacuum model of 0x182B28, whose results are unused while cal 0x57585 bit 5 is set (stock) and FFF8BB00 has no reader (read, grep). Stock 11435..9387 = MAP - baro >= -10.7 kPa (-1.55 psi) at 65 kPa baro to -26.7 kPa (-3.87 psi) at 97.5 kPa. Confidence: read.

table.name: Alternator Command from Target Voltage
table.description:
Alternator control duty by target charging voltage (probably). Changing it changes the charging voltage the alternator actually reaches. Stock linear: about 10 % duty at 11.7 V to 86 % at 15.1 V. Also feeds Idle Air Trim (Charging Command).
Details: When used: every pass of the charging module (0x138BB0, called from the module body at seg 0x130000, read): B71E = clamp(this(target FFF8B6F4), cal 0x397CE = 167, cal 0x397D0 = 1500); B718 = B71E (cal 0x57584 bit 4 clear, 0x1373C8). B718 is written to timer E channel 20 as duty = min(B718, 1667)/1667 (0, below 17) by 0x1E0000 -> 0x1D98AC (read), so 1667 = 100 % duty: the alternator control duty (inferred). B718 also drives Idle Air Trim (Charging Command) and the electrical-load idle logic. B6F4 is the rate-limited charging target (0x136854), starting at cal 0x399B6 = 14300 (mV, inferred). Stock linear: 174 (10.4 %) at 11.7 V to 1438 (86 %) at 15.1 V; 1140 (68 %) at 14.3 V. Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Radiator fan duty by coolant for an alternate (duty-based) fan control path. No effect on a stock car: only used when a calibration switch is set, which is off in stock; the stock fan follows the coolant / A/C stage logic. Stock 30 % at 94-95 degC rising to 70 % from 100 degC.
Details: When used: never in stock. With cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 set, 0x0F8AAC (read) uses this when received byte FFF88BAA (CAN 0x282 byte 3) < cal 0x342EC (148, 146 to fall back) and FFF8A807 bit 5 is clear: duty B27C = this(coolant FFF88A44) once coolant >= cal 0x342DC (95 C, falls off 3 C lower), 100 % from cal 0x342E4 (100 C); used in fan mode 1 (0x0F7A88). Stock 30 % at 94-95 C, rising 8 % per degree to 70 % from 100 C. Radiator fan module 0x0F7618 (40 ms task, read): the fan stage FFF8A805 (0/1/2) drives timer E channel 10 fully on for stage >= 1 (FFF9981C bit 0, 0x0F8F08 -> 0x1E417C -> 0x1D9B8E) and port PF6 for stage 2 (FFF9981C bit 4, 0x0F8E70 -> 0x1D4E56 -> PFDR), and feeds the idle air (0x0ECE60, 0x0F5248) and torque adders (0x0C2B2C); the stages follow coolant and the A/C request (0x0F8764), so a two-relay radiator fan (inferred). Off in stock: cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 is clear (0x00), so the stage comes from the coolant/A/C stage logic (0x0F8764 -> A80C -> 0x0F74A8) and this duty path is never evaluated (the lookups sit only in the cal-set branches of 0x0F70B4 / 0x0F8AAC, read). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (Coolant, Flag A807 Set, Off in Stock)

Off in stock: cal 0x1D0AE bit 0 is clear (0x00), so the stage comes from the coolant/A/C stage logic (0x0F8764 -> A80C -> 0x0F74A8) and this duty path is never evaluated (the lookups sit only in the cal-set branches of 0x0F70B4 / 0x0F8AAC, read). With the bit set, A805 = stage from the duty FFF8B278 (0x0F7EC4: stage 1 from 40 %, stage 2 from 70 %). Confidence: read.

table.name: Radiator Fan Duty (A/C, CAN 0x280 Value, Off in Stock)

Radiator fan duty with the A/C requested, by an unidentified CAN value. No effect on a stock car: only used when a calibration switch is set, which is off in stock; the stock fan follows the coolant / A/C stage logic.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)
table.description:
Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 1.0, blended with the DAM 0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Mostly equal to Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Open); keep consistent if you change the torque model.
Details: When used: always (10 ms torque module, no cal gate). Torque at DAM 1.0 by rpm and load, used only for a torque value sent over CAN (maximum available torque, inferred), not for engine control. Same values as Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Open) x 10 in 214 of 256 cells; up to 35 ft-lb (48 Nm) higher at 4800-6800 rpm. Keep consistent with that table if you change the torque model. 0x110444 (read; called from the 0x110000 module at seg_0x110000.c:1129 with B46C, rpm CD54, air B4D6, IAT 88A48, Boost Limit A84E, DAM 811AE, crank period CD46; stack arguments checked in the disassembly): B450 = Full-Load Air Flow (rpm); B476 = Full-Load Reference Pressure (rpm); FFF8A8DF = temperature ratio 51.2 x T/Tref (Tref = cal 0x35A7A, 24.6 degC); A8DE = IAT Factor(A8DF); A8D4 = 51.2 x (A84E + 13.3 kPa) / reference pressure; A8D3 = Boost Limit Factor(A8D4); B44E = max(air B4D6, B450 x A8DE x A8D3 x 25/65536); load A8BD = B44E x CD46 x 0.64/6e7 (grams per 180 degrees crank, with CD46 = FFF8CF5C = 3.2 us counts per 180 degrees, signals_rates_can.md) x cal 0x36508 (28345) x 0.005457, i.e. load % against 0.6465 g per cylinder (inferred: standard air density x 0.5 L); B494 = Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A6 = (CAN, DAM 0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A0 = (B494 x DAM + B4A6 x (16 - DAM))/16; FFF8A89C = clamp(B4A0/16 - B46C/16 + 625, 0, 255) = (torque - FFF8AF62 loss torque) / 1.2 ft-lb (1.6 Nm). A89C is only read by the CAN transmit builder in seg 0x080000 (FFF8CC9D / FFF8CC3F, read); none of B44E, B450, A8BD, B494, B4A0, B4A6 has another reader (grep, read). Because B44E is never below the full-load air estimate, the transmitted value is the torque the engine could make at full load (or the actual load if higher): a maximum-available-torque signal for other modules (inferred). It does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost in this ECU. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 0)
table.description:
Engine torque by rpm and load at DAM 0, blended with the DAM 1.0 table by DAM. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. Close to, but somewhat lower than, the Engine Torque from Load (DAM 0) tables.

A89C is only read by the CAN transmit builder in seg 0x080000 (FFF8CC9D / FFF8CC3F, read); none of B44E, B450, A8BD, B494, B4A0, B4A6 has another reader (grep, read). Because B44E is never below the full-load air estimate, the transmitted value is the torque the engine could make at full load (or the actual load if higher): a maximum-available-torque signal for other modules (inferred). It does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost in this ECU. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque)
table.description:
Full-load air flow by rpm at Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque); a floor on the air used for the maximum-available torque the ECU sends over CAN (inferred). Raise it with a bigger turbo, or other modules see too low a torque capacity. Does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.
Details: When used: always. Air flow the engine takes at full load at the Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque) and an IAT of 24.6 degC (cal 0x35A7A); scaled by the IAT and boost-limit factors it is a floor on the air used for the CAN torque value. Stock 15.9 g/s at 800 rpm, 116 g/s at 3200 rpm, 218 g/s (maximum) from 5600 rpm, i.e. a volumetric efficiency of about 0.98-1.17 at the reference pressure (inferred). Raise it if a bigger turbo makes more air at the same pressure, or other modules will see a low torque capacity. 0x110444 (read; called from the 0x110000 module at seg_0x110000.c:1129 with B46C, rpm CD54, air B4D6, IAT 88A48, Boost Limit A84E, DAM 811AE, crank period CD46; stack arguments checked in the disassembly): B450 = Full-Load Air Flow (rpm); B476 = Full-Load Reference Pressure (rpm); FFF8A8DF = temperature ratio 51.2 x T/Tref (Tref = cal 0x35A7A, 24.6 degC); A8DE = IAT Factor(A8DF); A8D4 = 51.2 x (A84E + 13.3 kPa) / reference pressure; A8D3 = Boost Limit Factor(A8D4); B44E = max(air B4D6, B450 x A8DE x A8D3 x 25/65536); load A8BD = B44E x CD46 x 0.64/6e7 (grams per 180 degrees crank, with CD46 = FFF8CF5C = 3.2 us counts per 180 degrees, signals_rates_can.md) x cal 0x36508 (28345) x 0.005457, i.e. load % against 0.6465 g per cylinder (inferred: standard air density x 0.5 L); B494 = Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A6 = (CAN, DAM 0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A0 = (B494 x DAM + B4A6 x (16 - DAM))/16; FFF8A89C = clamp(B4A0/16 - B46C/16 + 625, 0, 255) = (torque - FFF8AF62 loss torque) / 1.2 ft-lb (1.6 Nm). A89C is only read by the CAN transmit builder in seg 0x080000 (FFF8CC9D / FFF8CC3F, read); none of B44E, B450, A8BD, B494, B4A0, B4A6 has another reader (grep, read). Because B44E is never below the full-load air estimate, the transmitted value is the torque the engine could make at full load (or the actual load if higher): a maximum-available-torque signal for other modules (inferred). It does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost in this ECU. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque)
table.description:
Manifold pressure that Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) refers to, by rpm. Raising the boost limit raises the estimate in proportion, up to 1.25x. Stock 104 kPa at 800 rpm up to 181 kPa at 5600 rpm. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.
Details: When used: always. Manifold pressure (kPa x 256, absolute) that Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) refers to; the current Boost Limit (FFF8A84E) is divided by it to scale that air estimate. Stock 104 kPa at 800 rpm, 165 kPa at 2000 rpm, 170 kPa at 2400-5200 rpm, 181 kPa peak at 5600 rpm (15.1-26.2 psia). If you raise the Boost Limit, the ratio rises and the estimate follows it up to 1.25 x (Full-Load Air Flow Boost Limit Factor). 0x110444 (read; called from the 0x110000 module at seg_0x110000.c:1129 with B46C, rpm CD54, air B4D6, IAT 88A48, Boost Limit A84E, DAM 811AE, crank period CD46; stack arguments checked in the disassembly): B450 = Full-Load Air Flow (rpm); B476 = Full-Load Reference Pressure (rpm); FFF8A8DF = temperature ratio 51.2 x T/Tref (Tref = cal 0x35A7A, 24.6 degC); A8DE = IAT Factor(A8DF); A8D4 = 51.2 x (A84E + 13.3 kPa) / reference pressure; A8D3 = Boost Limit Factor(A8D4); B44E = max(air B4D6, B450 x A8DE x A8D3 x 25/65536); load A8BD = B44E x CD46 x 0.64/6e7 (grams per 180 degrees crank, with CD46 = FFF8CF5C = 3.2 us counts per 180 degrees, signals_rates_can.md) x cal 0x36508 (28345) x 0.005457, i.e. load % against 0.6465 g per cylinder (inferred: standard air density x 0.5 L); B494 = Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A6 = (CAN, DAM 0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A0 = (B494 x DAM + B4A6 x (16 - DAM))/16; FFF8A89C = clamp(B4A0/16 - B46C/16 + 625, 0, 255) = (torque - FFF8AF62 loss torque) / 1.2 ft-lb (1.6 Nm). A89C is only read by the CAN transmit builder in seg 0x080000 (FFF8CC9D / FFF8CC3F, read); none of B44E, B450, A8BD, B494, B4A0, B4A6 has another reader (grep, read). Because B44E is never below the full-load air estimate, the transmitted value is the torque the engine could make at full load (or the actual load if higher): a maximum-available-torque signal for other modules (inferred). It does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost in this ECU. Confidence: read.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow IAT Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description:
Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by intake temperature ratio. Stock rises with intake temperature, which is unusual and not fully understood. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.
Details: When used: always. Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by absolute-temperature ratio IAT/Tref (Tref = cal 0x35A7A, 24.6 degC). Stock = sqrt(ratio) to 1 % (0.44 at 0.2, 0.70 at 0.5, 1.0 at 1.0, 1.41 at 2.0). Note: the factor rises with IAT as read, which is unusual for an air-mass estimate (doubt not resolved; the CAN value only). 0x110444 (read; called from the 0x110000 module at seg_0x110000.c:1129 with B46C, rpm CD54, air B4D6, IAT 88A48, Boost Limit A84E, DAM 811AE, crank period CD46; stack arguments checked in the disassembly): B450 = Full-Load Air Flow (rpm); B476 = Full-Load Reference Pressure (rpm); FFF8A8DF = temperature ratio 51.2 x T/Tref (Tref = cal 0x35A7A, 24.6 degC); A8DE = IAT Factor(A8DF); A8D4 = 51.2 x (A84E + 13.3 kPa) / reference pressure; A8D3 = Boost Limit Factor(A8D4); B44E = max(air B4D6, B450 x A8DE x A8D3 x 25/65536); load A8BD = B44E x CD46 x 0.64/6e7 (grams per 180 degrees crank, with CD46 = FFF8CF5C = 3.2 us counts per 180 degrees, signals_rates_can.md) x cal 0x36508 (28345) x 0.005457, i.e. load % against 0.6465 g per cylinder (inferred: standard air density x 0.5 L); B494 = Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A6 = (CAN, DAM 0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A0 = (B494 x DAM + B4A6 x (16 - DAM))/16; FFF8A89C = clamp(B4A0/16 - B46C/16 + 625, 0, 255) = (torque - FFF8AF62 loss torque) / 1.2 ft-lb (1.6 Nm). A89C is only read by the CAN transmit builder in seg 0x080000 (FFF8CC9D / FFF8CC3F, read); none of B44E, B450, A8BD, B494, B4A0, B4A6 has another reader (grep, read). Because B44E is never below the full-load air estimate, the transmitted value is the torque the engine could make at full load (or the actual load if higher): a maximum-available-torque signal for other modules (inferred). It does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost in this ECU. Confidence: read.

table.name: Full-Load Air Flow Boost Limit Factor (CAN Torque)
table.description:
Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by the ratio of the current boost limit to Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque). Stock passes the ratio through, capped at 1.25. Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost.
Details: When used: always. Multiplier on Full-Load Air Flow Estimate (CAN Torque) by the ratio of the current Boost Limit (FFF8A84E, kPa abs) to Full-Load Reference Pressure (CAN Torque). Stock passes the ratio through and caps it at 1.25 (64 counts). 0x110444 (read; called from the 0x110000 module at seg_0x110000.c:1129 with B46C, rpm CD54, air B4D6, IAT 88A48, Boost Limit A84E, DAM 811AE, crank period CD46; stack arguments checked in the disassembly): B450 = Full-Load Air Flow (rpm); B476 = Full-Load Reference Pressure (rpm); FFF8A8DF = temperature ratio 51.2 x T/Tref (Tref = cal 0x35A7A, 24.6 degC); A8DE = IAT Factor(A8DF); A8D4 = 51.2 x (A84E + 13.3 kPa) / reference pressure; A8D3 = Boost Limit Factor(A8D4); B44E = max(air B4D6, B450 x A8DE x A8D3 x 25/65536); load A8BD = B44E x CD46 x 0.64/6e7 (grams per 180 degrees crank, with CD46 = FFF8CF5C = 3.2 us counts per 180 degrees, signals_rates_can.md) x cal 0x36508 (28345) x 0.005457, i.e. load % against 0.6465 g per cylinder (inferred: standard air density x 0.5 L); B494 = Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A6 = (CAN, DAM 0)(rpm, A8BD), B4A0 = (B494 x DAM + B4A6 x (16 - DAM))/16; FFF8A89C = clamp(B4A0/16 - B46C/16 + 625, 0, 255) = (torque - FFF8AF62 loss torque) / 1.2 ft-lb (1.6 Nm). A89C is only read by the CAN transmit builder in seg 0x080000 (FFF8CC9D / FFF8CC3F, read); none of B44E, B450, A8BD, B494, B4A0, B4A6 has another reader (grep, read). Because B44E is never below the full-load air estimate, the transmitted value is the torque the engine could make at full load (or the actual load if higher): a maximum-available-torque signal for other modules (inferred). It does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost in this ECU. Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate
table.description:
How fast, by rpm, the engine torque reported over CAN to other modules (for example stability control) fades out at a fuel cut and returns after it. It does not change fuelling or throttle. Stock slow at low rpm, instant at 8000 rpm.
Details: When used: always while running, 10 ms (0x10ED6C from 0x111AB8, task 0x1DFE3C, read). Axis FFF8CE9C (rpm; the function's param_1, read). A weight w = FFF854FC moves toward 0 while the cylinder fuel cut FFF8A64C bit 0 is set and toward 0xFF00 otherwise, by (target - w) x this/255 per pass (read). The DAM-blended engine torque FFF8B48A (= DAM x B490/16 + (16 - DAM) x B4A2/16, DAM FFF811AE) is scaled by w/0xFF00 about the 16000 zero point (B48E, read), and FFF8B404 = (that - 16000 - (05D3E4(rpm, FFF88AE6) + FFF8B46E + FFF8AF62 - 48000))/8 + 10000, i.e. faded torque minus loss terms in 10000 + 10 x Nm (read). FFF8B404 is packed into the engine CAN TX frames (0x08B1B6 / 0x08C220, bytes FFF8CC91/92) and is the 'actual torque' of the VDC torque-request loop 0x117778 (VDC Torque Request Correction); B48E and A8F0 (= w >> 8) have no readers (ram_xref, read). So this only shapes how fast the torque reported to the other control units falls at a fuel cut and returns after it; it does not change fuelling or the throttle directly. Stock 0.16 per pass at <= 800 rpm, 0.40 at 2000, 0.80 at 4000, 1.0 (instant) at 8000 rpm. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts MAF sensor voltage to airflow (g/s) in 64 fixed steps from 0 to 4.92 V; this airflow drives the ECU's air model, load and fuel. Rescale every point when fitting a bigger intake or a different MAF, and keep peak flow below the P0103 voltage limit (stock 4.79 V). An internal 218 g/s cap on one copy of the airflow affects only purge, TGV, monitors and similar side functions, not fuel, load or timing.
Details: When used: always (4 ms task prefix 0x1E2CB4, read). ADC channel 2 (0xFFFFE844) -> FFF8C990 (10-bit) x ADC trim FFF82038 / 32768, capped at 1023, x 64 -> FFF8CA48 -> FFF88A1A (0x1D87C8, read). FFF82038 is a per-unit gain trim copied at start from a stored data block (FFF81050, 0x1CF324) and used only within 125/128...131/128, else 1.0 (cals 0x28BA2 / 0x28BA3 / 0x28BA0, read); 65536 = 5 V (inferred). 0x06CA98 subtracts a start-up correction (only while FFF88CE5 is set) and floors at MAF Sensor Voltage Floor -> FFF88CFA; 0x06C9F8 looks up FFF88CFA >> 2 in this 64-point u32 table (boot routine 0x68EC: index = input / 256 with linear interpolation, input capped at 0x3F00, so above 4.92 V the last point holds) -> FFF8921C -> FFF88820 (the cal 0x57585 bit 7 filter is off in stock). g/s = value / 76800 (OBD PID 0x10 chain, read). The axis is implicit: point n is at n x 0.078125 V (0...4.92 V). FFF88820 feeds the manifold/airflow model 0x11D704 / 0x11D4E4, which the load and fuel calculations use, and the torque model 0x0C3E34 (read). Stock 1.4 g/s up to 0.47 V, 312.6 g/s at 4.77 V, 355.3 g/s at 4.92 V. For a bigger housing or another MAF, rescale every point to the new g/s at that voltage and keep peak flow below MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (stock 4.79 V = 318 g/s on the stock curve; P0103 after 13 passes). Limits elsewhere (read): the scan-tool/OBD MAF value FFF88A4A saturates at 300 g/s, and FFF8B4D6, a u16 copy of the model's air quantity (g/s x 300), saturates at 218 g/s (0x11DEE0). That 218 g/s cap does not limit fuel, load, ignition or boost. The base fuel quantity (0x0B8030) and engine load (0x0B7EFC) are computed from the unsaturated cylinder flow FFF8C250, and no ignition routine reads FFF8B4D6. Its readers are: the evap purge module (0x0D4C14, 0x0D4E78: purge flow = purge rate x air) and the evap monitor 0x18C3B0; TGV request logic and TGV transition fuel (0x10D93C, 0x0CA144); the EGR fresh-air option (0x0FA7C4, off in stock); the torque model's air-path lag lookup (0x0C34F8, axis ends at 208 g/s); the exhaust temperature model's filter and fuel-cut terms (0x0C9878, axis ends at 210 g/s); catalyst/rear-O2 heater energy and OBD monitor enables (0x101CF0, 0x134374, 0x1B3280, 0x1B3A48, 0x1259EC, 0x09FE44); charging control (0x136CD8, 0x13741C); the 'air since start' sum 0x10A270; and the CAN full-load air estimate 0x110444. All of these use thresholds far below 218 g/s, or axes whose last breakpoint is below it. The only one that can still change above 218 g/s is the CAN estimate, which takes the larger of FFF8B4D6 and its own value (inferred: little effect). The limits that matter at high airflow are the 4.92 V end of this table, MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit, the 256 % (3.31 g/rev) ceiling of engine load (0x0B7EFC) and Base Fuel Quantity Limit; the model's cylinder flow FFF8C250 itself does not saturate. Identical in both images. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Multiplier
table.description:
Gain of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt (stock 63 kPa per volt). For a 3-bar or larger sensor set it to the new sensor's slope and set MAP Sensor Offset to match. The ECU's MAP value cannot go above 256 kPa absolute (about 22 psi boost at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted, so anything higher reads as 256 kPa.
Details: When used: always (2 ms task prefix 0x1E2AA2; also 0x1E220A / 0x1E4D00 at start-up, read). MAP (kPa x 256) = ADC channel 18 sample FFF88D3A (16-bit left-justified 10-bit value, not corrected by the ADC trim FFF82038) x this >> 8 + MAP Sensor Offset, limited to 0...65535 (0x6E00, read) -> FFF8913C, the MAP the engine uses (-> FFF88A34 -> FFF88666; FFF8869C for the airflow model) and FFF89040 / FFF89A32 (OBD MAP). FFF89140 = the same minus 0xD4C (13.3 kPa), limited the same way, is the boost-control pressure FFF88FF4. With 65536 = 5 V (inferred) the unit is kPa per volt = value / 5: stock 315 = 63 kPa/V, so with the stock offset 0.5 V = 7.9 kPa and 4.5 V = 259.9 kPa. Hard limit (read): the MAP value cannot exceed 255.99 kPa absolute (about 22.3 psi gauge at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted; with stock scaling that is reached at 4.44 V, and the boost-control copy saturates at 269.3 kPa actual MAP. To fit a different (e.g. 3-bar) sensor: this = sensor slope in kPa per V x 5, and MAP Sensor Offset = sensor kPa at 0 V x 256; example 0.5 V = 20 kPa, 4.5 V = 300 kPa -> 70 kPa/V -> 350, offset -15 kPa -> -3840. Readings above 256 kPa are still clipped. Range faults use raw voltage: P0107 below MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0108 above MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit; while the MAP fault flag FFF88E28 bit 3 is set MAP = cal 0x58EA4 x FFF8ADF0 / 32768 instead (read). The TMAP's temperature element is probably Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 (change that table too if the new sensor's thermistor differs). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: MAP Sensor Offset
table.description:
Offset of the manifold pressure sensor conversion (stock -23.6 kPa), i.e. the sensor's reading extrapolated to 0 V. Set it together with MAP Sensor Multiplier when fitting a different MAP sensor. The result is still limited to 256 kPa absolute.
Details: When used: always (2 ms task prefix 0x1E2AA2, read): offset of the MAP conversion in kPa x 256, added to sample x MAP Sensor Multiplier >> 8 before the result is limited to 0...65535 (255.99 kPa). Equals the sensor's (extrapolated) reading at 0 V. Stock -6048 = -23.6 kPa. For a different sensor: offset = kPa at 0 V x 256 = (kPa at V1 - slope x V1) x 256; example 0.5 V = 20 kPa, 4.5 V = 300 kPa -> -15 kPa -> -3840. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Floor
table.description:
Lowest value the corrected MAF voltage may reach after the ECU subtracts its post-start MAF correction (a decaying start-up offset); it applies at all times after the first pass. Stock 0.4 V. Normally leave alone.
Details: Lower limit of the dynamically corrected MAF voltage FFF88CFA (0x06CA98, read). The correction (voltage minus a gain x rate term, cal 0x5758E/0x57590/0x57587) only runs while FFF88CE5 is set. Stock 0.4 V. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0107)
table.description:
Sensor voltage below which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted low (P0107) and a substitute MAP is used. It works on raw voltage, so it does not change when you rescale the MAP sensor. Stock 0.36 V.
Details: When used: always while the monitor is enabled (FFF88E66 bit 1, FFF89183 = 0). 0x06FC80 (read): P0107 (FFF89B0B bit 2, record slot of P0107) is set when the MAP sensor sample FFF88D3A (ADC channel 18, 16-bit left-justified, not trimmed) stays below this for cal 0x56702 (200) passes; while set the ECU replaces MAP by cal 0x58EA4 x FFF8ADF0 / 32768 (fault flag FFF88E28 bit 3, read in 0x1E2AA2). It compares raw voltage, so it does not move when MAP Sensor Multiplier / Offset are changed. Stock 4697 = 0.358 V (with stock scaling -1.0 kPa). A replacement sensor whose lowest output (engine-off vacuum is not reached, so the lowest is about 20-30 kPa) is above this needs no change. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0108)
table.description:
Sensor voltage above which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted high (P0108). Raw voltage, independent of the MAP scaling. Stock 4.84 V.
Details: When used: always while the monitor is enabled (FFF88E66 bit 1, FFF89183 = 0). 0x06FC80 (read): P0108 (FFF89B0B bit 1) is set when the MAP sensor sample FFF88D3A stays above this for cal 0x56703 (200) passes; the substitute MAP is then used (FFF88E28 bit 3). Raw voltage, independent of MAP Sensor Multiplier / Offset. Stock 63499 = 4.845 V. Note the MAP value itself is limited to 255.99 kPa (see MAP Sensor Multiplier) whatever the voltage. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0102)
table.description:
MAF voltage below which the MAF circuit-low code P0102 is set. Stock 0.12 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: with the ignition/run input on (FFF8A297 bit 1) for at least cal 0x5700D (26) passes and FFF88E66 bit 1 set. 0x070048 (read): P0102 (FFF89AFC bit 6) is set when the MAF voltage FFF88D48 (ADC channel 2 sample x 64, before the ADC trim and before the start-up correction) has been below this for cal 0x57007 (13) passes, cleared after cal 0x57008 (13) passes above. Stock 1587 = 0.121 V. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0103)
table.description:
MAF voltage above which the MAF circuit-high code P0103 is set. Stock 4.79 V, about 318 g/s on the stock MAF curve; with a larger intake keep peak flow below this voltage.
Details: When used: with the ignition/run input on (FFF8A297 bit 1) for at least cal 0x57009 (26) passes and FFF88E66 bit 1 set. 0x06FF70 (read): P0103 (FFF89AFC bit 5) is set when the MAF voltage FFF88D48 (ADC channel 2 x 64, untrimmed) has been above this for cal 0x57007 (13) passes, cleared after cal 0x57008 (13) passes below. Stock 62760 = 4.788 V, which on the stock MAF Sensor Scaling is 318 g/s. With a larger MAF housing make sure peak flow stays below this voltage (the scaling table itself stops at 4.92 V); raising it towards 4.9 V is possible but leaves less margin to detect a shorted signal (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
table.description:
Voltage below which the main IAT sensor is flagged as shorted (reads impossibly hot, P0112). Stock 0.22 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89185 = 0. 0x070310 (read): P0112 (IAT circuit low, FFF89AFD bit 6) is set when the IAT sensor voltage FFF88D38 (ADC channel 19 x 64, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x566F0 (13) passes. Low voltage = very hot reading (NTC). Stock 2927 = 0.223 V (about 170 C on the stock curve). While the IAT is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the ECU looks up the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 174 = 3.40 V, about 20 C) instead (0x06AF58, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0113)
table.description:
Voltage above which the main IAT sensor is flagged as open (reads impossibly cold, P0113). Stock 4.72 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89185 = 0. 0x0702A8 (read): P0113 (IAT circuit high, FFF89AFD bit 5) is set when the IAT sensor voltage FFF88D38 (ADC channel 19) is above this for cal 0x566F1 (13) passes. High voltage = open circuit / very cold. Stock 61815 = 4.716 V (about -43 C on the stock curve). Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
table.description:
Voltage below which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0097). Stock 0.22 V; check it if a replacement TMAP sensor has a different thermistor.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89188 = 0. 0x0703D4 (read): P0097 (IAT sensor 2 circuit low, FFF89B17 bit 0) is set when the IAT 2 sensor voltage FFF88D40 (ADC channel 20 x 64, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x57014 (13) passes. While IAT 2 is faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 174 = 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used (0x06B304, read). Stock 2927 = 0.223 V. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
table.description:
Voltage above which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0098). Stock 4.72 V; check it if a replacement TMAP sensor has a different thermistor.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89188 = 0. 0x070378 (read): P0098 (IAT sensor 2 circuit high, FFF89B17 bit 1) is set when the IAT 2 sensor voltage FFF88D40 (ADC channel 20) is above this for cal 0x57010 (13) passes. Stock 61815 = 4.716 V. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0117)
table.description:
Voltage below which the coolant sensor is flagged as shorted (P0117). Stock 0.33 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8918B = 0. 0x070520 (read): P0117 (FFF89AFC bit 1) is set when the coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (multiplexed ADC channel 21, input 0, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x566F2 (13) passes. Stock 4291 = 0.327 V (about 141 C on the stock curve). While the coolant sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) the coolant value follows a warm-up model instead (cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2, 0x06BA46, read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
table.description:
Voltage above which the coolant sensor is flagged as open (P0118). Stock 4.71 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8918B = 0. 0x0704B8 (read): P0118 (FFF89AFC bit 0) is set when the coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E is above this for cal 0x566F3 (13) passes. Stock 61769 = 4.713 V (about -42 C). Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
table.description:
Voltage below which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0197). Stock 0.18 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8919F = 0. 0x0705E4 (read): P0197 (FFF89B1D bit 6) is set when the oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (multiplexed ADC channel 21, input 7, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x5703A (13) passes. Stock 2411 = 0.184 V. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)
table.description:
Voltage above which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0198). Stock 4.71 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8919F = 0. 0x070588 (read): P0198 (FFF89B1D bit 7) is set when the oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 is above this for cal 0x57037 (13) passes. Stock 61769 = 4.713 V. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
table.description:
Rail pressure sensor voltage below which P0192 (circuit low) is set. Stock 0.23 V; change only with a different sensor.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF891D1 = 0. 0x06FDF8 (read): P0192 (FFF89B17 bit 6) is set when the rail pressure sensor sample FFF88D44 (ADC channel 17, 16-bit, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x56710 (250) passes. Stock 3044 = 0.232 V (below the sensor's 0.5 V zero point). Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0193)
table.description:
Rail pressure sensor voltage above which P0193 (circuit high) is set. Stock 3.25 V, which is about 20.6 MPa (2990 psi) with the stock sensor, a pressure the stock system should never reach.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF891D1 = 0. 0x06FDF8 (read): P0193 (FFF89B17 bit 7) is set when the rail pressure sensor sample FFF88D44 is above this for cal 0x56711 (250) passes. Stock 42647 = 3.254 V, which with the stock sensor conversion is 20.6 MPa (2990 psi): a reading the pump should never produce, so it is treated as a circuit fault (inferred). Raise it only together with a sensor or pump change. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Zero-Pressure Voltage
table.description:
Rail pressure sensor voltage that reads as zero pressure. Stock 0.50 V. Change it with Rail Pressure Sensor Gain only when fitting a different rail pressure sensor.
Details: When used: always (0x06D43A, read). Rail pressure FFF88F82 = Rail Pressure Sensor Gain x max(0, FFF88AAA - this) / 2, where FFF88AAA is the 10-bit sample of ADC channel 17 (FFF88D44 >> 6, 2 ms task 0x1E2AA2); the result is limited to Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum and becomes FFF88AAC and (filtered when FFF8A29C bit 0 is set) FFF88886, the rail pressure used by injection, the HPFP and the rail-pressure DTCs (read). Stock 102 = 0.498 V: the stock sensor reads 0 MPa at 0.5 V (inferred). For a different rail pressure sensor set this to its zero-pressure output. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Gain
table.description:
Slope of the rail pressure sensor conversion. Stock about 1087 psi (7.5 MPa) per volt, so the stock sensor spans 0 at 0.5 V to about 4350 psi (30 MPa) at 4.5 V. Change it only for a different rail pressure sensor.
Details: When used: always (0x06D43A, read; a byte, read with MOVU.B). Rail pressure counts per 10-bit ADC count = this / 2 (counts of 0.61 kPa, 1639.34 per MPa). Stock 120 = 7.50 MPa (1087 psi) per volt, so the stock sensor spans 0 MPa at 0.5 V to 30.0 MPa at 4.5 V (inferred from the arithmetic and Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum = 30.0 MPa). For a different sensor: this = sensor MPa per V / 0.062464. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Maximum
table.description:
Highest rail pressure the sensor conversion can report. Stock 30 MPa (about 4350 psi), the full span of the stock sensor.
Details: When used: always (0x06D43A, read): the converted rail pressure is limited to this (unsigned min, 0x753C) before it becomes FFF88AAC / FFF88886. Stock 49180 = 30.0 MPa (4351 psi), the full span of the stock sensor (inferred). Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Fault Value
table.description:
Rail pressure the ECU assumes while the rail pressure sensor is faulted. Stock about 51 psi (0.35 MPa). Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E2C bit 2 or FFF88EDA bit 7 is set (rail pressure sensor fault, inferred from the flags' use) the converted rail pressure is replaced by this (0x06D43A, read). Stock 574 = 0.35 MPa (51 psi). Normally leave alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Multiplier
table.description:
Gain of the ECU's barometric pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt. Stock 22.2 kPa per volt. This sensor is probably inside the ECU; leave alone.
Details: When used: always (0x1D886A, read). Barometric pressure FFF8D060 (kPa x 256) = filtered sample FFF8D062 x this >> 8 + Barometric Sensor Offset, limited to 0...65535; FFF8D062 is a 3:1 running average of multiplexer channel 3 of ADC channel 12 (FFF8CA32, untrimmed). With 65536 = 5 V (inferred) the unit is kPa per volt = value / 5. Stock 111 = 22.2 kPa/V, so 101.3 kPa reads at 4.08 V. FFF8D060 -> FFF8CE60 -> FFF88668 (rate-limited by cals 0x1D0B2 / 0x1D0B4 = 34 per pass), the barometric pressure every baro table and gauge-pressure conversion uses (read). The sensor is not one of the externally wired inputs (inferred: no harness connector was identified); normally leave alone. Confidence: read.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Offset
table.description:
Offset of the barometric pressure sensor conversion. Stock 10.8 kPa. Leave alone.
Details: When used: always (0x1D886A, read): offset of the barometric pressure conversion in kPa x 256 (see Barometric Sensor Multiplier). Stock 2767 = 10.8 kPa. While the barometric sensor fault flag FFF88E2A bit 0 is set (passed to the driver as FFF8CA4C bit 7 by 0x1D766E, read) FFF8D060 is forced to 0x654C = 101.3 kPa. Confidence: read.

table.name: Barometric Sensor Enable
table.description:
When set (stock), the ECU uses its barometric pressure sensor. When cleared, it assumes sea-level pressure (101.3 kPa) everywhere, so altitude compensation stops working.
Details: When used: always. 0x06AA54 (via 0x06B66A, read): with this bit set the barometric pressure FFF88668 follows the sensor value FFF8CE60 (rate-limited by cals 0x1D0B2 / 0x1D0B4); with it clear FFF88668 is fixed at 0x654C = 101.3 kPa and FFF886DE / FFF886DA are not updated (0x1E220A, 0x06B650, read). Stock set (0x80). Clearing it makes every baro compensation assume sea level. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure High Limit
table.description:
Fuel rail pressure limit for P0088 (rail pressure too high): the code trips when actual pressure exceeds this value plus a 2.5 MPa hysteresis for about 2 seconds (17.5 MPa in stock), and also triggers fail-safe; after a trip, pressure must drop back to this value to recover. Stock 15.0 MPa. If you raise target rail pressure, keep peak actual pressure below this plus 2.5 MPa.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read): the absolute high-pressure test fails while actual FFF88884 > this + hysteresis cal 0x574DE (4098 = 2.5 MPa; the hysteresis widens the limit while the test is in its normal state, 0x6C4C) for cal 0x574E2 (200) passes, and recovers only when actual <= this; it sets FFF89BDE bit 2 -> P0088 and the fail-safe flag FFF88EDA bit 6 (0x080B96). Stock 24590 = 15.0 MPa, so the effective trip point is 17.5 MPa (28688 counts) and recovery is at 15.0 MPa. If you raise target rail pressure, keep peak actual pressure below this + 2.5 MPa, and keep this above the normal operating pressure so a tripped test can recover. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0087 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description:
How far actual rail pressure may fall below target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0087 sets, after about 10 seconds. Stock 3.3 MPa. Raising it makes the code harder to set.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read): in HPFP state FFF8AB35 = 3, target - actual > this for cal 0x574E6 (1000) passes sets P0087 (FFF89BDE bit 7 via bit 1); outside state 3 the limit is cal 0x577BA (65535 = off). Stock 5410 = 3.3 MPa. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: P0088 Rail Pressure Deviation Limit
table.description:
How far actual rail pressure may rise above target (in normal high-pressure pump operation) before P0088 sets, after about 10 seconds. Stock 6.0 MPa. Raising it makes the code harder to set.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read): in HPFP state 3, actual - target > this for cal 0x574E8 (1000) passes sets P0088 (FFF89BDE bit 6 via bit 0); otherwise cal 0x577BC (off). Stock 9836 = 6.0 MPa. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. Confidence: read.

table.name: Cold Start Timing Monitor Band (Coolant)
table.description:
Diagnostic threshold, not a tuning table: how far final timing may exceed the cold-start spark target, by coolant, before the P050B cold-start timing monitor counts a fault. One entry edits all three copies. Stock 8 degrees up to 75 C (167 F), no check (63.5) from 80 C (176 F).
Details: When used: one data block (0x04B0B2) read through three descriptors: 05B428, 0607FC and 060808 - this entry edits all three. (1) P050B cold-start timing monitor (0x1CB088 group): 0x1CB66C counts the passes where final timing FFF8A744 minus the active spark target FFF8A647 exceeds this (coolant FFF88A44), and 0x1CB6BC the passes where it does not, while the monitor runs (FFF8ADE2 bit 0) (read); see my research notes. (2) 0x0D8FC8: in the scan-tool mode set by UDS 0x2E DID 0x2004 (FFF89042 = 0xF0..0xF5, written by 0x0B0E6C, read) FFF8A729 = this + 0..10, added to the alternate timing path of 0x0D9E40 (read). Stock 16 = 8 degrees up to 167 F (75 C), 127 = 63.5 degrees (no check) from 176 F (80 C). Diagnostic, not a tuning table. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1
table.description:
First reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor: how much the front A/F sensor reading may swing, by rpm and load, over the 25-second test window. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. A fault also needs A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 to be exceeded. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.
Details: P219A also needs the crank-roughness confirmation: the channel judgements 0x18F980 / 0x18F928 report "exceeded" only when this reference is exceeded and the roughness latch from A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 / 2 (05FC7C / 05FCDC) is set (read, Phase 19). When used: while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACCE bits 0 and 1). A/F imbalance monitor 0x18FF34 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C) sets P219A (result FFF8ACCF bit 0, DTC monitor record slot 623, read). Over a window of cal 0x436D4 = 2500 passes (25 s) while its conditions FFF8ACCE bits 0/1 hold it sums the A/F-sensor swings, |change| of lambda x 8192 FFF88AF8 over each rising and falling run (FFF8C4E8, 0x18DB0C / 0x18DCCC, read), and two references: FFF8C4EC from 05FC10 and FFF8C4F0 from 05FC3C (0x18DD78 / 0x18DE88: per pass + table(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616) x 05FC24/32 x 05FC30/16, both 1.0 in stock). At the window end measured > reference x coolant factor (05FD58/05FD70, 1.0 in stock) gives FFF8ACCE bit 4 / bit 2 (0x1913E0 / 0x19154C), judgements FFF8ACCB / FFF8ACCA = 2 and FFF8ACCF bit 1 / bit 3; either of these sets the P219A result in 0x19198C (read). This is the first reference (judgement FFF8ACCB, enabled by cal 0x436C0 = 1). Raising it makes P219A harder to set. Stock 12-67 per pass (0.0015-0.008 lambda) at 1500 rpm, up to 291 (0.036) at 2500-4000 rpm and 2.07 g/rev (160 % load); 65536168 from 4500 rpm (the sum saturates, so no failure can be found there). Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2
table.description:
Second, higher reference for the P219A (A/F imbalance) monitor, used with A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2 as confirmation. Raising it makes P219A harder to set. Above about 4000 rpm the reference climbs steeply (interpolating to the 4500 rpm row, which is effectively infinite), so running above about 4000 rpm during the window stops the test from failing.
Details: P219A also needs the crank-roughness confirmation: the channel judgements 0x18F980 / 0x18F928 report "exceeded" only when this reference is exceeded and the roughness latch from A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1 / 2 (05FC7C / 05FCDC) is set (read, Phase 19). When used: while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACCE bits 0 and 1). A/F imbalance monitor 0x18FF34 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C) sets P219A (result FFF8ACCF bit 0, DTC monitor record slot 623, read). Over a window of cal 0x436D4 = 2500 passes (25 s) while its conditions FFF8ACCE bits 0/1 hold it sums the A/F-sensor swings, |change| of lambda x 8192 FFF88AF8 over each rising and falling run (FFF8C4E8, 0x18DB0C / 0x18DCCC, read), and two references: FFF8C4EC from 05FC10 and FFF8C4F0 from 05FC3C (0x18DD78 / 0x18DE88: per pass + table(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616) x 05FC24/32 x 05FC30/16, both 1.0 in stock). At the window end measured > reference x coolant factor (05FD58/05FD70, 1.0 in stock) gives FFF8ACCE bit 4 / bit 2 (0x1913E0 / 0x19154C), judgements FFF8ACCB / FFF8ACCA = 2 and FFF8ACCF bit 1 / bit 3; either of these sets the P219A result in 0x19198C (read). This is the second reference (judgement FFF8ACCA, enabled by cal 0x436C1 = 1); it is higher than Threshold 1 and its judgement additionally needs FFF8ACD6 / FFF8ACDB (FFF8ACDB = the crank-roughness latch of A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2, 0x191920; FFF8ACD6 not decoded) instead of FFF8ACD4 / FFF8ACD8. Stock 40-200 per pass at 1500 rpm, up to 511 (0.062 lambda) at 2500 rpm / 2.07 g/rev (160 % load); 65536168 from 4500 rpm. Confidence: read.

table.name: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT
table.description:
Tells the ECU whether it is in a manual or an AT/CVT car (clear = manual in every manual image). It decides gear calculation, the gear torque limits and whether the AT/CVT Coding table variants are used. Do not change on a manual car.
Details: Clear in every manual image (byte 0xFD) and set in the 2016 CVT image LF75300G (0xFB) (read, my research notes). While Transmission Coding: From Input Port is clear, FFF886AB bit 7 (manual coding) = NOT this bit (read, 0x06A38C at 0x06A73A..0x06A824). The bit is also read directly, whatever From Input Port says, by 0x0B83F8 (0x0B8544 / 0x0B8514 -> FFF8A618 bits 0/1 -> 0x0B8154, read; meaning not identified). With the manual coding: gear is computed from the rpm/speed ratio (0x0B914C), Requested Torque uses its A tables only, the gear torque limit table applies (0x0BB1AC), and the flag-set table variants are the live ones; with automatic/CVT coding the gear and a torque limit come from a received CAN frame and the AT/CVT Coding table variants are used (read; meaning inferred). Do not change on a manual car. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 1 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 1's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D168C writes FFF8C060 = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1E4 (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. Descriptor 05B1FC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 2
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 2 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 2's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D1848 writes FFF8C064 = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1E6 (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. Descriptor 05B210. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 3
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 3 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 3's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D1A04 writes FFF8C068 = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1E8 (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. Descriptor 05B224. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 4
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 4 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 4's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D1BC0 writes FFF8C06C = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1EA (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. Descriptor 05B238. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Strategy byte = injections per cycle (FFF8A69E, 0x0CF3EC, read): this one applies with one injection (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6A3 by 0x0CF630 (read). Injector 1's quantity (0x0D168C) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A69F equals 1 (read). The strategy byte is probably the number of injections per cycle (inferred from the split-injection code). All 128 (x1.0) in stock. Descriptor 05ADE8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 2 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 2 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Applies with one injection per cycle (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6A6 by 0x0CF684 (read). Injector 2's quantity (0x0D1848) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A6A0 equals 1 (read). The strategy byte is probably the number of injections per cycle (inferred from the split-injection code). All 128 (x1.0) in stock. Descriptor 05AE24. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 3 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 3 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Applies with one injection per cycle (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6A9 by 0x0CF6D8 (read). Injector 3's quantity (0x0D1A04) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A6A1 equals 1 (read). The strategy byte is probably the number of injections per cycle (inferred from the split-injection code). All 128 (x1.0) in stock. Descriptor 05AE60. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 4 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 4 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Applies with one injection per cycle (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6AC by 0x0CF72C (read). Injector 4's quantity (0x0D1BC0) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A6A2 equals 1 (read). The strategy byte is probably the number of injections per cycle (inferred from the split-injection code). All 128 (x1.0) in stock. Descriptor 05AE9C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset
table.description:
Pressure offset added to measured rail pressure before looking up Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4), by rpm and load; probably the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor. Stock all 0 (no effect).
Details: 0x06D43A (read): FFF89222 = sat(rail pressure FFF88886 + this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616)), interpolated by 0x00671C (descriptor 0x0608E4: data, u16 axis, u8 axis, 16, 16; row = rpm, read). FFF89222 indexes the injector flow compensation 05A844 used only for injectors 2 and 4 (0x0CB0C8, read); injectors 1 and 3 use 05A838 with FFF88886. Likely the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor (inferred from the boxer layout). Signed, in the rail-pressure unit. Stock all 0 (2015, 2016). Descriptor boot 0608E4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 (an early warm-up phase); the one the stock car uses, since the fallback version never activates. Stock 15 MPa flat.
Details: When used: The combustion mode 1 target in stock (FFF899D7 bit 0 never sets, read). 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is clear. Stock 15 MPa flat. Descriptor 05EB4C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Catalyst Heating)
table.description:
Fixed rail pressure target during stratified catalyst heating (combustion mode 2). Stock 15 MPa.
Details: 0x165180 (read): fixed target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 2 (stratified catalyst heating). Stock 24590 = 15.0 MPa. Address 03F288. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target A
table.description:
Rail pressure target while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active; stock 0.35 MPa, which appears to mean no high-pressure pumping. No effect on a healthy car.
Details: 0x165180 (read): target while FFF88F4A bit 1 is set (injector-driver faults P062D / P2146, set by 0x080B96, read); if bit 2 is also set the lower of A and B is used. Stock 574 = 0.35 MPa, i.e. no high-pressure pumping (inferred). Address 03F50E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Fail-Safe Target B
table.description:
Second fail-safe rail pressure target; the lower of A and B is used when both apply. Nothing that activates it was found, so it probably never applies. Stock 0.35 MPa.
Details: 0x165180 (read): target while FFF88F4A bit 2 is set. No setter of that bit was found in either image. Stock 574 = 0.35 MPa. Address 03F50C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit

scaling.category: mg fuel per cylinder (stock Injector Scaling)
scaling.units: mg (stoich fuel per cylinder per cycle)

scaling.category: base pulse (0.3 MPa reference, any Injector Scaling)

table.description:
Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling: stock it allows about 5 g of air per revolution, but lowering the injector flow figure (for example for E85) lowers the ceiling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.
Details: When used: always while running (every pass of 0x0B7E00, which computes load and the base fuel quantity, read). Upper limit of the base (stoichiometric) fuel quantity FFF8ADEA. 0x0B8030 (read) computes FFF8ADEA = air quantity FFF8C250 x Injector Scaling x 0.10266 / 14.7 / 4 / rpm x 0.125 (= 0.5587 x Injector Scaling x air per cylinder per cycle in g) and stores min(that, this) (0x0B80FC-0x0B8112: MOVU.W @0x23696, CMP/GE, read). The limited value is what the rest of the fuel path uses: the base pulse 0x0D15EC (FFF8C05C = 16 x FFF8ADEA x trims), before the enrichment/fuel factor 0x0D1528 and the flow compensation and latency 0x0D2BB8; the transient-fuel film model 0x0F5F84; the fuel load FFF8ADEE (0x0B895C); and the fuel-used accumulators 0x06B70E (read). Above the limit the base pulse stops rising with airflow, so the mixture goes lean as air keeps rising; enrichment is applied on top of the limited value and does not lift it (inferred from the order of the calls). The raw unit includes Injector Scaling, so the limit in air terms moves with it: air per revolution at the limit = this x 3.580 / Injector Scaling (raw) g/rev = this x reference injector flow [g/s] x 0.0004704. Shown in g/rev for stock Injector Scaling 2918 (2.61 g/s). Stock 4060 = 4.98 g/rev (2.49 g per cylinder per cycle, about 556 g/s at 6700 rpm), well beyond the stock turbo. With Injector Scaling at 1.74 g/s (fuel added for E85 by lowering the flow figure) the limit drops to 3.32 g/rev; below about 1.73 g/s it falls under the 3.31 g/rev (256 %) ceiling of engine load FFF8ADE4 (0x0B7EFC, read) and becomes the first limit reached. When you raise Injector Scaling raw (lower reference flow), raise this in proportion: new = 4060 x new raw / 2918 keeps 4.98 g/rev (u16, up to 65535). table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear (stock; the first argument of 0x0CE854), the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128, both all zero in stock (read). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. Descriptor 05AC6C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description:
Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. Stock identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling; edit all five together. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.
Details: When used: whenever the open-loop delay has expired (see below); the blend follows TGV position and AVCS state. TGV-closed base, weight 1 - a (AVCS not in active control). 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear (stock): FFF8A681 = clamp(blend + Additive x DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128 - 05AC14 x 05AC3C(DAM)/128 (Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) x its DAM multiplier; both all zero in stock), 0, 255). With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). Stock: byte-identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling (05AC6C) and to the other three tables of this group (AFR 14.7 down to about 10.7 at high load); edit all five together. Descriptor 05ABB0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cranking Fuel Pedal Multiplier (Special Start, Off in Stock)

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used. Stock never uses multiple injections (the quantity windows are disabled), so it has no effect.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Stock never uses multiple injections: the Double/Triple Injection Quantity Windows are 65535 (read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. Descriptor 05AF94. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 2nd, Off in Stock)

Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the second pulse with two injections per cycle (0x0CB604, read). Unused in stock (windows 65535). table.name: Double Injection Split

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description:
Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC. Stock pinned at the late limit, about 170 degrees after TDC. Has no effect in stock: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share is 0, so the pulse gets no fuel.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC; negative = AFTER that TDC (expansion stroke). This angle is an offset in segment 0, the 180 degrees after firing TDC (0x0CB604 mode 3 uses it with segment 0; the pulse-fit check 0x075D84 places it B064 + 1440 after the first pulse B062, read), so it is shown as -offset/2: clamped to 0 to -179.5 (0x0D0468, read), and -170 to -179.5 act as -169.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock pins at the -179.5 clamp (stored -170 at spark 24 BTDC only): a late expansion-stroke pulse, about 170 degrees ATDC in effect (its quantity is Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share, cal 0x2A3CA, which is 0 in stock, so stock fires no second pulse in this mode). Catalyst-heating mode = FFF8A85C 2 (0x109B4C, read): it maps to fuel mode 3 (0x108B08), in which the ignition target is FFF8A76C (0x0DA51C, read) and the injection angle is FFF8B062 (0x0CB394, read). FFF8B064 = this(FFF8A76C), clamped to 0-359 (0x0D0468, read); used for the second injection's angle by 0x0CB604 (read). Descriptor 05B194. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal)
table.description:
Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 40 BTDC (100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with late spark); identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. Second pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 0.5-180 BTDC (code 1080-1439, 0x0D023C, read), i.e. the compression stroke; 0.5-10 BTDC act as 10.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock 40 BTDC, and 100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with the spark target at 7 degrees ATDC or later. When used: Selected by FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) in 0x0D023C: this one while it is clear (read). Stock identical to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Injection angle FFF8B060 from rpm and FFF8A76B (0x0D023C, read), the second-injection angle in fuel mode 2 (0x0CB604, read). Descriptor 05B130. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are closed. Stock identical to the TGV Normal table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. Second pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 0.5-180 BTDC (code 1080-1439, 0x0D023C, read). Stock as the TGV Normal table (40 / 100 BTDC). When used: Used while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set (0x0D023C, read). Alternate of Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal) (0x0D023C, read). Descriptor 05B144. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal)
table.description:
First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 270 BTDC cold to 290 BTDC hot; identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. First pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 180.5-360 BTDC (code 720-1079, 0x0D00A8, read), i.e. the intake stroke. Stock 270 BTDC cold to 290 BTDC hot, the same window as the main injection. When used: while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear. 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C, args read): in fuel state FFF8906B 2/3, FFF8B05E = this(rpm FFF8CD54, coolant FFF88A44) + 05B068(rpm, load) x 05B090(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + 05B0E0(spark FFF8A76B, coolant) (all three 0 or neutral in stock), clamped 720..1079; under FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 only this table; cal 0x38448 bit 5 (clear) would force cal 0x1208A. 0x0CB394 uses FFF8B05E - 720 as the injection angle of cylinders in injector mode 2 (fuel mode 2 = combustion modes 1 and 3, the catalyst-heating phase 2 / start sequence) (read). Axes 850-1600 rpm x coolant. Stock 900 cold to 860 hot, identical to the TGV Closed table. Descriptor 05B0B8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Closed)

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Rpm x load correction to the phase 2 first-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later. Stock all 0, no effect.
Details: When used: catalyst-heating phase 2 first pulse while the TGVs are closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 set); then it replaces the TGV Normal adder and 05B0A4 replaces the multiplier (0x0D00A8, read). 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, cal 0x38448 bit 5, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, coolant FFF88A44, spark target FFF8A76B, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B05E), read): in fuel states 2/3 FFF8B05E = Base(rpm, coolant) + Base Adder(rpm, load) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + Base Spark Adder(spark, coolant), clamped to code 720-1079 (180.5-360 BTDC); with FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 set only the Base is used (read). table.description:

Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Correction to the phase 2 second-pulse angle with the TGVs closed; positive = later. Stock all 0, no effect.
Details: When used: catalyst-heating phase 2 second pulse while the TGVs are closed (FFF8A881 bit 4); scaled by 05B16C/255. 0x0D023C (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, spark target FFF8A76B, rpm/50 FFF8CD56, cal 0x38448 bit 4, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, rpm FFF8CD54, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B060, &FFF8B00A), read): unless rpm > cal 0x1CBD8 (20480 = 4000 rpm), FFF8B060 = Phase 2 Injection Angle(rpm/50, spark) + this adder(rpm/50, spark) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 (adder skipped while FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5), clamped to code 1080-1439 (180-0.5 BTDC) in fuel states 2/3 (read).
