table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 2, Channel 2)
table.description:
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 2 of 8 (index 1 of FFF8CDB0; enabled in stock: bit 1 of cal 0x1B97D is clear), on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 4 to 97 (raw); the sibling tables for channels 1, 7 and 8 (masked in stock) are all 0. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 05BEAC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 066B04. Confidence: read.

Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed; identical to the TGV Open table in stock. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections), and in stock the target is far lower, so raising this map at idle or when coasting does nothing.
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. table.name: Boost Limit
table.description:
Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run. Stock 211 kPa absolute peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost.
Details: 0x1086F8 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A84F (raw) and FFF8A84E = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, where f is the target's baro/IAT factor: the compensated boost ceiling (read). The torque-model task 0x0C3D14 copies it to FFF8AFAE = A84E << 8 (0x0C3D0C, read). AFAE is the full-load manifold pressure of the throttle/torque model. Target MAP FFF8AF6A = (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this (0x0C2F0C). FFF8AF8A = Throttle Required Area column input AFA8 x this (0x0C3408). The pressure ratio AF6C = AF8A / this (0x0C2F9C) selects the high-pressure spark-compensation filter above 0.85 (all read). Also read by the airflow/torque model 0x111AB8 (role there not decoded). It is not an overboost cut; see Overboost Limit for that. Stock 211 kPa abs peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost. Raise it with Target Boost. Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per step everywhere, i.e. no Stage 1 limit.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding; unused in stock (manual coding). AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock, 255 = x1) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Stock 24000 everywhere = 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per 10 ms, i.e. no Stage 1 limit (same as the high-gear cells of the Stage 2 AT/CVT Coding tables). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 0598BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 063D5C. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEDE by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BAFA8->0x0CAAF0 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); 0x0BE140->0x0CDBF8 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); 0x186F0C->0x18C4A0 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); 0x18ACB8->0x18FCDC (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEDE (4 reference(s), votes {'023C0E': 4}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x023C0E is accessed as u16. Stock 34304 (LF75404S 34304). Matches the layout address. Address 023C0E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Reset RPM
table.description:
End of the rev-limit state: the throttle cap stays until rpm falls to this and boost is below Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP, while fuel already returns at Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM. Keep it about 100 rpm below Rev Limit RPM. Stock 6600 rpm.
Details: When used: always. Release rpm of the rev latch (part 1): once Rev Limit RPM is exceeded, state 0x0B (and its throttle cap) stays until rpm <= this and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The fuel cut itself ends at Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, so in stock fuel returns at 6,700 rpm and only the throttle cap lasts down to 6,600 rpm. Keep it below Rev Limit RPM. Stock 33792 = 6,600 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEE0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0CDBF8 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE0 (1 reference(s), votes {'023C10': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x023C10 is accessed as u16. Stock 33792 (LF75404S 33792). Matches the layout address. Address 023C10. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP
table.description:
The rev-limit fuel cut and state cannot end while manifold pressure is at or above this, even below their reset rpm. Stock 168 kPa absolute (about 9.7 psi). Raise it if you want the cut to release on rpm alone at high boost.
Details: When used: always. Neither the rev latch (part 1) nor the full-cut latch (part 2) releases while MAP FFF88FF4 is at or above this, even below its reset rpm, so at high boost the fuel cut lasts until the closed throttle has pulled the manifold below it. Stock 39603 = 168 kPa abs (about 9.7 psi gauge). At 65535 the release depends on rpm only (read: the test is MAP < this). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEF2 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BAE98->0x0CAA08 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); 0x0BE140->0x0CDBF8 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEF2 (2 reference(s), votes {'023C22': 2}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x023C22 is accessed as u16. Stock 39603 (LF75404S 39603). Matches the layout address. Address 023C22. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:
Overboost limit by rpm, compensated for baro and intake temperature like the boost target. Boost 26.7 kPa over it for 2 s sets the overboost flag, and 33 kPa over it starts the overboost cut (throttle cap, then a full fuel cut once the flag is set). Raise it when raising boost targets (stock 211 kPa absolute peak). Note: the boost-control pressure reading stops at about 269 kPa absolute, so an Overboost Limit above about 236 kPa absolute (269 minus the 33 kPa cut margin) can never trigger the overboost cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768 (read; cal 0x290A8 = 1 would use a fixed value, 0 in stock). Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. The flag makes the state-0x0B cut a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Rev Limit RPM); on its own, outside state 0x0B, it reduces nothing. It also feeds a diagnostic 0x1B8310. Stock 211 kPa abs peak, the same as Boost Limit from 2,000 rpm. Raise it with Target Boost. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 05CFD4 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 116C84, see Boost Limit. Descriptor 067CDC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP

(5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Evidence: 0x0B.. limit-state function: the stage-1 limit is the first constant, replaced by the reset constant while the stage-1 flag (FFF840CB) is set, and the reset constant is the default of the next comparison; LF75404S uses Stage 1 Pressure / Reset Pressure in exactly those places. table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description:
Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables). Set in stock; cleared, the limiter is probably fuel-cut only.
Details: Set in stock. With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). Cleared, the rev limiter and the overboost cut become fuel-only: no throttle closing during the cut (inferred). LF79002P: located from LF75404S 023CEA by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 029FAA bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this. Stock 0 kPa.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. The flag forces the zero torque cap in the overboost/rev cut state (0x0BAE98 -> FFF8AE8A, applied in limit state 0x0B; Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) and also feeds 0x1B8310 (0x1B828C / 0x1B83CC, the overboost diagnostic, inferred in my research notes), so this margin also sets how long that monitor sees overboost. Stock 0. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEF6 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 023C26. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:
Boost above Overboost Limit plus this enters the overboost cut state: the throttle is capped at once, and fuel to all cylinders is cut only if the 2-second overboost flag is also set. Stock 33 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Overboost latch FFF84167 (0x0BE140, read): sets when MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit (the baro/IAT-compensated FFF8A851) + this, and releases when MAP < that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). While set (and no higher state) the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0B, the same state as the rev limiter (see Rev Limit RPM). In that state the throttle-side request is capped at once (Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base) by rpm, or the stage tables above 256 kPa abs); fuel is cut on all four cylinders every event only once the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 is also set (MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay, 2.0 s stock) or rpm reaches Rev Limit Full Cut RPM; spark is not retarded. When MAP falls below the release level the state ends and fuel returns even if the flag is still set (inferred from the state gating, read). Stock 8448 = 33 kPa, about 244 kPa abs at the 211 kPa stock limit peak. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEE6 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0CDBF8 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE6 (1 reference(s), votes {'023C16': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x023C16 is accessed as u16. Stock 8448 (LF75404S 8448). Matches the layout address. Address 023C16. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)
table.description:
How far boost must fall below the overboost cut level before the overboost cut state ends. Stock 15 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Subtracted from the overboost latch level while the latch FFF84167 is set (0x0BE208-0x0BE222, read): the overboost cut state 0x0B releases when MAP FFF88FF4 < Overboost Limit + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) - this. See Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) for what the state does. Stock 3840 = 15 kPa, so the state releases 18 kPa above the Overboost Limit. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEE8 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0CDBF8 (ref 2 access(es), target 2, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE8 (2 reference(s), votes {'023C18': 2}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x023C18 is accessed as u16. Stock 3840 (LF75404S 3840). Matches the layout address. Address 023C18. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:
Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing. Stock 255 km/h (no effect in stock).
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed latch, see Vehicle Speed Limit). 0x0C058C (read): latch FFF84188 sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this (minus Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis while above it) and holds until speed is below and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP; while set, FFF8AF1A = zero torque, which in state 0x0C cuts fuel on all four cylinders every event (0x0B9DC8, 0x0C1AC8). Without it state 0x0C reduces nothing. Stock 255 km/h (off). LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEF9 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 023C29. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold
table.description:
Vehicle speed above which the rev-limit fuel cut uses the Stage 1 / Stage 2 rpm values instead of the Full Cut pair. Stock 255 km/h can never be exceeded, so no effect in stock.
Details: When used: always, but stock never switches. Vehicle speed FFF99835 (km/h, a byte) above which the full-cut latch (part 2) uses Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) instead of Rev Limit Full Cut RPM / Reset RPM. Once at or below it, the speed must exceed this + Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis (saturating at 255) to switch (0x0BAEE2-0x0BAF0E). Stock 255 = never (the speed byte cannot exceed 255). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01DEEA by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: the counterpart of LF75404S 0x0BAE98, 0x0C0000-segment overrev function (seg_0x0C0000.c:7389): speed threshold 023C1A (+ hysteresis 023C1B), and while at or below it the set/reset rpm 023B5C / 023B5A (read); same structure as the reference. Address 023C1A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the vehicle-speed limiter. Set in stock; leave it set.
Details: Set in stock. Same as Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut for limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed limiter) (0x0DD568, read). Bits 5 and 4 do the same for states 0x19 and 0x1A (not decoded); state 0x1B always uses the normal target. Leave set. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 0239AE by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 029C6E bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the rev limiter and overboost cut instead of retarding it. Set in stock; leave it set.
Details: Set in stock (byte 0xF0). In limit state 0x0B (rev limiter, overboost cut) 0x0DD568 sets the spark angle FFF8A76A to the normal spark target FFF8A72A instead of base timing FFF8A645 minus Torque Reduction Spark Retard (asm 0x0DD5F8-0x0DD62A, read), so the limiter does not retard the spark. Cleared, the full cut would ask for about 34 degrees of retard (ratio floor cal 0x2FDE4 = 102, inferred from the table). Leave set. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 0239AE by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 029C6E bit 7 (value 128). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: External Torque Limit Baro Factor (Off in Stock)
External Torque Limit IAT Factor (Off in Stock)
Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (1 Cylinder)
table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Stock 75 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Stock 192 = 75 %. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 023D53 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 02A013. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Intake-temperature factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp. Has no effect on a stock car because the base step is 0. Stock all 1.0.
Details: 0x0C30F8: FFF8AF7E = cal 0x11ACE x this(IAT) x 05A080(baro) >> 14, the per-pass step of the AF9C throttle offset ramp (0x0C3700). cal 0x11ACE = 0, so inactive in stock; all 1.0. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 05A074 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: three look-alike readers 0x0D2768/0x0D27B8/0x0D2808 (= LF75404S 0x0C30F8/0x0C3150/0x0C31A8), told apart by their gain cal (0x11ACE / 0x11AD0 / 0x1080E, same addresses as 2015) and call order, and they keep the 2015 data addresses (read): IAT table of 0x0D2768 (cal 0x11ACE), data 0x011ADC as LF75404S 05A074 (read); the automatic port had 064610, which is the third reader 0x0D2808 (cal 0x1080E, = 05A0A4). Descriptor 0645E0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Air Spark Compensation Limit
table.description:
Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Stock 1.5x at 22.5 degrees or more up to 3.1x at -15 degrees, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three.
Details: 0x0C37D8 (read): FFF8AFA8 = 32768 x (AF2C/AF64) x min(this(final timing FFF8A642), AF56)/8192; the result indexes Throttle Required Area 05A148. It caps the spark-efficiency air compensation (AF56, normally ~1.0) as a function of the actual final timing; stock 1.50x at >=22.5 deg up to 3.13x at -15 deg, so it does not bind in normal warm running. table.description:
2017+ / Forester version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Stock 1.0 at no drop to 0.7 at 30 C drop, the same for every stored temperature. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs, on a hot restart: coolant at start high enough (cals 0x4B638/0x4B639 = 10/110, i.e. the same >= 60 C, 50 C to stay test as LF75404S cals 0x4234C/D) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= cal 0x4B63B (130 = 80 C). 2017+/Forester replacement of the LF75404S 1D table A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (05F1E4), which these images do not have. LF79002P 0x1866D8 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x1802F4; stack arguments checked in the LF79002P disassembly: param_9 @72 = FFF81678, called at 0x18716A, read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature (K x 32) starts at max(FFF81678 x this(FFF81678, coolant drop)/256, min(IAT, coolant) (C150/C152)). table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder (Zero in Stock)

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, A table (weight w). Stock -11...30 degrees. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 05E4BC by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: intake target function 0x1646AC (= LF75404S 0x15C250): each target 2D table is summed with its own coolant offset table x the coolant factor 0692FC, weighted by the barometric blend w (Altitude = w, Sea Level = 1-w); Normal vs High Pedal by the high-pedal flag, TGV-closed set blended by the TGV weight. Descriptor 069344. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time
table.description:
Time after rpm first reaches idle target when the staged air starts to rise, by start type and coolant. Stock 0 or 0.6 s hot. Part of a timed post-start air bump (probably for hot restarts; stock only active at -40 degC and from 70 degC coolant).

A pass counter starts once rpm first reaches the idle target after the start (cal 0x257A8 = 0 margin) and runs while the engine runs; every 4th pass (cal 0x257A6): before Start Time the staged air is held (0 after a start), between Start Time and End Time it rises by Ramp Step per check up to Level + IAT Add, after End Time it is multiplied by Decay. Axes: start type FFF8A6E8 x coolant FFF88A44. Stock: active only at -40 degC and from 70 degC up (zeros between = Start/End 0, so the staged air is decayed to 0 at once; checked as real data, the five data blocks are contiguous 160-byte arrays with no overlap) - a hot-restart air bump (inferred). Used while FFF8A881 bit4 is clear (TGVs not forced closed). This table: Start Time, shown in seconds of the 10 ms pass counter (stock 0, 0.60 s = 60 passes when hot). p16 (read): 0x0F1270 runs every 10 ms; its pass counter FFF84E42 counts 10 ms passes and the decay/ramp steps apply every 4th pass (40 ms). table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 (65535 = no filter in stock) -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V (identical to IAT 2). table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.

ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 (no filter in stock) -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock identical to IAT 1. table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling

Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.

So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Stock: full (219) at the lowest input, empty at 2432 and above. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 0608A4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 06B9E8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.

Identity (inferred): its companion input ADC channel 4 (FFF89390, 0x06C554) is a linear signal centred on 2.5 V (FFF89396 = 12800 - 0.488 x (sample - 32768); SSM x/128 + 28 puts zero at 2.5 V, about -50 A per volt), i.e. a bidirectional battery current, read by charging control 0x136BC0 and idle 0x0EE338; the two inputs share their filter cal block and their range monitors (FFF88BCA bits 2-5, 0x0715B0-0x07175C) are both enabled by cal 0x57584 bit 4, which is clear in stock (monitors off). Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 0608B0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 06B9F4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description:
How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active. Stock about 130 s of heating at -40 C to about 90 s at 60 C.

FFF88E6E sums FFF8CE0B every 40 ms (0x06ED92, read), so it is heater energy since start; FFF8CE0B = 0 while the heater is held off (initial delay from 0x608F4, high load, battery out of range; 0x06E7D8, read). FFF8881E = 2 x (ADC channel 11 - ADC channel 25) (0x1E0000 task, read); it is the oxygen-sensor signal that gates Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (0x0CAE40: FFF8881E < cal 0x14F5C, read), so the second path is 'sensor already reads rich' (inferred). FFF8A833 bit 7 feeds the catalyst/rear-O2 module 0x101CF0 (0x1023E0, 0x102B58) and the rear O2 diagnostics 0x1B8890 / 0x1B902C (P0137, result FFF8AD93 bit 7) and 0x123C68 (read). Meaning 'sensor ready / warmed up' inferred. Stock 26250 at -40 C falling to 18125 at 60 C start coolant; at 13.75 V with the default heater stage that is about 130 s and 90 s of heating (inferred, 200 counts/s). Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor being treated as ready. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 05CEB0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 067BB8. Confidence: inferred.

LF79002P: located from LF75404S 0609C4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 06BBC0. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level, by rpm and load, that confirms channel 1 of the P219A A/F imbalance monitor. It sets no code by itself; P219A needs both this and A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1 exceeded. Raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never). Stock off below 1500 rpm, above 4000 rpm and below 0.91 g/rev (70 % load).
Details: When used: once per combustion event (0x1908E4, crank-synchronous list 0x1E1D1C) while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACD1). Confirms channel 1 of P219A (A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1). 0x18E130 (read): threshold FFF8BC5E = this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616) x 05FCB0(coolant)/8192 x 05FCBC/128 (both 1.0 in stock) x 1.0 (float constants 1000/2^33 and 8.192, 0x18E23C / 0x18E248, read); x 100 instead (capped at 65535, so during that window any cell >= 336 can never be exceeded) until the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 has been unchanged for cal 0x4496E = 150 passes (1.5 s; FFF8ACCD bit 5, 0x1912B4) - the A/C-state stability bit 6 (0x191324, cal 0x436B2 = 0) is always set; 65535 while FFF88A2D bit 0; 05FC90 (all 65535) replaces it near standstill with the pedal released (FFF8ACCD bit 0: FFF88C64 bit 5 and speed < 2 km/h) and 05FC68 (all 65535) while FFF8AA3F is set. 0x18F14C sets FFF8ACC5 = 2 when the crank fluctuation FFF8BC5C - 0x8000 > threshold x 250/256 (so an event counts when the fluctuation exceeds 0.977 x the cell value). 0x18D180... count those events per cylinder (FFF8ACC2 = 1..4, cylinder inferred) into FFF8BC24/28/2C/30 and in total FFF8BC48; at the end of a 2000-event window (FFF8BC20 = cal 0x436F0) 0x18F364 judges FFF8ACC7 = 2 'rough' when a cylinder count > cal 0x436F4 (17) or the total > cal 0x436F6 (17) (with a cylinder share > cal 0x43704 = 0) (read). That latches FFF8ACD8 (0x191850). The channel 1 judgement 0x18F980 gives FFF8ACCB = 2 (exceeded, which sets FFF8ACCF bit 1 and through it the P219A result in 0x19198C) only when the A/F swing exceeded its reference (FFF8ACCE bit 4) AND FFF8ACD8 (or FFF8ACD4) is set; FFF8ACCB = 1 (passed) when the swing passed (FFF8ACCE bit 5, cal 0x436C0 = 1) (read). So the roughness test is a required confirmation: a channel 1 P219A needs both the A/F swing and this crank roughness. (The alternative pass by roughness, FFF8ACD5 and FFF8ACD9, cannot occur in stock: with cal 0x436EE = 0 the second window FFF8BC1E always matches, so FFF8ACC7 never reaches 4; read.) The largest count and its limit are also Mode $06 values FFF815CE / FFF815D0 (0x18EB24 / 0x18EBA8, test 0xDC in the 0x0A0000 reporter, read). Raising cells makes the confirmation harder (65535 = never), lowering makes it easier; it does not set a DTC by itself. Threshold 1 = the table 0x192C14 reads in the flag-clear, param_2-clear branch: 06ABB4 (as 0x18E130 reads 05FC7C). The automatic code pick 06AC14 is the table of the code-identical sibling 0x192D1C (Threshold 2); stock data equal LF75404S 05FC7C (read). Descriptor 06ABB4. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never). Stock off outside 1500-4000 rpm and 0.91-2.07 g/rev (70-160 % load).

LF79002P: located from LF75404S 05FCDC by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: A/F imbalance threshold readers 0x192C14 and 0x192D1C (= LF75404S 0x18E130 / 0x18E250; same code: 1D lookup by FFF8xxxx, 2D lookup chosen by a flag and param_2, 1D byte lookup of param, product clamped to 7999.878 x 8.192; the 2017-style builds drop the 4th flag argument) are called in the same order as in LF75404S (Threshold 2 reader first, then Threshold 1) and write FFF8C2E0 / FFF8C2E2, copied to the next words by the 11-insn functions as LF75404S FFF8BC5E / FFF8BC60 (read). table.name: EGR Enable

table.name: Transmission Coding: From Input Port
table.description:
When set, the manual/automatic coding is read from a hardware input instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT. Clear in all stock images; leave clear.

When set, the transmission coding (FFF886AB bit 7) is taken from a latched input-port bit (FFF80238 bit 7, set once port bit FFF8A2A4 bit 7 is seen) instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT (read, 0x06A38C). table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B
table.description:
Enables the second (Path B) tip-in torque shaping. Clear in stock, and all Path B tables are 0 and its rpm limit is 0, so setting only this bit does essentially nothing. Leave clear unless you calibrate the whole Path B set.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0x01). The torque module 0x0BE694 passes this bit to the rise shaping 0x0BB958 (BLD.B #6 at 0x0BF3D0, stack argument 11, read), and the torque monitor call passes it to 0x1877B4 (read). When set, Path B of the target-torque rise shaping can act (all "Target Torque Rise ... (Path B, ..., Off in Stock)" tables), and a request below Path B Start Torque passes unshaped. Path B also needs rpm <= cal 0x22A04, which is 0 in stock, so setting only this bit changes nothing but the Start Torque bypass (and Path B tables are all 0 ft-lb in stock, so that bypass never triggers). Leave clear unless the whole Path B set is calibrated. Bit 7 of the same byte is a separate switch passed to another torque routine (seg_0x0B0000.c:9252). LF79002P: located from LF75404S 023704 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: the rise-shaping function 0x0CB4BC (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0BB958; it reads the Path B pedal multiplier table) is called once, with (cal 0x299C4 & 0x40) as its only bit-6 cal flag argument, as LF75404S passes cal 0x23704 bit 6 (read); stock byte 0x01 (bit 6 clear). Address 0299C4 bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description:
When set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate, Off in Stock) probably replaces the normal open loop fueling strategy. Clear in stock; leave clear unless you have filled that table.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0x8F). Passed by the open-loop fueling readers 0x0CE854 and 0x0CE5E8 (read): when set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate, Off in Stock) is used in place of the base + DAM-scaled knock additive strategy (inferred). Leave clear unless you have filled that table. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 02F79A by the code that reads it (read). Address 036B76 bit 4 (value 16). Confidence: read.

table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description:
When set, Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock) is used while the cams are probably not yet under control. Clear in stock; leave clear.
Details: Clear in stock. 0x11E308 uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock) only when this bit is set and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear (read); FFF8A83B bit 7 = AVCS ready (inferred). Leave clear. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 02C4D0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Caller passes (DAT_00033888 & 1) as param_2 of 0x12C630, the counterpart of LF75404S 0x11E308 (bodies identical modulo addresses); LF75404S passes (0x2C4D0 & 1) in the same slot; neighbouring call passes 0x33888 bit1 where LF75404S passes 0x2C4D0 bit1. Stock byte 0x00 (bit clear), same as LF75404S. Address 033888 bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing: Pedal-Released Tables Enable
table.description:
Set in stock: with the pedal released, Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed/Open) replaces the normal EGR Active/Off base timing tables. Clear it to use the normal base timing tables off-throttle too.
Details: Set in stock (all images). With this bit set and FFF8A774 bit 0 (pedal released) set, Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed/Open) replaces the EGR Active/Off base timing tables (read, 0x0C2C08). Clear it to use the normal base timing tables with the pedal released. LF79002P: located from LF75404S 01071E by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Caller passes (DAT_0001071e & 1) as param_8 of 0x0D22C0 (pair of LF75404S 0x0C2C08), with FFF8ACEA bit0 as param_9; callee uses param_8/param_9 in the same test as LF75404S. Stock byte 0x01 (bit set), same as LF75404S. Address 01071E bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 1
table.description:
Allows double/triple injection while one of the high-pedal latches is set (clear = not allowed; clear in stock). Has no effect on a stock car because the multi-injection windows are disabled, so stock always uses single injection.

Only matters if the double/triple injection windows are opened (they are 65535 in stock, so stock always uses single injection). table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 1 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 1's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D168C writes FFF8C060 = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1E4 (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05B1FC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 009DA0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Strategy byte = injections per cycle (FFF8A69E, 0x0CF3EC, read): this one applies with one injection (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6A3 by 0x0CF630 (read). Injector 1's quantity (0x0D168C) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A69F equals 1 (read). The strategy byte is probably the number of injections per cycle (inferred from the split-injection code). All 128 (x1.0) in stock. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05ADE8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0098A4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset
table.description:
Pressure offset added to measured rail pressure before looking up Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4), by rpm and load; probably the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor. Stock all 0 (no effect).
Details: 0x06D43A (read): FFF89222 = sat(rail pressure FFF88886 + this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616)), interpolated by 0x00671C (descriptor 0x0608E4: data, u16 axis, u8 axis, 16, 16; row = rpm, read). FFF89222 indexes the injector flow compensation 05A844 used only for injectors 2 and 4 (0x0CB0C8, read); injectors 1 and 3 use 05A838 with FFF88886. Likely the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor (inferred from the boxer layout). Signed, in the rail-pressure unit. Stock all 0 (2015, 2016). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0608E4 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: FUN_0000684c(&0x063438, rpm FFF8E51C, load FFF8BA26) added to the rail pressure and saturated, the same code as LF75404S 0x06D43A (read); descriptor {data, rpm axis u16, load axis u8, 16, 16} read from the image. Descriptor boot 063438. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 4, Start Delay)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Released)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 3, Pedal Applied)
Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 (an early warm-up phase); the one the stock car uses, since the fallback version never activates. Stock 15 MPa flat.
Details: When used: The combustion mode 1 target in stock (FFF899D7 bit 0 never sets, read). 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is clear. Stock 15 MPa flat. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EB4C by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: Phase 11: the selector flag (2017 FFF8AD5A bit 0, 2018 FFF8BC16 bit 0, 2015 FFF8A7E2 bit 0) is state FFF8AD55 in {1,2,3,4,6} (0x103C64 / 0x0FD5FC in 2017). State 1 is forced while FFF889FB bit 7 (2015 FFF886AB bit 7) is set, and that bit is set permanently by the transmission coding cal (2015 0x2F794/0x2F796, 2017 0x36B70/0x36B72, 2018 0x37FEC/0x37FEE: bit 1 clear, bit 6 clear) in all four stock images (read). So the flag-set table is the one the stock (manual) car uses; the flag-clear table is for the other coding, whose state machine uses engine speed minus a received transmission speed (AT/CVT, inferred). rail-pressure selection 0x1693A4, combustion mode 1, fallback flag clear (read). Descriptor 00DC88. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1). Only used with the automatic/CVT transmission coding; no effect on a manual car.
Details: When used: Only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding (Cal Switches: Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT); unused on a manual car (read). LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1). Evidence: Phase 11: the selector flag (2017 FFF8AD5A bit 0, 2018 FFF8BC16 bit 0, 2015 FFF8A7E2 bit 0) is state FFF8AD55 in {1,2,3,4,6} (0x103C64 / 0x0FD5FC in 2017). State 1 is forced while FFF889FB bit 7 (2015 FFF886AB bit 7) is set, and that bit is set permanently by the transmission coding cal (2015 0x2F794/0x2F796, 2017 0x36B70/0x36B72, 2018 0x37FEC/0x37FEE: bit 1 clear, bit 6 clear) in all four stock images (read). So the flag-set table is the one the stock (manual) car uses; the flag-clear table is for the other coding, whose state machine uses engine speed minus a received transmission speed (AT/CVT, inferred). This is the flag-clear table, not used by the stock calibration. rail-pressure selection 0x1693A4, combustion mode 1, fallback flag clear (read). Descriptor 00DCD8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit

scaling.category: mg fuel per cylinder (stock Injector Scaling)
scaling.units: mg (stoich fuel per cylinder per cycle)

scaling.category: base pulse (0.3 MPa reference, any Injector Scaling)

table.description:
Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling: stock it allows about 5 g of air per revolution, but lowering the injector flow figure (for example for E85) lowers the ceiling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.
Details: When used: always while running (every pass of 0x0B7E00, which computes load and the base fuel quantity, read). Upper limit of the base (stoichiometric) fuel quantity FFF8ADEA. 0x0B8030 (read) computes FFF8ADEA = air quantity FFF8C250 x Injector Scaling x 0.10266 / 14.7 / 4 / rpm x 0.125 (= 0.5587 x Injector Scaling x air per cylinder per cycle in g) and stores min(that, this) (0x0B80FC-0x0B8112: MOVU.W @0x23696, CMP/GE, read). The limited value is what the rest of the fuel path uses: the base pulse 0x0D15EC (FFF8C05C = 16 x FFF8ADEA x trims), before the enrichment/fuel factor 0x0D1528 and the flow compensation and latency 0x0D2BB8; the transient-fuel film model 0x0F5F84; the fuel load FFF8ADEE (0x0B895C); and the fuel-used accumulators 0x06B70E (read). Above the limit the base pulse stops rising with airflow, so the mixture goes lean as air keeps rising; enrichment is applied on top of the limited value and does not lift it (inferred from the order of the calls). The raw unit includes Injector Scaling, so the limit in air terms moves with it: air per revolution at the limit = this x 3.580 / Injector Scaling (raw) g/rev = this x reference injector flow [g/s] x 0.0004704. Shown in g/rev for stock Injector Scaling 2918 (2.61 g/s). Stock 4060 = 4.98 g/rev (2.49 g per cylinder per cycle, about 556 g/s at 6700 rpm), well beyond the stock turbo. With Injector Scaling at 1.74 g/s (fuel added for E85 by lowering the flow figure) the limit drops to 3.32 g/rev; below about 1.73 g/s it falls under the 3.31 g/rev (256 %) ceiling of engine load FFF8ADE4 (0x0B7EFC, read) and becomes the first limit reached. When you raise Injector Scaling raw (lower reference flow), raise this in proportion: new = 4060 x new raw / 2918 keeps 4.98 g/rev (u16, up to 65535). On AT/CVT codings, while FFF886AB bit 5 is set (meaning not decoded), the value is first smoothed by boot filter 0x6CEC with cal 0x23694 (stock 255); the limit applies on either path (read). 4060 in all eight images; the same code in LF78001H 0x0C1770, LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LV9N 0x0A6840 (read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 023696 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: Base fuel quantity cap: the first-stage fuel quantity routine (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0B8030; LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LF78001H 0x0C1770) stores min(quantity, this cal); stock 4060 as in LF75404S (read, my research notes). Address 02A94A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Double Injection, Off in Stock)
table.description:

table.name: Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1, Fallback, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Rail pressure target in combustion mode 1 after a warm-up fallback has latched. Off in stock: the fallback is enabled by a calibration switch that is off. Stock 15 MPa flat.
Details: When used: Used only while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set, a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch (0x081EFC) gated by cal 0x59134 bit 0, which is 0 in stock, so never used in stock (read). 0x165180 (read): target in combustion mode FFF8A85C = 1 while FFF899D7 bit 0 is set (else Target Rail Pressure (Combustion Mode 1)); coolant FFF88A44. Stock 15 MPa flat. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EB84 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: Phase 11: the selector flag (2017 FFF8AD5A bit 0, 2018 FFF8BC16 bit 0, 2015 FFF8A7E2 bit 0) is state FFF8AD55 in {1,2,3,4,6} (0x103C64 / 0x0FD5FC in 2017). State 1 is forced while FFF889FB bit 7 (2015 FFF886AB bit 7) is set, and that bit is set permanently by the transmission coding cal (2015 0x2F794/0x2F796, 2017 0x36B70/0x36B72, 2018 0x37FEC/0x37FEE: bit 1 clear, bit 6 clear) in all four stock images (read). So the flag-set table is the one the stock (manual) car uses; the flag-clear table is for the other coding, whose state machine uses engine speed minus a received transmission speed (AT/CVT, inferred). rail-pressure selection 0x1693A4, fallback flag FFF89E0D bit 0 set, never in stock (read). table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear (stock; the first argument of 0x0CE854), the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128, both all zero in stock (read). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 009728. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description:
Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. Stock identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling; edit all five together. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.
Details: When used: whenever the open-loop delay has expired (see below); the blend follows TGV position and AVCS state. TGV-closed base, weight 1 - a (AVCS not in active control). 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear (stock): FFF8A681 = clamp(blend + Additive x DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128 - 05AC14 x 05AC3C(DAM)/128 (Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) x its DAM multiplier; both all zero in stock), 0, 255). With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). Stock: byte-identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling (05AC6C) and to the other three tables of this group (AFR 14.7 down to about 10.7 at high load); edit all five together. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05ABB0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00948C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description:
Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC. Stock pinned at the late limit, about 170 degrees after TDC. Has no effect in stock: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share is 0, so the pulse gets no fuel.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Stock boundaries are 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load) (this is boundary 1, stock 31.5 %). Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). 0x0DFA88 also sums it into the total knock correction FFF8A77B, whose only consumer (0x0DDBBC -> FFF8A770) is zero in stock (read). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one (most of the high-load map in stock); where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Stock 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load).
