Details: When used: while FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set; weight DAM/16 (the DAM 1 table). 0x0D9D48 (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8) blends the two tables by DAM FFF811AE (0..16): FFF8A741 = (DAM 1 table x DAM + DAM 0 table x (16 - DAM))/16, 32 = no change; then 0x0D9B28 sets FFF8A73C = FFF8A741 when FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set (cal 0x32DEA != 0x5A as in stock), else 32, and 0x0DA600 adds FFF8A73C - 32 (0.5-degree units) to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (read). FFF8A8A3 bit 6 (0x11C04C, read) = combustion mode FFF8A85C = 4, coolant within cal 0x36502..0x36500 (all), DAM >= cal 0x364FE (0), FFF8A8A4 bit 6 set (the injection-timing high-pedal latch 0x11C0C4 that selects Injection Timing (High Pedal), 90 % / 85 % in stock; not the AVCS latch bit 7 used by Base Timing DAM Blend) and open-loop enrichment FFF8A684 <= (FFF8B32A - 32768)/128 (closed-loop target offset term). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (same as Base Timing DAM Blend). Unlike Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (Off in Stock), this path is live in stock, but both tables are flat 32, so it adds nothing. Stock 32 (0 degrees) everywhere. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05B574 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00A1F0. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D, Unused in Stock)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires. Unused in stock because every Secondary Knock Threshold is at maximum, so that detector never triggers. Stock about 1.4 degrees.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. Stock 4 counts = 1.41 degrees. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01C277 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0E2BE4->0x0EDC08 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [1]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01C277 (1 reference(s), votes {'0227A7': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x0227A7 is accessed as u8. Stock 4 (LF75404S 4). Matches the layout address. Address 0227A7. Confidence: read.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold (Off in Stock)
Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0) (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. It has no effect on a stock car: it is only used when a calibration switch is set to a specific value, which it is not in stock. 32 = no change. Stock +2 degrees at low rpm, varying to 0 from 4000 rpm; identical to its DAM 1 pair.
Details: When used: never in stock. Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). Off in Stock (read): FFF8A740 has two readers (ram_xref, instruction level): 0x0D9B28 uses it only when cal 0x32DEA == 0x5A ('Z'), and stock is 0x00, so FFF8A73C = FFF8A741 x 50 / 50 under FFF8A8A3 bit 6, else 32; and 0x0E0E44, whose output FFF8A777 bit 1 is read only by the same 0x0D9B28 branch (FFF8A777 readers: 0x0DF0B8 call args and the init 0x0DF59C). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. So in stock neither table changes timing or any other output. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Stock flat across load and varying with rpm: 36 (+2 degrees) at 400-1200 rpm, 32 (no change) at 1600, 34 (+1) at 2000-2400, 36 (+2) at 2800-3600 rpm and 32 (no change) from 4000 rpm; identical to 05B560. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05B54C by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: timing parent 0x0EA868 calls the two code-identical 77-insn DAM blend readers as callees 21 and 22 (0x8A0 calls not counted), as LF75404S 0x0DF0B8 calls 0x0D9BD4 (Alternate: 05B560 DAM 1, then 05B54C DAM 0, output FFF8A73F) and 0x0D9D48 (Blend B: 05B574 DAM 1, then 05B588 DAM 0, output FFF8A741) as callees 20 and 21 (read). Here 0x0E54DC reads 00A1DC (DAM 1) then 00A1C8 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6A; 0x0E5628 reads 00A1F0 (DAM 1) then 00A204 (DAM 0) and writes FFF8BB6C (read). The consumers match by use: FFF8A73F / FFF8BB6A are used once (with FFF8A73B-type term), FFF8A741 / FFF8BB6C twice (x0x32 and with the FFF8A738-type term) (read). So 0x0E54DC = Alternate (0x0D9BD4) and 0x0E5628 = Blend B (0x0D9D48). Phase 18 had put the Alternate entries on the Blend B reader's tables (00A204/00A1F0), now shared with the Phase 19 Blend B entries (port_sanity duplicate); stock data equal LF75404S 05B54C/05B560 (read). Descriptor 00A1C8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Short Window)
table.description:
Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off); this is the active path in stock and drives FBKC states 7 / 0x0E (retard 0x1C275 / 0x1C274, 4 counts = 1.41 degrees). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4); all 65535 in stock, so it never fires (states 6 / 0x0D). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. Knock Threshold (0x0E77E0, read): looked up by rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500) and load FFF8A616 for each event slot; set A (05C104/118/12C/140) while FFF8A7C1 = 0, i.e. the nominal (short) window; set B (05C154/168/17C/190) while A7C1 = 1, i.e. the extended window (0x0E77E0 at 0x0E7836-0x0E784A; flag polarity read in 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30, the earlier names had the two sets swapped). A higher value needs a larger knock signal to count as knock (less sensitive). Set A (nominal / short window). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05C104 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00ADD8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 2, Channel 2)
table.description:
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 2 of 8 (index 1 of FFF8CDB0; enabled in stock: bit 1 of cal 0x1B97D is clear), on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 4 to 97 (raw); the sibling tables for channels 1, 7 and 8 (masked in stock) are all 0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05BEAC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00AB80. Confidence: read.

table.description:
AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1). Not used on this manual-transmission calibration, so it has no effect on a stock car. Stock 0, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 1 (0x0DBB20, read: the AT/CVT curve branch, mirrored by the MT branch that reads Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1); the MT coding flag s4 picks the MT curve). Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. table.name: A/C Cut Timing Retard Step (Alternate Logic) (Off in Stock)
Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed; identical to the TGV Open table in stock. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections), and in stock the target is far lower, so raising this map at idle or when coasting does nothing.
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. The TGV Closed and TGV Open tables are identical in stock. Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 set (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. In stock the request at idle (about 6-8 degrees at 500-900 rpm, warm) is far below this map (19-28 degrees at 400-1000 rpm, 0.13-0.39 g/rev (10-30 % load)), and it stays below it when coasting (17 vs 34 degrees at 2000 rpm), so idle and coast timing are set by Closed-Pedal Timing Target and raising this map there has no effect (computed from stock data); lowering it below the target does take effect. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05A034 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 008580. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation RPM Multiplier
Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance (Coolant at Start)
Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description:
Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths. Stock +17 degrees cold at low rpm, down to about -10 to -12.5 when warm.

table.name: Boost Limit
table.description:
Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run. Stock 211 kPa absolute peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost.
Details: 0x1086F8 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A84F (raw) and FFF8A84E = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, where f is the target's baro/IAT factor: the compensated boost ceiling (read). The torque-model task 0x0C3D14 copies it to FFF8AFAE = A84E << 8 (0x0C3D0C, read). AFAE is the full-load manifold pressure of the throttle/torque model. Target MAP FFF8AF6A = (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this (0x0C2F0C). FFF8AF8A = Throttle Required Area column input AFA8 x this (0x0C3408). The pressure ratio AF6C = AF8A / this (0x0C2F9C) selects the high-pressure spark-compensation filter above 0.85 (all read). Also read by the airflow/torque model 0x111AB8 (role there not decoded). It is not an overboost cut; see Overboost Limit for that. Stock 211 kPa abs peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost. Raise it with Target Boost. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05CFC8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00BDB4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per step everywhere, i.e. no Stage 1 limit.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding; unused in stock (manual coding). AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock, 255 = x1) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Stock 24000 everywhere = 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per 10 ms, i.e. no Stage 1 limit (same as the high-gear cells of the Stage 2 AT/CVT Coding tables). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0598BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 007CEC. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEDE by the code that reads it (read). Address 02440E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:
Overboost limit by rpm, compensated for baro and intake temperature like the boost target. Boost 26.7 kPa over it for 2 s sets the overboost flag, and 33 kPa over it starts the overboost cut (throttle cap, then a full fuel cut once the flag is set). Raise it when raising boost targets (stock 211 kPa absolute peak). Note: the boost-control pressure reading stops at about 269 kPa absolute, so an Overboost Limit above about 236 kPa absolute (269 minus the 33 kPa cut margin) can never trigger the overboost cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768 (read; cal 0x290A8 = 1 would use a fixed value, 0 in stock). Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. The flag makes the state-0x0B cut a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Rev Limit RPM); on its own, outside state 0x0B, it reduces nothing. It also feeds a diagnostic 0x1B8310. Stock 211 kPa abs peak, the same as Boost Limit from 2,000 rpm. Raise it with Target Boost. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05CFD4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00BDC0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description:
Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables). Set in stock; cleared, the limiter is probably fuel-cut only.
Details: Set in stock. With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). Cleared, the rev limiter and the overboost cut become fuel-only: no throttle closing during the cut (inferred). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 023CEA by the code that reads it (read). Address 02AF9E bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this. Stock 0 kPa.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. The flag forces the zero torque cap in the overboost/rev cut state (0x0BAE98 -> FFF8AE8A, applied in limit state 0x0B; Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) and also feeds 0x1B8310 (0x1B828C / 0x1B83CC, the overboost diagnostic, inferred in my research notes), so this margin also sets how long that monitor sees overboost. Stock 0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEF6 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 024426. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:
Boost above Overboost Limit plus this enters the overboost cut state: the throttle is capped at once, and fuel to all cylinders is cut only if the 2-second overboost flag is also set. Stock 33 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Overboost latch FFF84167 (0x0BE140, read): sets when MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit (the baro/IAT-compensated FFF8A851) + this, and releases when MAP < that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). While set (and no higher state) the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0B, the same state as the rev limiter (see Rev Limit RPM). In that state the throttle-side request is capped at once (Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base) by rpm, or the stage tables above 256 kPa abs); fuel is cut on all four cylinders every event only once the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 is also set (MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay, 2.0 s stock) or rpm reaches Rev Limit Full Cut RPM; spark is not retarded. When MAP falls below the release level the state ends and fuel returns even if the flag is still set (inferred from the state gating, read). Stock 8448 = 33 kPa, about 244 kPa abs at the 211 kPa stock limit peak. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEE6 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0C6814 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE6 (1 reference(s), votes {'024416': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x024416 is accessed as u16. Stock 8448 (LF75404S 8448). Matches the layout address. Address 024416. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)
table.description:
How far boost must fall below the overboost cut level before the overboost cut state ends. Stock 15 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Subtracted from the overboost latch level while the latch FFF84167 is set (0x0BE208-0x0BE222, read): the overboost cut state 0x0B releases when MAP FFF88FF4 < Overboost Limit + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) - this. See Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) for what the state does. Stock 3840 = 15 kPa, so the state releases 18 kPa above the Overboost Limit. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEE8 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0C6814 (ref 2 access(es), target 2, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE8 (2 reference(s), votes {'024418': 2}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x024418 is accessed as u16. table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:
Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing. Stock 255 km/h (no effect in stock).

The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEEB by its caller in the decompiled code (read). table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Stock 75 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Stock 192 = 75 %. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. table.description:
Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Stock 1.5x at 22.5 degrees or more up to 3.1x at -15 degrees, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Stock EGR and non-EGR tables are identical.
Details: When used: every pass of the 0x110000 torque module. Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR). Stock: 14-49 ft-lb (19-66 Nm) at zero load, 260-306 ft-lb (352-415 Nm) at 2.81 g/rev (217 % load) from 2400 rpm (119 ft-lb, 162 Nm cap at 800 rpm); identical to the EGR table 05D64C. 0x118318 (DAM 1 set -> FFF8B490) and 0x1186A4 (DAM 0 set -> FFF8B4A2), called from 0x110000 with rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616, TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (read): closed = TGV-closed x (1 - w) + TGV-closed-EGR x w, open = TGV-open x (1 - w) + TGV-open-EGR x w with w = B290/256, result = closed x (1 - B3E8) + open x B3E8, all above the 16000 zero point (read; same blend as the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables in 0x0C0010). 0x10ED6C interpolates the two sets by DAM: FFF8B48A = B490 x DAM + B4A2 x (1 - DAM) with FFF811AE = DAM x 16 (read), and 0x118A40 subtracts (B490 - B4A2) x (1 - DAM) from the torque it reports as FFF8B4B2 (0.1 ft-lb, 0.1 Nm, 10000 = 0) (read). They do not set the throttle or boost; they shape the estimated/reported engine torque (inferred). Axes: rpm FFF8CE9C x load % FFF8A616. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D638 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) CORRECTION of the existing curated_LF9C100P placement (00C530, which is the DAM 0 set). 0x120EB8 is the first call (-> FFF8C96C, the B490/DAM 1 slot of the DAM interpolator 0x118654, identical to LF75404S 0x10ED6C after normalisation); lookup 1 -> &DAT_00C4E0 (LF75404S 05D638). table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. Map A while no open-loop enrichment is active. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. FFF8C562 = S filtered (weight 05A578 while FFF8AFCC is rising, 05A5A0 while falling, by rpm x load); FFF8C564 = (U - S + fuel-cut term FFF8B040) filtered (weights 05A680 / 05A6A8 by air quantity FFF8B4D6 x FFF8B066); estimate FFF8AFD0 = FFF8C562 + FFF8C564, so in steady state FFF8AFD0 tends to Map B. 0x0CE854 enables Primary Open Loop Fueling while FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), and 0x0C5880 integrates 05A82C(FFF8AFD0) into FFF8C03C, the second enable path (read). Reading FFF8AFD0 as an exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate is inferred: the enriched maps are lower than the stoichiometric ones, retard raises the value (multiplier 0.75 at 25 degrees advanced to 1.2 at 20 degrees retarded) and the value gates the enrichment. Raising these maps brings Primary Open Loop Fueling in earlier (lower load); lowering them delays it. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05A564 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 008D58. Confidence: inferred.

A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (2D)
table.description:
2017+ / Forester version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Stock 1.0 at no drop to 0.7 at 30 C drop, the same for every stored temperature. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs, on a hot restart: coolant at start high enough (cals 0x4B638/0x4B639 = 10/110, i.e. the same >= 60 C, 50 C to stay test as LF75404S cals 0x4234C/D) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= cal 0x4B63B (130 = 80 C). 2017+/Forester replacement of the LF75404S 1D table A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (05F1E4), which these images do not have. LF79002P 0x1866D8 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x1802F4; stack arguments checked in the LF79002P disassembly: param_9 @72 = FFF81678, called at 0x18716A, read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature (K x 32) starts at max(FFF81678 x this(FFF81678, coolant drop)/256, min(IAT, coolant) (C150/C152)). FFF81678 is the pipe temperature latched when the engine stops (0x1866B8, read; = LF75404S FFF815BA). Axis 1 = that stored pipe temperature (u16, K x 32; the lookup 0x1B0D7C clamps it and the drop to the axis ends), axis 2 = the coolant drop since the engine last ran, FFF8069B - FFF88D96 x 160/65536 - 10 (s8, degC) (read). Data u8, unsigned interpolation in 0x1B0D7C, layout [stored-temperature index x 8 + drop index] (read). The starting temperature drives the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release (see A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure). Stock identical in all four images and in every row (no dependence on the stored temperature): 1.00 (255) at 0 C drop, 0.95 at 5, 0.90 at 10, 0.85 at 15, 0.80 at 20, 0.75 at 25, 0.70 at 30 and 35 C drop - the same curve as LF75404S 05F1E4, with 5 C steps. LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have. Evidence: Phase 19 group X (my research notes): reader 0x183B20, call site 183BD8; replaces the 1D hot-restart factor of the 2015 code (read). Descriptor 00E370. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder (Zero in Stock)
table.description:

table.name: Intake Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Low, breakpoint 0x496BD)
table.description:
Upper limit on the final intake cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables. With the stock breakpoints (all 255) this Low table is the ceiling at every temperature and the Mid/High tables are never used, so anything lowered here caps the cam target at all temperatures unless the breakpoints are changed too. Stock is 90 degrees everywhere, so it never limits on a stock car.

Cold-engine correction (degrees of exhaust retard) added to the final exhaust cam target at altitude (whatever the TGV state), scaled by Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor. Positive = more retard. All 0 in stock.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): adds to the exhaust cam target in crank degrees of RETARD; positive = more retard, negative = less (stock cold values down to -51 pull the exhaust cam back to its rest position). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Coolant term: this x w x Exhaust Cam Coolant Factor / 128. All 0 in stock. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E864 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: exhaust target function 0x164098 (= LF79002P exhaust target function): each target 2D table plus its own coolant offset x coolant factor 00D824, weighted by the barometric blend w (Altitude = w, Sea Level = 1-w); Normal vs High Pedal by the high-pedal flag; TGV-closed set blended by the TGV weight. Read from the decompiled code. Descriptor 00D920. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Cam Target Ceiling (Oil Temp Low, breakpoint 0x496C5)
table.description:
Upper limit on the final exhaust cam target, interpolated by (probably) oil temperature between the Low / Mid / High ceiling tables. With the stock breakpoints (all 255) this Low table is the ceiling at every temperature and the Mid/High tables are never used, so anything lowered here caps the cam target at all temperatures unless the breakpoints are changed too. Stock is 90 degrees everywhere, so it never limits on a stock car.
Details: When used: Always, as a cap on the final cam target interpolated by oil temperature (inferred input) between the breakpoints; stock tables are 90 degrees and the breakpoints 255, so it never limits in stock (read). LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Exhaust Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude). Evidence: exhaust target function 0x164098 reads three 2D tables (rpm x load, same axes as its targets) and interpolates them by FFF88E7D against breakpoints 0x496C5 (low) / 0x496C6 (mid) / 0x496C4 (high); at or below the low breakpoint the low table applies, above the high one no limit (0x7FFF). The result caps the final cam target: target = min(target, ceiling) (read). FFF88E7D is the high byte of the sensor value written in 0x060000-area code that LF75404S has as FFF88A9D, the oil temperature path (input identity inferred). Stock: all three tables are 90 degrees (no effect) and all breakpoints 255 (read) (template: Exhaust Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude) for the exhaust cam-retard scaling and the rpm x load axis scalings; the 20x16 shape comes from this image's own descriptor). Descriptor 00D844. Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Barometric Blend
table.description:
Share (0-100 %) of the altitude (A) cam target tables versus the sea-level (B) tables, by barometric pressure. Stock: 100 % altitude tables at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft), 0 % at or above 98 kPa, so near sea level only the B tables are used.

AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. This table is w itself: the share of every A table (the B tables get the rest), by barometric pressure FFF88668 (0x15B1E0 looks it up and stores FFF8B948, read). Stock 100 % A at or below 84 kPa, ramping to 0 % at 98 kPa and above. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E3FC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D388. Confidence: read.

table.name: High Pedal Exit Threshold
table.description:
Accelerator position below which the high-pedal flag clears and the cams return to the normal (set 1) targets. Keep it below High Pedal Entry Threshold. Stock 85 %.
Details: High-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (0x10F848 -> FFF8B410, 0x11C15C, read): FFF8B410 counts passes with the accelerator FFF88A5E at or above this threshold (by barometric pressure FFF88A42 = FFF88668) while vehicle speed FFF88BE8 changes by less than cal 0x35B16... per pass (by gear FFF888A0) and FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6 and FFF8A8A2 bit 6 are clear. The bit sets once FFF8B410 reaches 05D740 (1 pass) and clears after the pedal stays below cal 0x36518 for cal 0x36516 passes. The AVCS uses the bit to pick cam target set 2; 12 other functions read FFF8A8A4 (not reviewed). Below this the latch clears. Stock 55705 = 85 %. p16 (read): the pass counter FFF8B410 (0x10F848 <- 0x1140BC <- 0x1E1560) runs in the 80 ms OS task (one pass = 80 ms); the latch 0x11C15C runs every 10 ms. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 036518 by the code that reads it (read). Address 03EADE. Confidence: read.

Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5)
table.description:
Main idle speed target by coolant in normal running; this is the table to edit to change idle speed on a manual car. Stock 1450 rpm cold to 700 rpm from 80 degC. Automatic/CVT cars use Mode 6 instead (identical in stock).
Details: When used: warm idle in normal running (the idle mode manual cars use). 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 5 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Stock mode 5: 1450 rpm cold -> 700 rpm at >=80 degC. This is the table to edit to change warm idle speed on a manual car (data at 0x024B10). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 024B10 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: idle-speed reader 0x0FBC98 (= LF75404S 0x0F1BCC) calls the implicit-axis lookup on the same tables in the same order, and they sit in the same memory order (read): second-to-last lookup. Data at 02BEA4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, AT/CVT, Mode 6)
table.description:
Warm idle speed target by coolant for automatic/CVT cars only; a manual car never uses this table. Stock identical to Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5); to change idle on a manual edit Mode 5.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT transmission coding. With the manual coding the idle mode never becomes 6 (0x0F2BCC passes the mode through unchanged while FFF88ADA bit 7 is set, and 0x0F354C produces only modes 1-5 and 7, read), so on a manual car edit Mode 5. 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 6 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Stock identical to Mode 5 (1450 rpm cold -> 700 rpm at >=80 degC); to change warm idle on a manual car edit Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) (0x024B10). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 024B30 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: idle-speed reader 0x0FBC98 (= LF75404S 0x0F1BCC) calls the implicit-axis lookup on the same tables in the same order, and they sit in the same memory order (read): last lookup. Data at 02BEC4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description:

Details: When used: idle mode 1 (engine stopped, or dropped out of the running state) and mode 2 (after a start with coolant below 75 C / 167 F, until the car moves or, once the warm-up flag FFF88EA2 bit 1 has cleared, coolant reaches 50 C / 122 F; held at least 200 time-since-start counts) (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 1/2 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC in 10 degC steps (lookup 0x7414, read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 024AB0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: idle-speed reader 0x0FBC98 (= LF75404S 0x0F1BCC) calls the implicit-axis lookup on the same tables in the same order, and they sit in the same memory order (read): first lookup. Data at 02BE44. Confidence: read.

Idle Base Air (Mode 5)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle (the warm-idle mode on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. At a settled warm idle the TGVs are normally commanded closed, so Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed) is probably the table in use: change both together, and together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) so idle feedback does not have to learn the difference. Stock hot value is about 1.9 % throttle.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling

Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling

Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling

Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold

How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active. Stock about 130 s of heating at -40 C to about 90 s at 60 C.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1
table.description:

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit

scaling.category: mg fuel per cylinder (stock Injector Scaling)
scaling.units: mg (stoich fuel per cylinder per cycle)

scaling.category: base pulse (0.3 MPa reference, any Injector Scaling)

table.description:
Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling: stock it allows about 5 g of air per revolution, but lowering the injector flow figure (for example for E85) lowers the ceiling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.
Details: When used: always while running (every pass of 0x0B7E00, which computes load and the base fuel quantity, read). Upper limit of the base (stoichiometric) fuel quantity FFF8ADEA. 0x0B8030 (read) computes FFF8ADEA = air quantity FFF8C250 x Injector Scaling x 0.10266 / 14.7 / 4 / rpm x 0.125 (= 0.5587 x Injector Scaling x air per cylinder per cycle in g) and stores min(that, this) (0x0B80FC-0x0B8112: MOVU.W @0x23696, CMP/GE, read). The limited value is what the rest of the fuel path uses: the base pulse 0x0D15EC (FFF8C05C = 16 x FFF8ADEA x trims), before the enrichment/fuel factor 0x0D1528 and the flow compensation and latency 0x0D2BB8; the transient-fuel film model 0x0F5F84; the fuel load FFF8ADEE (0x0B895C); and the fuel-used accumulators 0x06B70E (read). Above the limit the base pulse stops rising with airflow, so the mixture goes lean as air keeps rising; enrichment is applied on top of the limited value and does not lift it (inferred from the order of the calls). The raw unit includes Injector Scaling, so the limit in air terms moves with it: air per revolution at the limit = this x 3.580 / Injector Scaling (raw) g/rev = this x reference injector flow [g/s] x 0.0004704. Shown in g/rev for stock Injector Scaling 2918 (2.61 g/s). Stock 4060 = 4.98 g/rev (2.49 g per cylinder per cycle, about 556 g/s at 6700 rpm), well beyond the stock turbo. With Injector Scaling at 1.74 g/s (fuel added for E85 by lowering the flow figure) the limit drops to 3.32 g/rev; below about 1.73 g/s it falls under the 3.31 g/rev (256 %) ceiling of engine load FFF8ADE4 (0x0B7EFC, read) and becomes the first limit reached. When you raise Injector Scaling raw (lower reference flow), raise this in proportion: new = 4060 x new raw / 2918 keeps 4.98 g/rev (u16, up to 65535). On AT/CVT codings, while FFF886AB bit 5 is set (meaning not decoded), the value is first smoothed by boot filter 0x6CEC with cal 0x23694 (stock 255); the limit applies on either path (read). 4060 in all eight images; the same code in LF78001H 0x0C1770, LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LV9N 0x0A6840 (read). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 023696 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: Base fuel quantity cap: the first-stage fuel quantity routine (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0B8030; LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LF78001H 0x0C1770) stores min(quantity, this cal); stock 4060 as in LF75404S (read, my research notes). Address 02A792. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear (stock; the first argument of 0x0CE854), the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128, both all zero in stock (read). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 066D84. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description:
Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. Stock identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling; edit all five together. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.
Details: When used: whenever the open-loop delay has expired (see below); the blend follows TGV position and AVCS state. TGV-closed base, weight 1 - a (AVCS not in active control). 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear (stock): FFF8A681 = clamp(blend + Additive x DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128 - 05AC14 x 05AC3C(DAM)/128 (Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) x its DAM multiplier; both all zero in stock), 0, 255). With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). Fade time for After-Start Enrichment 2: the enrichment falls linearly to zero over this time after start (unfaded while cranking). Larger = longer enrichment. Used with the TGVs open.
Details: Fade time FFF843F2 for After-Start Enrichment 2 (0x0CD834, read): the enrichment falls linearly from full to zero after 8 x this many counts of FFF8B06A (read). In cranking mode (FFF8906B = 2) the enrichment is used unfaded (read). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. table.description:

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description:
Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC. Stock pinned at the late limit, about 170 degrees after TDC. Has no effect in stock: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share is 0, so the pulse gets no fuel.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC; negative = AFTER that TDC (expansion stroke). This angle is an offset in segment 0, the 180 degrees after firing TDC (0x0CB604 mode 3 uses it with segment 0; the pulse-fit check 0x075D84 places it B064 + 1440 after the first pulse B062, read), so it is shown as -offset/2: clamped to 0 to -179.5 (0x0D0468, read), and -170 to -179.5 act as -169.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock pins at the -179.5 clamp (stored -170 at spark 24 BTDC only): a late expansion-stroke pulse, about 170 degrees ATDC in effect (its quantity is Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share, cal 0x2A3CA, which is 0 in stock, so stock fires no second pulse in this mode). Catalyst-heating mode = FFF8A85C 2 (0x109B4C, read): it maps to fuel mode 3 (0x108B08), in which the ignition target is FFF8A76C (0x0DA51C, read) and the injection angle is FFF8B062 (0x0CB394, read). FFF8B064 = this(FFF8A76C), clamped to 0-359 (0x0D0468, read); used for the second injection's angle by 0x0CB604 (read). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05B194 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 067394. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal)
table.description:
Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 40 BTDC (100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with late spark); identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. Second pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 0.5-180 BTDC (code 1080-1439, 0x0D023C, read), i.e. the compression stroke; 0.5-10 BTDC act as 10.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock 40 BTDC, and 100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with the spark target at 7 degrees ATDC or later. When used: Selected by FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) in 0x0D023C: this one while it is clear (read). Stock identical to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Injection angle FFF8B060 from rpm and FFF8A76B (0x0D023C, read), the second-injection angle in fuel mode 2 (0x0CB604, read). table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Stock boundaries are 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load) (this is boundary 1, stock 31.5 %). Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). 0x0DFA88 also sums it into the total knock correction FFF8A77B, whose only consumer (0x0DDBBC -> FFF8A770) is zero in stock (read). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one (most of the high-load map in stock); where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Stock 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 01C240 by the code that reads it (read). Address 022730. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 2, Channel 2)
table.description:
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 2 of 8 (index 1 of FFF8CDB0; enabled in stock: bit 1 of cal 0x1B97D is clear), on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 4 to 97 (raw); the sibling tables for channels 1, 7 and 8 (masked in stock) are all 0. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05BEAC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0681A0. Confidence: read.

For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 3 (Event 3), knock channel 2 of 8 (index 1 of FFF8CDB0; enabled in stock: bit 1 of cal 0x1B97E is clear), on the knock window where FFF8A7C4 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C1A0[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D4, gain curve cal 0x26F8F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 0 to 117 (raw); the sibling tables for channels 1, 7 and 8 (masked in stock) are all 0. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05BF4C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 068240. Confidence: read.

Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed; identical to the TGV Open table in stock. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections), and in stock the target is far lower, so raising this map at idle or when coasting does nothing.
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. The TGV Closed and TGV Open tables are identical in stock. Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 set (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. In stock the request at idle (about 6-8 degrees at 500-900 rpm, warm) is far below this map (19-28 degrees at 400-1000 rpm, 0.13-0.39 g/rev (10-30 % load)), and it stays below it when coasting (17 vs 34 degrees at 2000 rpm), so idle and coast timing are set by Closed-Pedal Timing Target and raising this map there has no effect (computed from stock data); lowering it below the target does take effect. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). AT/CVT warm-up fallback copy of Start Spark Target Run-Time Adder (Mode 1). Not used on this manual-transmission calibration, so it has no effect on a stock car. Stock identical to the manual table.
Details: When used: FFF8A7E2 bit 0 clear, FFF899D7 bit 0 set. Identical to 05D0D0 in stock. 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set, which is 0 in stock, so the Warm-Up Fallback tables are never used in stock (read). Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32 (both tables 0 in stock, so the normal request); in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set (clear in stock) A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0 (0 in stock). Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). All four sets are identical in stock.
