table.name: Boost Limit
table.description:
Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run. Stock 211 kPa absolute peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost.
Details: 0x1086F8 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A84F (raw) and FFF8A84E = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, where f is the target's baro/IAT factor: the compensated boost ceiling (read). The torque-model task 0x0C3D14 copies it to FFF8AFAE = A84E << 8 (0x0C3D0C, read). AFAE is the full-load manifold pressure of the throttle/torque model. Target MAP FFF8AF6A = (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this (0x0C2F0C). FFF8AF8A = Throttle Required Area column input AFA8 x this (0x0C3408). The pressure ratio AF6C = AF8A / this (0x0C2F9C) selects the high-pressure spark-compensation filter above 0.85 (all read). Also read by the airflow/torque model 0x111AB8 (role there not decoded). It is not an overboost cut; see Overboost Limit for that. Stock 211 kPa abs peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost. Raise it with Target Boost. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05CFC8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0693A0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Boost IAT Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Target Boost and Boost Limit by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change). Stock 0.78 at -40 F, 1.05 near 104 F, 0.96 from 140 F.
Details: 0x108778: FFF8B3B2 = 2 x Target Boost Baro Compensation x this x FFF8A84B / 128 (32768 = x1), the factor on the absolute boost target and Boost Limit (read). Stock 0.78 at -40 F, 1.05 near 104 F, 0.96 from 140 F. Implicit 16-point u8 table (boot lookup 0x71E0, axis 0..240 step 16) on FFF88663 = (IAT_c50 x 410 - 3972) / 256 from 0x06AF58, where IAT_c50 = FFF88662 = intake air temperature + 50 degC (the OBD IAT source, read); axis = -40.3 + 9.99 x n degC, shown in degF. 128 = x1.0. table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per step everywhere, i.e. no Stage 1 limit.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding; unused in stock (manual coding). AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock, 255 = x1) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Stock 24000 everywhere = 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per 10 ms, i.e. no Stage 1 limit (same as the high-gear cells of the Stage 2 AT/CVT Coding tables). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 0598BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 06535C. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 0.7-2.2 ft-lb (1-3 Nm) per step in gears 1-2, no limit in higher gears.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 with FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so unused in stock. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. A second shaping path (Path B) exists but is off in stock (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Stock 0.7-2.2 ft-lb (1-3 Nm) per pass in gears 1-2, 74 ft-lb (100 Nm, no limit) in higher gears. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F714. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05995C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0653FC. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:

table.description:

With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:

Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:

Details: When used: always. Overboost latch FFF84167 (0x0BE140, read): sets when MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit (the baro/IAT-compensated FFF8A851) + this, and releases when MAP < that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). While set (and no higher state) the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0B, the same state as the rev limiter (see Rev Limit RPM). In that state the throttle-side request is capped at once (Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base) by rpm, or the stage tables above 256 kPa abs); fuel is cut on all four cylinders every event only once the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 is also set (MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay, 2.0 s stock) or rpm reaches Rev Limit Full Cut RPM; spark is not retarded. table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold
table.description:
Vehicle speed above which the rev-limit fuel cut uses the Stage 1 / Stage 2 rpm values instead of the Full Cut pair. Stock 255 km/h can never be exceeded, so no effect in stock.
Details: When used: always, but stock never switches. Vehicle speed FFF99835 (km/h, a byte) above which the full-cut latch (part 2) uses Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) instead of Rev Limit Full Cut RPM / Reset RPM. Once at or below it, the speed must exceed this + Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis (saturating at 255) to switch (0x0BAEE2-0x0BAF0E). Stock 255 = never (the speed byte cannot exceed 255). Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 01DEEA by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: the counterpart of LF75404S 0x0BAE98, overrev function (seg_0x0C0000.c:7087): speed threshold 0243DA (+ hysteresis 0243DB), and while at or below it the set/reset rpm 02431C / 02431A (read); same structure as the reference. Address 0243DA. Confidence: read.

table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Stock 75 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Stock 192 = 75 %. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. table.name: Throttle Air Spark Compensation Limit
table.description:
Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Stock 1.5x at 22.5 degrees or more up to 3.1x at -15 degrees, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three.
Details: 0x0C37D8 (read): FFF8AFA8 = 32768 x (AF2C/AF64) x min(this(final timing FFF8A642), AF56)/8192; the result indexes Throttle Required Area 05A148. It caps the spark-efficiency air compensation (AF56, normally ~1.0) as a function of the actual final timing; stock 1.50x at >=22.5 deg up to 3.13x at -15 deg, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares its data (0x0107E8) with 05A124 and 05F414 (0x185FFC): editing one edits all three. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05A118 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: twins 0x0D23F8 (reads 065CC0) and 0x0D2498 (reads 065CCC) share data 0x0107E8; the parent calls 0x0D2498(FFF8B542) then 0x0D23F8(FFF8B540) as LF75404S calls 0x0C385C(AF2E -> AFAA, 05A124) then 0x0C37D8(AF2C -> AFA8, 05A118), and the 0x0D23F8 output FFF8B5BC feeds 0x0D3850, the Throttle Required Area (065CF0) reader, as AFA8 feeds 05A148 (read). The automatic port had 065CCC, the Alt Request twin (same data). Descriptor 065CC0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Stock EGR and non-EGR tables are identical.
Details: When used: every pass of the 0x110000 torque module. Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR). Stock: 14-49 ft-lb (19-66 Nm) at zero load, 260-306 ft-lb (352-415 Nm) at 2.81 g/rev (217 % load) from 2400 rpm (119 ft-lb, 162 Nm cap at 800 rpm); identical to the EGR table 05D64C. 0x118318 (DAM 1 set -> FFF8B490) and 0x1186A4 (DAM 0 set -> FFF8B4A2), called from 0x110000 with rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616, TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (read): closed = TGV-closed x (1 - w) + TGV-closed-EGR x w, open = TGV-open x (1 - w) + TGV-open-EGR x w with w = B290/256, result = closed x (1 - B3E8) + open x B3E8, all above the 16000 zero point (read; same blend as the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables in 0x0C0010). 0x10ED6C interpolates the two sets by DAM: FFF8B48A = B490 x DAM + B4A2 x (1 - DAM) with FFF811AE = DAM x 16 (read), and 0x118A40 subtracts (B490 - B4A2) x (1 - DAM) from the torque it reports as FFF8B4B2 (0.1 ft-lb, 0.1 Nm, 10000 = 0) (read). So these are the engine torque the ECU expects from the air charge, at full and at zero knock-learning advance (inferred from the DAM interpolation). They do not set the throttle or boost; they shape the estimated/reported engine torque (inferred). Axes: rpm FFF8CE9C x load % FFF8A616. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05D638 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) CORRECTION of the existing curated_LF79100P placement (069B1C, which is the DAM 0 set). 0x126960 is the first call (-> FFF8BB28, the B490/DAM 1 slot of the DAM interpolator 0x11E444, identical to LF75404S 0x10ED6C after normalisation); lookup 1 -> &DAT_069ACC (LF75404S 05D638). ROM: 069ACC 16x16 u16 data u16@03E70E; axes identical to LF75404S; data identical to LF75404S (0/256 cells differ), stock min/max 17522/49201 (LF75404S 17522/49201). Descriptor 069ACC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Below Idle Target)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while rpm is far below the idle target (2017+ and Forester builds). Has no effect on a stock car: the trigger is set to about 3000 rpm below idle target, so it never happens. Stock equal to the normal table.
Details: When used: Only while the below-idle latch (new in the Forester and 2017+ builds) is set: rpm - idle target <= cal 0x11AF4 (with hysteresis). Stock cal is about -3000 rpm, so it never sets and these tables are unused in stock (read cal, inferred effect). Stock data equal the normal tables. LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Torque Model Filter Multiplier A. Evidence: table new in 2017+ builds, read by 0x0D0D6C in state S2 when the latch FFF84250 is set (rpm FFF8D424 - idle target FFF8B8B2 <= cal 0x11AF4, hysteresis 0x11AF6); stock cal 0x11AF4 = -15360 raw (about -3000 rpm) so not used in stock (inferred); stock data equal to the 2015-equivalent table; Alt flag clear, TGV normal (read). Descriptor 065A3C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description:
Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Stock 1.0 flat. Leave alone.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S1: after combustion-mode change 4 -> 1, while in mode 1, FFF886AB bit 5 set and final timing above the spark target. Stock 1.0 flat. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 059EA0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0659DC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt)
table.description:
Alternate version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A, used when an unidentified flag is set. Leave alone unless you know the model.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGVs normal, A7E2 bit 0 set. Stock 0.375 to -20 degC, 1.5 at 0-30 degC, 1.9 at 60-80 degC, 0.9 above 90 degC. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 059EAC by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0D0D6C (= LF75404S 0x0C1EA8; same states, cals 0x107D6/0x10808/0x107D7) adds a latch FFF84250 in state S2: set when rpm FFF8D424 - idle target FFF8B8B2 <= cal 0x11AF4 (hysteresis cal 0x11AF6) (read); S2 then picks by Alt flag FFF8ADA2 bit 0, latch, TGV closed FFF8AE44 bit 4. Latch clear = the 2015 set (read: these keep the 2015 data addresses); stock cal 0x11AF4 = 0xC400 (-15360 raw, about -3000 rpm), so the latch is never set in stock (inferred); this = S2, Alt set, latch clear, TGV normal; data 0x010892 as LF75404S 059EAC (read). Descriptor 0659E8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt, Below Idle Target)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt) used while rpm is far below the idle target (2017+ and Forester builds). Has no effect on a stock car: the trigger is set to about 3000 rpm below idle target, so it never happens. Stock equal to the normal table.
Details: When used: Only while the below-idle latch (new in the Forester and 2017+ builds) is set: rpm - idle target <= cal 0x11AF4 (with hysteresis). Stock cal is about -3000 rpm, so it never sets and these tables are unused in stock (read cal, inferred effect). Stock data equal the normal tables. LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (Alt). Evidence: table new in 2017+ builds, read by 0x0D0D6C in state S2 when the latch FFF84250 is set (rpm FFF8D424 - idle target FFF8B8B2 <= cal 0x11AF4, hysteresis 0x11AF6); stock cal 0x11AF4 = -15360 raw (about -3000 rpm) so not used in stock (inferred); stock data equal to the 2015-equivalent table; Alt flag set, TGV normal (read). Descriptor 065A24. Confidence: read.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier A (TGV Closed)
table.description:
Version of Torque Model Filter Multiplier A used while the TGVs are closed. Identical to the TGV-normal table in stock.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGV closed (A881 bit 4), A7E2 bit 0 clear. Stock identical to 059E94. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 059ED0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0D0D6C (= LF75404S 0x0C1EA8; same states, cals 0x107D6/0x10808/0x107D7) adds a latch FFF84250 in state S2: set when rpm FFF8D424 - idle target FFF8B8B2 <= cal 0x11AF4 (hysteresis cal 0x11AF6) (read); S2 then picks by Alt flag FFF8ADA2 bit 0, latch, TGV closed FFF8AE44 bit 4. Latch clear = the 2015 set (read: these keep the 2015 data addresses); stock cal 0x11AF4 = 0xC400 (-15360 raw, about -3000 rpm), so the latch is never set in stock (inferred); this = S2, Alt clear, latch clear, TGV closed (read); the automatic port had 065A24, the Alt + latch table. Descriptor 065A0C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description:
Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead: this one is unused there in stock.
Details: 0x0C2AD8 (read): A644 = this(AF58, coolant); AF5E = max(1.0, AF58 x A644/256) is the spark compensation actually allowed and is the normal value of the cap AF56 in 0x0C37D8. Stock: 1.0 at AF58 = 1.0, 0.63-0.90 at 1.4-2.0 (0.63-0.80 at 2.0), at 5.0 from 0.37 (cold) to 0.90 (20 degC). Used while TGVs are not forced closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 clear). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 059FA8 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0D1798 (= LF75404S 0x0C2AD8) now selects by TGV closed FFF8AE44 bit 4 and the Alt flag FFF8ADA2 bit 0 (same flag as in the filter reader 0x0D0D6C): 4 tables, 16x16 instead of 8x8 (same inputs AF58-equivalent x coolant, u8 x/256), and multiplies by a new factor (default 64 = 1.0) (read); this = TGV normal, Alt clear: the 2015 path (Alt clear is the case 2015 had no table for; inferred), stock values = 2015 rows/cols re-gridded (read). Descriptor 065B50. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter (Alt)
table.description:
The live version of Spark Air Compensation Limiter on 2017+ ROMs: selected by a flag that is always set in stock, so edit this one there.
Details: When used: Selected in 0x0D2134 (LF79002P; same in LF79100P and LF9C100P) while FFF8AD5A bit 0 is set, which it always is in stock (Phase 11), so this is the table a stock 2017+ car uses; the non-Alt table is used only while that bit is clear (read). Used with the TGVs open. Same role and stock data as the non-Alt table. LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have; scaling and axes as Spark Air Compensation Limiter. Evidence: limiter reader 0x0D1798 (= LF75404S 0x0C2AD8) reads four 16x16 tables, selected by TGV closed and by FFF8AD5A bit 0 (always set in stock, Phase 11): this Alt table is the live one; corrected 2026-11-01 (the earlier note had the filter reader's below-idle latch) (read; stock data identical to the non-Alt tables). Descriptor 065B14. Confidence: read.

table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter Baro Factor
table.description:
Barometric-pressure factor on Spark Air Compensation Limiter (2017+ and Forester builds). Has no effect on a stock car: it is only used when a calibration switch is set, which is off in stock, and the data is flat 1.0.
Details: When used: only when the cal bit given below (bit 7) is set; otherwise the factor is fixed at 64 (x1.0) (read). Multiplies Spark Air Compensation Limiter: the allowed spark air compensation = (spark air compensation ratio) x limiter x this >> 14, floored at 1.0 (read, 2017 0x0D2134). Axes: the spark air compensation ratio (8192 = 1.0) and barometric pressure (kPa x 256). 64 = x1.0. Stock: cal bit clear and data flat 64, so no effect. New in the Forester and 2017+ builds. LF79100P: a table LF75404S does not have. Evidence: reader 0x0D1828: when cal 0x2AE09 bit 7 is set the factor = this table(spark air compensation ratio, barometric pressure), else 64 (read); stock cal byte 0x00 (bit clear), data flat 64 (read). Descriptor 065B64. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Area from Throttle Position (Airflow Model)
Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Initial, Neutral)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Gain Multiplier (Falling MAP, Recovery, Neutral)
Manifold Model Falling-MAP Initial Duration (TGV Closed)
Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain
Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock)
Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure; -1.0 in stock so the modelled flow turns negative. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. Stock 192 = -1.0 as a signed byte, so the modelled flow turns negative (out of the manifold) (read). Normally leave alone. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 02B06D by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 0334B9. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. Map A while no open-loop enrichment is active. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. FFF8C562 = S filtered (weight 05A578 while FFF8AFCC is rising, 05A5A0 while falling, by rpm x load); FFF8C564 = (U - S + fuel-cut term FFF8B040) filtered (weights 05A680 / 05A6A8 by air quantity FFF8B4D6 x FFF8B066); estimate FFF8AFD0 = FFF8C562 + FFF8C564, so in steady state FFF8AFD0 tends to Map B. 0x0CE854 enables Primary Open Loop Fueling while FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), and 0x0C5880 integrates 05A82C(FFF8AFD0) into FFF8C03C, the second enable path (read). Reading FFF8AFD0 as an exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate is inferred: the enriched maps are lower than the stoichiometric ones, retard raises the value (multiplier 0.75 at 25 degrees advanced to 1.2 at 20 degrees retarded) and the value gates the enrichment. Raising these maps brings Primary Open Loop Fueling in earlier (lower load); lowering them delays it. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05A564 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0663B4. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
2017+ / Forester version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Stock 1.0 at no drop to 0.7 at 30 C drop, the same for every stored temperature. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs, on a hot restart: coolant at start high enough (cals 0x4B638/0x4B639 = 10/110, i.e. the same >= 60 C, 50 C to stay test as LF75404S cals 0x4234C/D) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= cal 0x4B63B (130 = 80 C). 2017+/Forester replacement of the LF75404S 1D table A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (05F1E4), which these images do not have. LF79002P 0x1866D8 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x1802F4; stack arguments checked in the LF79002P disassembly: param_9 @72 = FFF81678, called at 0x18716A, read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature (K x 32) starts at max(FFF81678 x this(FFF81678, coolant drop)/256, min(IAT, coolant) (C150/C152)). table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder (Zero in Stock)

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, A table (weight w). Stock -11...30 degrees. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05E4BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 06AA14. Confidence: inferred.

How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 1 -> 6. Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set (manual coding, stock here) and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05C6F4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 068AC0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Cold Idle, Mode 4, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold. No effect on a stock car: the thresholds that enter this mode are 0 in stock, so it never occurs.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. Both cals are 0 in stock, so mode 4 never occurs in stock (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 024AF0 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Data at 02BCCC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version). Probably never used on a stock car: that fallback is switched off by a calibration setting in stock (inferred).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch, gated off in stock by cal 0x59134 bit0 = 0 (my research notes), so never used in stock (inferred from that trace). This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05C760 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 068B2C. Confidence: read.

table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate, Off in Stock)
CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Alternate, Off in Stock)
CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Flag Set, Alternate, Off in Stock)
Idle Base Air (Mode 5)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle (the warm-idle mode on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. At a settled warm idle the TGVs are normally commanded closed, so Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed) is probably the table in use: change both together, and together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) so idle feedback does not have to learn the difference. Stock hot value is about 1.9 % throttle.
Details: When used: idle mode 5, normal idle (the warm-idle mode of a manual car). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant; the TGV-closed set is used while FFF8A881 bit4. Hot stock mode-5 value 1536 (TGV normal) / 1408 (closed) -> ~1.9 % throttle. Change with the idle speed target so the feedback need not learn the difference. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC (lookup 0x7414, read). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 02503E by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: base-air reader 0x100FCC (= LF75404S 0x0F0D24): position 15 of its 25 implicit-axis lookups, as in LF75404S, same memory order of the A/B sets (read). Data at 02C21A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) and Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Stock hot value slightly below the TGV-open table.
Details: When used: idle mode 5, normal idle (the warm-idle mode of a manual car). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant; this TGV-closed table is used while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set. Hot stock mode-5 value 1536 (TGV open) / 1408 (closed) -> ~1.9 % throttle. Change with the idle speed target so the feedback need not learn the difference. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC (lookup 0x7414, read). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). LF79100P: located from LF75404S 024F5E by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: base-air reader 0x100FCC (= LF75404S 0x0F0D24): position 19 of its 25 implicit-axis lookups, as in LF75404S, same memory order of the A/B sets (read). Data at 02C13A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant right after a cold start (below 75 degC) until the car moves or the engine warms, and while stopped, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.

Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). table.name: A/C Idle Air Steady (A/C Load Sw On, Neutral Sw Off, Above 14 km/h)
table.description:

For the first 40 passes = 0.4 s (cals 0x35195/0x35194) the kick part is the Initial Kick table, then it falls by 256 raw = 128 base-air units per 10 ms (cals 0x35192/0x35190) toward the Steady table. Selectors (read): FFF88BC6 bit7 = discrete input FFF8A29C bit5 (pin PA8, active low; an A/C load / refrigerant-pressure switch, inferred) debounced 300 x 10 ms = 3.0 s (0x080A64, 0x08058A), FFF88ADA bit6 = discrete input FFF8A29E bit5 (neutral switch, pin PH5, confirmed by its P0851/P0852 monitor 0x06F436), vehicle speed FFF88BE8 (km/h x 17.8) above 14 km/h (cal 0x35196 = 249), held until below 4 km/h (249 - cal 0x35198 178). table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Stock: full (219) at the lowest input, empty at 2432 and above. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 0608A4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 06D0EC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06C768, read). ADC channel 9 (0xFFFFE852, untrimmed) -> FFF8939A, filtered by cal 0x590F0 into FFF8939E (cal 0x590EE replaces the input while FFF88BCA bit 2 or 3 is set) and looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF893A0 (degC + 50), read only by the charging-voltage control 0x136CD8 (temperature-compensated voltage targets); the unfiltered value gives FFF893A1, reported by SSM as x - 10 (0x11F0E8, read). Identity (inferred): its companion input ADC channel 4 (FFF89390, 0x06C554) is a linear signal centred on 2.5 V (FFF89396 = 12800 - 0.488 x (sample - 32768); SSM x/128 + 28 puts zero at 2.5 V, about -50 A per volt), i.e. a bidirectional battery current, read by charging control 0x136BC0 and idle 0x0EE338; the two inputs share their filter cal block and their range monitors (FFF88BCA bits 2-5, 0x0715B0-0x07175C) are both enabled by cal 0x57584 bit 4, which is clear in stock (monitors off). A current + temperature pair used only for charging is the battery sensor, so this is battery temperature. Stock: 100 C at 0.32 V, 20 C at 2.37 V, -40 C from 4.71 V (NTC). Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 0608B0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 06D0F8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description:
How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active. Stock about 130 s of heating at -40 C to about 90 s at 60 C.
Details: When used: while the engine runs (run state FFF8906B = 3). 0x1028D0 (read; called from 0x101CF0): FFF8A833 bit 7 is set (and held until the run state leaves 3) when the accumulated rear O2 heater drive FFF88E6E > this(coolant at start FFF88A46; the -40 C row is used when the coolant sensor is faulted, FFF88E28 bit 1), or when FFF8881E >= cal 0x4B900 (9437) for cal 0x4B904 (50) passes. Rear O2 identity: the heater output FFF9980E bit 2 is driven by 0x06EC70 for FFF8CE0B of every 24 40-ms passes, and 0x073570 monitors that output against FFF8CE0B into FFF89CB4 bits 0/1, the P0037 / P0038 (heater circuit, bank 1 sensor 2) monitor records (dtc_monitors slots 182 / 180, read). FFF88E6E sums FFF8CE0B every 40 ms (0x06ED92, read), so it is heater energy since start; FFF8CE0B = 0 while the heater is held off (initial delay from 0x608F4, high load, battery out of range; 0x06E7D8, read). FFF8881E = 2 x (ADC channel 11 - ADC channel 25) (0x1E0000 task, read); it is the oxygen-sensor signal that gates Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (0x0CAE40: FFF8881E < cal 0x14F5C, read), so the second path is 'sensor already reads rich' (inferred). FFF8A833 bit 7 feeds the catalyst/rear-O2 module 0x101CF0 (0x1023E0, 0x102B58) and the rear O2 diagnostics 0x1B8890 / 0x1B902C (P0137, result FFF8AD93 bit 7) and 0x123C68 (read). Meaning 'sensor ready / warmed up' inferred. Stock 26250 at -40 C falling to 18125 at 60 C start coolant; at 13.75 V with the default heater stage that is about 130 s and 90 s of heating (inferred, 200 counts/s). Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor being treated as ready. LF79100P: located from LF75404S 05CEB0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 069288. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level, by rpm and load, that confirms channel 1 of the P219A A/F imbalance monitor. It sets no code by itself; P219A needs both this and A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1 exceeded. Raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never). Stock off below 1500 rpm, above 4000 rpm and below 0.91 g/rev (70 % load).
Details: When used: once per combustion event (0x1908E4, crank-synchronous list 0x1E1D1C) while the P219A monitor runs (FFF8ACD1). Confirms channel 1 of P219A (A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1). 0x18E130 (read): threshold FFF8BC5E = this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616) x 05FCB0(coolant)/8192 x 05FCBC/128 (both 1.0 in stock) x 1.0 (float constants 1000/2^33 and 8.192, 0x18E23C / 0x18E248, read); x 100 instead (capped at 65535, so during that window any cell >= 336 can never be exceeded) until the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 has been unchanged for cal 0x4496E = 150 passes (1.5 s; FFF8ACCD bit 5, 0x1912B4) - the A/C-state stability bit 6 (0x191324, cal 0x436B2 = 0) is always set; 65535 while FFF88A2D bit 0; 05FC90 (all 65535) replaces it near standstill with the pedal released (FFF8ACCD bit 0: FFF88C64 bit 5 and speed < 2 km/h) and 05FC68 (all 65535) while FFF8AA3F is set. 0x18F14C sets FFF8ACC5 = 2 when the crank fluctuation FFF8BC5C - 0x8000 > threshold x 250/256 (so an event counts when the fluctuation exceeds 0.977 x the cell value). 0x18D180... count those events per cylinder (FFF8ACC2 = 1..4, cylinder inferred) into FFF8BC24/28/2C/30 and in total FFF8BC48; at the end of a 2000-event window (FFF8BC20 = cal 0x436F0) 0x18F364 judges FFF8ACC7 = 2 'rough' when a cylinder count > cal 0x436F4 (17) or the total > cal 0x436F6 (17) (with a cylinder share > cal 0x43704 = 0) (read). That latches FFF8ACD8 (0x191850). The channel 1 judgement 0x18F980 gives FFF8ACCB = 2 (exceeded, which sets FFF8ACCF bit 1 and through it the P219A result in 0x19198C) only when the A/F swing exceeded its reference (FFF8ACCE bit 4) AND FFF8ACD8 (or FFF8ACD4) is set; FFF8ACCB = 1 (passed) when the swing passed (FFF8ACCE bit 5, cal 0x436C0 = 1) (read). So the roughness test is a required confirmation: a channel 1 P219A needs both the A/F swing and this crank roughness. (The alternative pass by roughness, FFF8ACD5 and FFF8ACD9, cannot occur in stock: with cal 0x436EE = 0 the second window FFF8BC1E always matches, so FFF8ACC7 never reaches 4; read.) The largest count and its limit are also Mode $06 values FFF815CE / FFF815D0 (0x18EB24 / 0x18EBA8, test 0xDC in the 0x0A0000 reporter, read). Raising cells makes the confirmation harder (65535 = never), lowering makes it easier; it does not set a DTC by itself. Evidence: A/F imbalance threshold readers 0x192DB0 and 0x192EB8 (= LF75404S 0x18E130 / 0x18E250; same code: 1D lookup by FFF8xxxx, 2D lookup chosen by a flag and param_2, 1D byte lookup of param, product clamped to 7999.878 x 8.192; the 2017-style builds drop the 4th flag argument) are called in the same order as in LF75404S (Threshold 2 reader first, then Threshold 1) and write FFF8C332 / FFF8C334, copied to the next words by the 11-insn functions as LF75404S FFF8BC5E / FFF8BC60 (read). Threshold 1 = the table 0x192DB0 reads in the flag-clear, param_2-clear branch: 06C2B8 (as 0x18E130 reads 05FC7C). The automatic port left it unresolved (conflict between the code-identical siblings 0x192DB0 and 0x192EB8); stock data equal LF75404S 05FC7C (read). Descriptor 06C2B8. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never). Stock off outside 1500-4000 rpm and 0.91-2.07 g/rev (70-160 % load).

Evidence: A/F imbalance threshold readers 0x192DB0 and 0x192EB8 (= LF75404S 0x18E130 / 0x18E250; same code: 1D lookup by FFF8xxxx, 2D lookup chosen by a flag and param_2, 1D byte lookup of param, product clamped to 7999.878 x 8.192; the 2017-style builds drop the 4th flag argument) are called in the same order as in LF75404S (Threshold 2 reader first, then Threshold 1) and write FFF8C332 / FFF8C334, copied to the next words by the 11-insn functions as LF75404S FFF8BC5E / FFF8BC60 (read). table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit

scaling.category: mg fuel per cylinder (stock Injector Scaling)
scaling.units: mg (stoich fuel per cylinder per cycle)

scaling.category: base pulse (0.3 MPa reference, any Injector Scaling)

table.description:
Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling: stock it allows about 5 g of air per revolution, but lowering the injector flow figure (for example for E85) lowers the ceiling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.
Details: When used: always while running (every pass of 0x0B7E00, which computes load and the base fuel quantity, read). Upper limit of the base (stoichiometric) fuel quantity FFF8ADEA. 0x0B8030 (read) computes FFF8ADEA = air quantity FFF8C250 x Injector Scaling x 0.10266 / 14.7 / 4 / rpm x 0.125 (= 0.5587 x Injector Scaling x air per cylinder per cycle in g) and stores min(that, this) (0x0B80FC-0x0B8112: MOVU.W @0x23696, CMP/GE, read). The limited value is what the rest of the fuel path uses: the base pulse 0x0D15EC (FFF8C05C = 16 x FFF8ADEA x trims), before the enrichment/fuel factor 0x0D1528 and the flow compensation and latency 0x0D2BB8; the transient-fuel film model 0x0F5F84; the fuel load FFF8ADEE (0x0B895C); and the fuel-used accumulators 0x06B70E (read). Above the limit the base pulse stops rising with airflow, so the mixture goes lean as air keeps rising; enrichment is applied on top of the limited value and does not lift it (inferred from the order of the calls). The raw unit includes Injector Scaling, so the limit in air terms moves with it: air per revolution at the limit = this x 3.580 / Injector Scaling (raw) g/rev = this x reference injector flow [g/s] x 0.0004704. Shown in g/rev for stock Injector Scaling 2918 (2.61 g/s). Stock 4060 = 4.98 g/rev (2.49 g per cylinder per cycle, about 556 g/s at 6700 rpm), well beyond the stock turbo. With Injector Scaling at 1.74 g/s (fuel added for E85 by lowering the flow figure) the limit drops to 3.32 g/rev; below about 1.73 g/s it falls under the 3.31 g/rev (256 %) ceiling of engine load FFF8ADE4 (0x0B7EFC, read) and becomes the first limit reached. When you raise Injector Scaling raw (lower reference flow), raise this in proportion: new = 4060 x new raw / 2918 keeps 4.98 g/rev (u16, up to 65535). On AT/CVT codings, while FFF886AB bit 5 is set (meaning not decoded), the value is first smoothed by boot filter 0x6CEC with cal 0x23694 (stock 255); the limit applies on either path (read). 4060 in all eight images; the same code in LF78001H 0x0C1770, LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LV9N 0x0A6840 (read). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 023696 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: Base fuel quantity cap: the first-stage fuel quantity routine (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0B8030; LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LF78001H 0x0C1770) stores min(quantity, this cal); stock 4060 as in LF75404S (read, my research notes). Address 0274B2. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear (stock; the first argument of 0x0CE854), the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128, both all zero in stock (read). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0614F8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)

table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used. Stock never uses multiple injections (the quantity windows are disabled), so it has no effect.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Stock never uses multiple injections: the Double/Triple Injection Quantity Windows are 65535 (read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05AF94 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: five slot functions 0D9D60/0D9DD8/0D9E50/0D9EC8/0D9F40 write FFF8B4C2..B4CA in order (LF75404S 0CFC20..0CFE10 write FFF8B054..B05C), slot A 0D9D60 reads 061820 (read); the automatic placement 061870 duplicated Triple 3rd. table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description:
Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC. Stock pinned at the late limit, about 170 degrees after TDC. Has no effect in stock: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share is 0, so the pulse gets no fuel.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC; negative = AFTER that TDC (expansion stroke). This angle is an offset in segment 0, the 180 degrees after firing TDC (0x0CB604 mode 3 uses it with segment 0; the pulse-fit check 0x075D84 places it B064 + 1440 after the first pulse B062, read), so it is shown as -offset/2: clamped to 0 to -179.5 (0x0D0468, read), and -170 to -179.5 act as -169.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock pins at the -179.5 clamp (stored -170 at spark 24 BTDC only): a late expansion-stroke pulse, about 170 degrees ATDC in effect (its quantity is Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share, cal 0x2A3CA, which is 0 in stock, so stock fires no second pulse in this mode). Catalyst-heating mode = FFF8A85C 2 (0x109B4C, read): it maps to fuel mode 3 (0x108B08), in which the ignition target is FFF8A76C (0x0DA51C, read) and the injection angle is FFF8B062 (0x0CB394, read). FFF8B064 = this(FFF8A76C), clamped to 0-359 (0x0D0468, read); used for the second injection's angle by 0x0CB604 (read). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05B194 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 061A20. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal)
table.description:
Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 40 BTDC (100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with late spark); identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. Second pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 0.5-180 BTDC (code 1080-1439, 0x0D023C, read), i.e. the compression stroke; 0.5-10 BTDC act as 10.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock 40 BTDC, and 100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with the spark target at 7 degrees ATDC or later. When used: Selected by FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) in 0x0D023C: this one while it is clear (read). Stock identical to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Injection angle FFF8B060 from rpm and FFF8A76B (0x0D023C, read), the second-injection angle in fuel mode 2 (0x0CB604, read). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05B130 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0619BC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal)

First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 270 BTDC cold to 290 BTDC hot; identical to the TGV Closed table.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation
table.description:
Timing added (negative = retard) for hot intake air, by intake air temperature, scaled by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier. It is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744, but it reaches the fired timing through FFF8A645 (FFF8A645 -> FFF8A76A -> FFF8A76D -> FFF8A74B -> FFF8A744, 0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600 / 0x0D9E40, read). FBKC Maximum Retard
table.description:
Largest amount of timing feedback knock correction can pull. The live knock retard never goes below minus this value, and it applies to all cylinders at once. Raising it allows more protective retard. Stock about 12 degrees.

table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Stock boundaries are 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load) (this is boundary 1, stock 31.5 %). Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). 0x0DFA88 also sums it into the total knock correction FFF8A77B, whose only consumer (0x0DDBBC -> FFF8A770) is zero in stock (read). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one (most of the high-load map in stock); where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Stock 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 01C240 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0EC070, pair of 0x0E1C58 (ratio 1.00): position of the ref cal in the cell computation; all 12 boundary/hysteresis cals map 0x1C240..0x1C256 -> 0x1FACC..0x1FAE2 in order (read). Address 01FACC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description:
Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. The path is live in stock but both tables are flat 32, so it adds nothing.
Details: When used: while FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set; weight (16 - DAM)/16 (the DAM 0 table). 0x0D9D48 (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8) blends the two tables by DAM FFF811AE (0..16): FFF8A741 = (DAM 1 table x DAM + DAM 0 table x (16 - DAM))/16, 32 = no change; then 0x0D9B28 sets FFF8A73C = FFF8A741 when FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set (cal 0x32DEA != 0x5A as in stock), else 32, and 0x0DA600 adds FFF8A73C - 32 (0.5-degree units) to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (read). FFF8A8A3 bit 6 (0x11C04C, read) = combustion mode FFF8A85C = 4, coolant within cal 0x36502..0x36500 (all), DAM >= cal 0x364FE (0), FFF8A8A4 bit 6 set (the injection-timing high-pedal latch 0x11C0C4 that selects Injection Timing (High Pedal), 90 % / 85 % in stock; not the AVCS latch bit 7 used by Base Timing DAM Blend) and open-loop enrichment FFF8A684 <= (FFF8B32A - 32768)/128 (closed-loop target offset term). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (same as Base Timing DAM Blend). Unlike Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (Off in Stock), this path is live in stock, but both tables are flat 32, so it adds nothing. Stock 32 (0 degrees) everywhere. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05B588 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Descriptor 061ED4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D, Unused in Stock)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires. Unused in stock because every Secondary Knock Threshold is at maximum, so that detector never triggers. Stock about 1.4 degrees.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. Stock 4 counts = 1.41 degrees. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 01C277 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0ECE3C is the counterpart of 0x0E2BE4 (callsites has no pair for it; it is the only LF78001H function with the FBKC state machine: same s8 integrator FFF84A16 (ref FFF8491A), same state compares on FFF8AB7F (ref FFF8A79C) 0x10/0x0F/0x0E/0x0D/0x0C/8-9/7/6/5/4/3/2/1). Forester adds a gate FFF8AB55==0 on states 0x0E/0x0D only. Whole cal block ref 0x1C26E..0x1C288 -> 0x1FAFA..0x1FB14 (+0x388C, every reference in both functions consistent). subtracted in state 0x0D (read). Address 01FB03. Confidence: read.

Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 6. Stock 4 counts = 1.41 degrees. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. LF78001H: located from LF75404S 01C276 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0ECE3C is the counterpart of 0x0E2BE4 (callsites has no pair for it; it is the only LF78001H function with the FBKC state machine: same s8 integrator FFF84A16 (ref FFF8491A), same state compares on FFF8AB7F (ref FFF8A79C) 0x10/0x0F/0x0E/0x0D/0x0C/8-9/7/6/5/4/3/2/1). Forester adds a gate FFF8AB55==0 on states 0x0E/0x0D only. Whole cal block ref 0x1C26E..0x1C288 -> 0x1FAFA..0x1FB14 (+0x388C, every reference in both functions consistent). subtracted in state 6 (read). Address 01FB02. Confidence: read.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold (Off in Stock)
Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0) (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. It has no effect on a stock car: it is only used when a calibration switch is set to a specific value, which it is not in stock. 32 = no change. Stock +2 degrees at low rpm, varying to 0 from 4000 rpm; identical to its DAM 1 pair.
Details: When used: never in stock. Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). Off in Stock (read): FFF8A740 has two readers (ram_xref, instruction level): 0x0D9B28 uses it only when cal 0x32DEA == 0x5A ('Z'), and stock is 0x00, so FFF8A73C = FFF8A741 x 50 / 50 under FFF8A8A3 bit 6, else 32; and 0x0E0E44, whose output FFF8A777 bit 1 is read only by the same 0x0D9B28 branch (FFF8A777 readers: 0x0DF0B8 call args and the init 0x0DF59C). FFF8A73E/A73F have no other readers. So in stock neither table changes timing or any other output. With cal 0x32DEA = 'Z' the base timing term FFF8A73C would ramp toward A740 (cal 0x32DEC per pass) and enter the base timing sum FFF8A74B (0x0DA600). Stock flat across load and varying with rpm: 36 (+2 degrees) at 400-1200 rpm, 32 (no change) at 1600, 34 (+1) at 2000-2400, 36 (+2) at 2800-3600 rpm and 32 (no change) from 4000 rpm; identical to 05B560. Evidence: timing parent 0x0E9B8C calls the two code-identical 77-insn DAM blend readers as callees 21 and 22 (0x8A0 calls not counted), as LF75404S 0x0DF0B8 calls 0x0D9BD4 (Alternate: 05B560 DAM 1, then 05B54C DAM 0, output FFF8A73F) and 0x0D9D48 (Blend B: 05B574 DAM 1, then 05B588 DAM 0, output FFF8A741) as callees 20 and 21 (read). So 0x0E4C64 = Alternate (0x0D9BD4) and 0x0E4DB0 = Blend B (0x0D9D48). Phase 18 had put the Alternate entries on the Blend B reader's tables (061ED4/061EC0), now shared with the Phase 19 Blend B entries (port_sanity duplicate); stock data equal LF75404S 05B54C/05B560 (read). Descriptor 061E98. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Short Window)
table.description:
Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off); this is the active path in stock and drives FBKC states 7 / 0x0E (retard 0x1C275 / 0x1C274, 4 counts = 1.41 degrees). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4); all 65535 in stock, so it never fires (states 6 / 0x0D). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. Knock Threshold (0x0E77E0, read): looked up by rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500) and load FFF8A616 for each event slot; set A (05C104/118/12C/140) while FFF8A7C1 = 0, i.e. the nominal (short) window; set B (05C154/168/17C/190) while A7C1 = 1, i.e. the extended window (0x0E77E0 at 0x0E7836-0x0E784A; flag polarity read in 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30, the earlier names had the two sets swapped). A higher value needs a larger knock signal to count as knock (less sensitive). Set A (nominal / short window). LF78001H: located from LF75404S 05C104 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: knock threshold reader 0x0F11A4 (= LF75404S 0x0E77E0, same body): branch param_2==0 reads 062A70/062A84/062A98/062AAC into FFF8C64C/C64E/C650/C652 (ref 05C104/118/12C/140 -> FFF8C1CC..C1D2, Threshold A Events 1-4), else branch 062AC0/062AD4/062AE8/062AFC (ref 05C154..190, Threshold B Events 1-4) (read); data regions agree (A data 01F21E.., B data 02B926.. as ref 01B992../027416..); Event 1 = first call. Descriptor 062A70. Confidence: read.

Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds.
