Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) and Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Stock hot value slightly below the TGV-open table.

FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time
table.description:

Axes: start type FFF8A6E8 x coolant FFF88A44. Stock: active only at -40 degC and from 70 degC up (zeros between = Start/End 0, so the staged air is decayed to 0 at once; checked as real data, the five data blocks are contiguous 160-byte arrays with no overlap) - a hot-restart air bump (inferred). table.description:
Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions). Stock 5 degC.
Details: TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum (hysteresis cal 0x37B46 - 16384, stock 409 = 1 C), requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. Confirms channel 1 of P219A (A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 1). 0x18E130 (read): threshold FFF8BC5E = this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616) x 05FCB0(coolant)/8192 x 05FCBC/128 (both 1.0 in stock) x 1.0 (float constants 1000/2^33 and 8.192, 0x18E23C / 0x18E248, read); x 100 instead (capped at 65535, so during that window any cell >= 336 can never be exceeded) until the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 has been unchanged for cal 0x4496E = 150 passes (1.5 s; FFF8ACCD bit 5, 0x1912B4) - the A/C-state stability bit 6 (0x191324, cal 0x436B2 = 0) is always set; 65535 while FFF88A2D bit 0; 05FC90 (all 65535) replaces it near standstill with the pedal released (FFF8ACCD bit 0: FFF88C64 bit 5 and speed < 2 km/h) and 05FC68 (all 65535) while FFF8AA3F is set. 0x18F14C sets FFF8ACC5 = 2 when the crank fluctuation FFF8BC5C - 0x8000 > threshold x 250/256 (so an event counts when the fluctuation exceeds 0.977 x the cell value). 0x18D180... count those events per cylinder (FFF8ACC2 = 1..4, cylinder inferred) into FFF8BC24/28/2C/30 and in total FFF8BC48; at the end of a 2000-event window (FFF8BC20 = cal 0x436F0) 0x18F364 judges FFF8ACC7 = 2 'rough' when a cylinder count > cal 0x436F4 (17) or the total > cal 0x436F6 (17) (with a cylinder share > cal 0x43704 = 0) (read). That latches FFF8ACD8 (0x191850). The channel 1 judgement 0x18F980 gives FFF8ACCB = 2 (exceeded, which sets FFF8ACCF bit 1 and through it the P219A result in 0x19198C) only when the A/F swing exceeded its reference (FFF8ACCE bit 4) AND FFF8ACD8 (or FFF8ACD4) is set; FFF8ACCB = 1 (passed) when the swing passed (FFF8ACCE bit 5, cal 0x436C0 = 1) (read). So the roughness test is a required confirmation: a channel 1 P219A needs both the A/F swing and this crank roughness. (The alternative pass by roughness, FFF8ACD5 and FFF8ACD9, cannot occur in stock: with cal 0x436EE = 0 the second window FFF8BC1E always matches, so FFF8ACC7 never reaches 4; read.) The largest count and its limit are also Mode $06 values FFF815CE / FFF815D0 (0x18EB24 / 0x18EBA8, test 0xDC in the 0x0A0000 reporter, read). Raising cells makes the confirmation harder (65535 = never), lowering makes it easier; it does not set a DTC by itself. Stock 615-775 at 1500 rpm (live in normal driving; only the 1.5 s neutral-settling window makes cells >= 336 unreachable), 200-556 at 3000 rpm, 138-388 at 3500 rpm, 163-220 at 4000 rpm for loads 0.91-2.07 g/rev (70-160 %); 65535 (off) below 1500 rpm, above 4000 rpm and below 0.91 g/rev (70 % load). LV9N101C: located from LF75404S 05FC7C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 053294. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 2
table.description:
Crankshaft roughness level that confirms channel 2 of the P219A monitor (paired with A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). Lower than Threshold 1, so more sensitive. Sets no code by itself; raising cells makes a fault harder (the maximum value = never). Stock off outside 1500-4000 rpm and 0.91-2.07 g/rev (70-160 % load).
Details: When used: as A/F Imbalance Monitor Crank Roughness Threshold 1, for channel 2 of P219A (A/F Imbalance Monitor Swing Threshold 2). 0x18E250 (read): same gating and scaling (x 05FD10(coolant)/8192 x 05FD1C/128, both 1.0) into FFF8BC60 -> FFF8BC64; 0x18F0F8 sets FFF8ACC4 = 2 on an exceedance; per-cylinder counters FFF8BC32..BC44 (0x18D4C8...) and the 2000-event window judgement FFF8ACC6 (0x18F1A0: a cylinder count > cal 0x436FC (17) or the total > cal 0x436FE (17) gives 2 'rough') latch FFF8ACDB (0x191920). The channel 2 judgement 0x18F928 gives FFF8ACCA = 2 (exceeded: FFF8ACCF bit 3 -> P219A result) only when the swing exceeded (FFF8ACCE bit 2) AND FFF8ACDB (or FFF8ACD6) is set; = 1 (passed) when the swing passed (FFF8ACCE bit 3, cal 0x436C1 = 1) (read). Mode $06 values FFF815D2 / FFF815D4 (0x18EFCC / 0x18F050, read). Stock 237-283 at 1500 rpm, 82-370 at 3000 rpm, 82-200 at 3500 rpm, 82-98 at 4000 rpm (lower = more sensitive than threshold 1), loads 0.91-2.07 g/rev (70-160 %); 65535 (off) elsewhere. table.name: EGR Enable
table.description:
Master switch for EGR (set in stock). Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off variants of base timing, closed loop target and throttle tables become the live ones (inferred).
Details: Set in stock. One of the EGR enable conditions computed by 0x0FAAFC (FFF8A811 bit 0), with coolant, rpm and load windows, engine running and normal combustion mode (read). Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off table variants (Base Timing (EGR Off, ...), Closed Loop Target (..., EGR Off), the non-EGR Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables) become the live ones (inferred). Evidence: (read) 0x0E4ADC (pair of 0x0F94A8) stores (0x2A9DA & 0x20) at @(40,R15) and passes it as param_8 of 0x0E60D8 (pair of 0x0FAAFC); stack slot checked in the disassembly (param_8 = param_5 slot + 4, as ref), tested at @(91,R15) in 0x0E60D8 like ref; also passed to 0x0E5260 (ref 0x0F9C3C). Same byte as the transmission-coding bit, as in ref. Stock byte 0x20: bit5 set (ref 0x20). Address 02A9DA bit 5 (value 32). Confidence: read.

table.name: Transmission Coding: From Input Port
table.description:
When set, the manual/automatic coding is read from a hardware input instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT. Clear in all stock images; leave clear.
Details: Clear in all stock images. When set, the transmission coding (FFF886AB bit 7) is taken from a latched input-port bit (FFF80238 bit 7, set once port bit FFF8A2A4 bit 7 is seen) instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT (read, 0x06A38C). Leave clear. LV9N101C: located from LF75404S 02F796 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) 0x05CA7C (pair of 0x06A38C; LV9N100F/101C code identical 0x50000-0x11CB66) reads the byte through literal 0x05CF04 = 0x0002A9DA, tests 0x40: set -> latch FFF80238 bit7 / port bit, clear -> 0x2A9D8 bit1 (literal 0x05D19C), same structure as ref. Stock byte 0x20: bit6 clear (ref 0x20). Address 02A9DA bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B
table.description:
Enables the second (Path B) tip-in torque shaping. Clear in stock, and all Path B tables are 0 and its rpm limit is 0, so setting only this bit does essentially nothing. Leave clear unless you calibrate the whole Path B set.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0x01). The torque module 0x0BE694 passes this bit to the rise shaping 0x0BB958 (BLD.B #6 at 0x0BF3D0, stack argument 11, read), and the torque monitor call passes it to 0x1877B4 (read). When set, Path B of the target-torque rise shaping can act (all "Target Torque Rise ... (Path B, ..., Off in Stock)" tables), and a request below Path B Start Torque passes unshaped. Path B also needs rpm <= cal 0x22A04, which is 0 in stock, so setting only this bit changes nothing but the Start Torque bypass (and Path B tables are all 0 ft-lb in stock, so that bypass never triggers). Leave clear unless the whole Path B set is calibrated. Bit 7 of the same byte is a separate switch passed to another torque routine (seg_0x0B0000.c:9252). LV9N101C: located from LF75404S 023704 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: the rise-shaping function 0x0A9F14 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0BB958; it reads the Path B pedal multiplier table) is called once, with (cal 0x1FCF8 & 0x40) as its only bit-6 cal flag argument, as LF75404S passes cal 0x23704 bit 6 (read); stock byte 0x01 (bit 6 clear). Address 01FCF8 bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description:
When set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate, Off in Stock) probably replaces the normal open loop fueling strategy. Clear in stock; leave clear unless you have filled that table.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0x8F). Passed by the open-loop fueling readers 0x0CE854 and 0x0CE5E8 (read): when set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate, Off in Stock) is used in place of the base + DAM-scaled knock additive strategy (inferred). table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description:
When set, Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock) is used while the cams are probably not yet under control. Clear in stock; leave clear.
Details: Clear in stock. 0x11E308 uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock) only when this bit is set and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear (read); FFF8A83B bit 7 = AVCS ready (inferred). table.name: Base Timing: Pedal-Released Tables Enable
table.description:
Set in stock: with the pedal released, Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed/Open) replaces the normal EGR Active/Off base timing tables. Clear it to use the normal base timing tables off-throttle too.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 1
table.description:

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 1 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 1's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D168C writes FFF8C060 = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1E4 (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B1FC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04EE50. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Strategy byte = injections per cycle (FFF8A69E, 0x0CF3EC, read): this one applies with one injection (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6A3 by 0x0CF630 (read). Injector 1's quantity (0x0D168C) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A69F equals 1 (read). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05ADE8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04EAC8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Injector 2/4 Rail Pressure Offset
table.description:
Pressure offset added to measured rail pressure before looking up Injector Flow Compensation (Injectors 2/4), by rpm and load; probably the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor. Stock all 0 (no effect).
Details: 0x06D43A (read): FFF89222 = sat(rail pressure FFF88886 + this(rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616)), interpolated by 0x00671C (descriptor 0x0608E4: data, u16 axis, u8 axis, 16, 16; row = rpm, read). FFF89222 indexes the injector flow compensation 05A844 used only for injectors 2 and 4 (0x0CB0C8, read); injectors 1 and 3 use 05A838 with FFF88886. Likely the pressure difference of the rail without the sensor (inferred from the boxer layout). Signed, in the rail-pressure unit. Stock all 0 (2015, 2016). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 0608E4 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x05FA8C-area reader calls the 2D lookup through pointer 0x5FBC8 = 0x053A5C with rpm and load, adds the rail pressure and saturates, the same code as LF75404S 0x06D43A (read); descriptor {data, rpm axis u16, load axis u8, 16, 16} read from the image. Descriptor boot 053A5C. Confidence: inferred.

Rail pressure target while an injector-driver fault (P062D / P2146) is active; stock 0.35 MPa, which appears to mean no high-pressure pumping. No effect on a healthy car.

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit

scaling.category: mg fuel per cylinder (stock Injector Scaling)
scaling.units: mg (stoich fuel per cylinder per cycle)

scaling.category: base pulse (0.3 MPa reference, any Injector Scaling)

table.description:
Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling: stock it allows about 5 g of air per revolution, but lowering the injector flow figure (for example for E85) lowers the ceiling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.
Details: When used: always while running (every pass of 0x0B7E00, which computes load and the base fuel quantity, read). Upper limit of the base (stoichiometric) fuel quantity FFF8ADEA. 0x0B8030 (read) computes FFF8ADEA = air quantity FFF8C250 x Injector Scaling x 0.10266 / 14.7 / 4 / rpm x 0.125 (= 0.5587 x Injector Scaling x air per cylinder per cycle in g) and stores min(that, this) (0x0B80FC-0x0B8112: MOVU.W @0x23696, CMP/GE, read). The limited value is what the rest of the fuel path uses: the base pulse 0x0D15EC (FFF8C05C = 16 x FFF8ADEA x trims), before the enrichment/fuel factor 0x0D1528 and the flow compensation and latency 0x0D2BB8; the transient-fuel film model 0x0F5F84; the fuel load FFF8ADEE (0x0B895C); and the fuel-used accumulators 0x06B70E (read). Above the limit the base pulse stops rising with airflow, so the mixture goes lean as air keeps rising; enrichment is applied on top of the limited value and does not lift it (inferred from the order of the calls). The raw unit includes Injector Scaling, so the limit in air terms moves with it: air per revolution at the limit = this x 3.580 / Injector Scaling (raw) g/rev = this x reference injector flow [g/s] x 0.0004704. Shown in g/rev for stock Injector Scaling 2918 (2.61 g/s). Stock 4060 = 4.98 g/rev (2.49 g per cylinder per cycle, about 556 g/s at 6700 rpm), well beyond the stock turbo. With Injector Scaling at 1.74 g/s (fuel added for E85 by lowering the flow figure) the limit drops to 3.32 g/rev; below about 1.73 g/s it falls under the 3.31 g/rev (256 %) ceiling of engine load FFF8ADE4 (0x0B7EFC, read) and becomes the first limit reached. When you raise Injector Scaling raw (lower reference flow), raise this in proportion: new = 4060 x new raw / 2918 keeps 4.98 g/rev (u16, up to 65535). table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear (stock; the first argument of 0x0CE854), the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128, both all zero in stock (read). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05AC6C by its caller in the decompiled code (read). table.description:
Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used. Stock never uses multiple injections (the quantity windows are disabled), so it has no effect.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Stock never uses multiple injections: the Double/Triple Injection Quantity Windows are 65535 (read). Injection angle for FFF8B054 (0x0C589C via 0x0CFC20-style helper, read): computed only while FFF99844 is 2 or 3 (otherwise a fixed 0x1FE) (0x0CFC20, read). 0x0CB394 uses B054 for two injections and B058 for three in normal fuel mode (read); the Double Injection tables cover 1100-3200 rpm, the Triple Injection tables 600-1300 rpm. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05AF94 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04EC74. Confidence: inferred.

Details: Share of the fuel in the first of two injections (0x0D05D8 -> FFF8B068 -> FFF8A6D1, read); the second gets the rest (0x0D0D50). Limited by FFF8A6DA (read). All zero in stock. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B1A0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04EDF4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description:
Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC. Stock pinned at the late limit, about 170 degrees after TDC. Has no effect in stock: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share is 0, so the pulse gets no fuel.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC; negative = AFTER that TDC (expansion stroke). This angle is an offset in segment 0, the 180 degrees after firing TDC (0x0CB604 mode 3 uses it with segment 0; the pulse-fit check 0x075D84 places it B064 + 1440 after the first pulse B062, read), so it is shown as -offset/2: clamped to 0 to -179.5 (0x0D0468, read), and -170 to -179.5 act as -169.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock pins at the -179.5 clamp (stored -170 at spark 24 BTDC only): a late expansion-stroke pulse, about 170 degrees ATDC in effect (its quantity is Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share, cal 0x2A3CA, which is 0 in stock, so stock fires no second pulse in this mode). Catalyst-heating mode = FFF8A85C 2 (0x109B4C, read): it maps to fuel mode 3 (0x108B08), in which the ignition target is FFF8A76C (0x0DA51C, read) and the injection angle is FFF8B062 (0x0CB394, read). FFF8B064 = this(FFF8A76C), clamped to 0-359 (0x0D0468, read); used for the second injection's angle by 0x0CB604 (read). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B194 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04EDE8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal)
table.description:
Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 40 BTDC (100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with late spark); identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. Second pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 0.5-180 BTDC (code 1080-1439, 0x0D023C, read), i.e. the compression stroke; 0.5-10 BTDC act as 10.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock 40 BTDC, and 100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with the spark target at 7 degrees ATDC or later. When used: Selected by FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) in 0x0D023C: this one while it is clear (read). Stock identical to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Injection angle FFF8B060 from rpm and FFF8A76B (0x0D023C, read), the second-injection angle in fuel mode 2 (0x0CB604, read). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B130 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04EDAC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base (TGV Normal)
table.description:
First-pulse (intake stroke) injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2 and the start sequence, by rpm and coolant, limited to 180.5-360 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 270 BTDC cold to 290 BTDC hot; identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. First pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 180.5-360 BTDC (code 720-1079, 0x0D00A8, read), i.e. the intake stroke. Stock 270 BTDC cold to 290 BTDC hot, the same window as the main injection. When used: while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear. 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C, args read): in fuel state FFF8906B 2/3, FFF8B05E = this(rpm FFF8CD54, coolant FFF88A44) + 05B068(rpm, load) x 05B090(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + 05B0E0(spark FFF8A76B, coolant) (all three 0 or neutral in stock), clamped 720..1079; under FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 only this table; cal 0x38448 bit 5 (clear) would force cal 0x1208A. 0x0CB394 uses FFF8B05E - 720 as the injection angle of cylinders in injector mode 2 (fuel mode 2 = combustion modes 1 and 3, the catalyst-heating phase 2 / start sequence) (read). Axes 850-1600 rpm x coolant. Stock 900 cold to 860 hot, identical to the TGV Closed table. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B0B8 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0BD540 is the counterpart of 0x0D00A8 (callsites has no pair; called from 0x0B35C8 in the 0x0D00A8 slot with the same args less the last flag; same 0x2D0..0x437 clamp and 0x4CE default). It reads the base 0x4ED70 (FUN_18e134 with p3/p9, = 05B0B8 via FUN_1b0680) and the adders 0x4ED48/0x4ED5C/0x4ED84 (= 05B068/05B090/05B0E0); it has no param_11 (TGV closed) branch, so no 05B0CC/05B0A4/05B07C/05B0F4 counterparts (disassembly loads only these four descriptors). Data-class address confirmed (read). Descriptor 04ED70. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Adder (TGV Normal)
Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Base Spark Adder (TGV Normal)
table.description:
Correction by spark target and coolant to the phase 2 first-pulse angle, TGVs not closed; positive = later. Stock all 0, no effect.
Details: When used: catalyst-heating phase 2 first pulse, TGVs not forced closed (0x0D00A8, read). 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, cal 0x38448 bit 5, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, coolant FFF88A44, spark target FFF8A76B, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B05E), read): in fuel states 2/3 FFF8B05E = Base(rpm, coolant) + Base Adder(rpm, load) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + Base Spark Adder(spark, coolant), clamped to code 720-1079 (180.5-360 BTDC); with FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 set only the Base is used (read). This table is the adder by spark target FFF8A76B (rows, ign_raw) and coolant FFF88A44 (columns); it is not scaled. Units (FU_UNITS): added to the code angle, so a positive value moves the pulse LATER (fewer degrees BTDC), x/2 degrees (fu_units_inj_delta_later). Stock all 0. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B0E0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: first-pulse reader 0x0BD540 (= LF75404S 0x0D00A8) (read): cVar5 = FUN_0018dbf8(&04ED84, (int)param_10, param_9), added with the 04ED48 x 04ED5C product, the same call and arguments as LF75404S FUN_001ae250(&05B0E0, (int)param_10, param_9); this build has only the one (TGV Normal) set. 16x16 s8 data at 0x015987, s8 axis 0x015976 (bytes equal LF75404S 0x0160DE: -30..48), u16 axis 0x032F98; stock data all zero, equal to the reference. Descriptor 04ED84. Confidence: inferred.

Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle)
table.description:
Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection). Used with the pedal released and the car stopped. Stock 40 % almost everywhere; the three tables are identical.
Details: When used: fuel mode 2, pedal released and stopped, FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x10A604 (read) writes FFF8A85F = this(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF88A44; coolant at start FFF88A46 instead if cal 0x2996C bit 3, clear in stock) at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8); 0 when FFF8A657 bit 7 or FFF8A857 bit 7, cal 0x2A340 (51) if cal 0x2996C bit 4 (clear). 0x0D0A7C-0x0D0C14 copy A85F into the per-injector split FFF8A6D6...A6D9 when that injector's fuel mode FFF8A858...A85B is 2 (combustion modes 1 and 3, 0x108B08) (read); the second pulse gets A6D6/256 of the quantity (0x0D1FB8) at the Catalyst Heating Phase 2 injection angle B060, and A6D6 = 0 means no second pulse (my research notes) (read). Selection: pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A389 (2 km/h) -> 05D1A0 (05D1C8 if FFF899D7 bit 0), otherwise 05D1B4 (read). The same data blocks are also read by 0x10BF88 through descriptors 05D224 / 05D238 / 05D24C, so one entry covers both. Stock 102 (40 % in the second pulse) everywhere except 0 (single injection) at 1200-1600 rpm with coolant at the 40 degC end of the axis (axis -30...40 degC); the three tables are identical. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05D1A0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0F596C (pair of 0x10A604; identical in both): if (param_6 && p7 < cal 0x262FD) -> 0x50C44 else 0x50C58 (= ref bVar1 -> 05D1A0 else 05D1B4); there is no third branch (ref param_11 selector -> 05D1C8) and the disassembly loads only 0x50C44/0x50C58. Idle-gated branch (read). Descriptor 050C44. Confidence: read.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Readiness Idle Stability Time
table.description:
How long the idle must be steady (pedal released, normal running) before the catalyst-heating readiness flag sets, by rpm change and rpm versus idle target. Its exact role after that is inferred. Stock 80-115 passes when rpm is steady, up to 500 when falling or low.
Details: When used: combustion mode 4 with the pedal released (FFF88C64 bit 5), only because cal 0x2996C bit 2 is set (stock) (0x10AAB0, read). The readiness flag FFF8A856 bit 5 (0x10AAB0 -> abStack, read) additionally needs a pass counter FFF853E6 (reset whenever the conditions drop) to reach this(rpm change FFF8CEA6, rpm - idle target FFF8B236), i.e. the idle has to be steady for this many passes (disassembly 0x10AB72-0x10AB98: R5 = CEA6, R6 = CE9C - B236, read). The other readiness conditions are the coolant window of Catalyst Heating Coolant Minimum/Maximum shrunk by cal 0x29A5C and further cals (my research notes). A856 bit 5 is used by the mode logic 0x109B4C (with a timer from 05D170, 0x109AA8) (read); its exact role there (re-entry of the heating modes) is inferred. Stock 80-115 passes when rpm is steady and at/above target, up to 500 passes when rpm is falling fast or below target. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05D204 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 050C94. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.
Details: When used: every 80 ms pass (0x0D60FC, read): A70A = this(target purge flow FFF8B0C0, manifold vacuum FFF8CDFA). The final duty is A713 + (100 % - A713) x this, with A713 = Purge Valve Minimum Duty (0x0D6118, read), and 0 when this is 0. B0C0 = purge rate x air quantity FFF8B4D6 / 256, in the air-quantity unit (read). Stock: 0 at zero flow; at 1.07 g/s 100 % with no vacuum, 48 % at 6.7 kPa, 16 % at 53 kPa; 100 % from 8.6 g/s. Higher vacuum needs less duty for the same flow. Purge module (inferred: canister purge): 0x0D4E78 (80 ms task 0x1E1560) and 0x0D4C14 (20 ms task 0x1E0AE8) (read). Chain (read): purge rate A70C (limits A6FD/A70F, ramp A709, cut B0A0) -> purge flow B0C0 = A70C x air FFF8B4D6/256 -> valve duty A70A = 05B314(B0C0, vacuum) -> A70B with minimum duty A713 -> A707 -> timer E channel 22 (0x1D98D6); A707 is also checked by the circuit monitor 0x072090 (driver status FFF88BF4 bits 10/11). table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Stock boundaries are 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load) (this is boundary 1, stock 31.5 %). Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). 0x0DFA88 also sums it into the total knock correction FFF8A77B, whose only consumer (0x0DDBBC -> FFF8A770) is zero in stock (read). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one (most of the high-load map in stock); where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Stock 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 01C240 by the code that reads it (read). Address 018CFC. Confidence: read.

Stock boundaries are 2,400 / 4,400 / 7,200 / 10,000 / 11,000 / 12,000 rpm; only the first two fall inside the 6,700 rpm rev limit, so just three rpm ranges are used. Keep them in increasing order.

Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). 0x0DFA88 also sums it into the total knock correction FFF8A77B, whose only consumer (0x0DDBBC -> FFF8A770) is zero in stock (read). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one (most of the high-load map in stock); where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). rpm boundary. table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 0)
table.description:
Timing offset added to base timing in a high-pedal, enrichment-limited condition in one combustion mode, blended with Base Timing DAM Blend B (DAM 1) by DAM; this table applies at DAM 0. 32 = no change, 0.5-degree steps. The path is live in stock but both tables are flat 32, so it adds nothing.
Details: When used: while FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set; weight (16 - DAM)/16 (the DAM 0 table). 0x0D9D48 (per combustion event, from 0x0DF0B8) blends the two tables by DAM FFF811AE (0..16): FFF8A741 = (DAM 1 table x DAM + DAM 0 table x (16 - DAM))/16, 32 = no change; then 0x0D9B28 sets FFF8A73C = FFF8A741 when FFF8A8A3 bit 6 is set (cal 0x32DEA != 0x5A as in stock), else 32, and 0x0DA600 adds FFF8A73C - 32 (0.5-degree units) to the base timing sum FFF8A74B (read). FFF8A8A3 bit 6 (0x11C04C, read) = combustion mode FFF8A85C = 4, coolant within cal 0x36502..0x36500 (all), DAM >= cal 0x364FE (0), FFF8A8A4 bit 6 set (the injection-timing high-pedal latch 0x11C0C4 that selects Injection Timing (High Pedal), 90 % / 85 % in stock; not the AVCS latch bit 7 used by Base Timing DAM Blend) and open-loop enrichment FFF8A684 <= (FFF8B32A - 32768)/128 (closed-loop target offset term). Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (same as Base Timing DAM Blend). Unlike Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (Off in Stock), this path is live in stock, but both tables are flat 32, so it adds nothing. Stock 32 (0 degrees) everywhere. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05B588 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04F1DC. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D, Unused in Stock)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires. Unused in stock because every Secondary Knock Threshold is at maximum, so that detector never triggers. Stock about 1.4 degrees.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. Stock 4 counts = 1.41 degrees. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 01C277 by the code that reads it (read). Address 018D33. Confidence: read.

table.name: FLKC Counted-Cell Learned Value Threshold (Off in Stock)
Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0) (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. It has no effect on a stock car: it is only used when a calibration switch is set to a specific value, which it is not in stock. 32 = no change. Stock +2 degrees at low rpm, varying to 0 from 4000 rpm; identical to its DAM 1 pair.
Details: When used: never in stock. Weighted (16 - DAM)/16. 0x0D9BD4 (read): FFF8A73F = ((16 - DAM) x 05B54C + DAM x 05B560) / 16 in the 32-offset half-degree frame, DAM = FFF811AE (0..16), tables by rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4. 0x0D9CA0: FFF8A73E = (A73F + FFF8A73B - 32) x FFF8B0D2 / 256 + 32, and FFF8A740 = A73E when FFF8A8A5 bit 4 is set, else A73D (the 05B574/05B588 path) (read). table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 2, Channel 2)
table.description:
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 2 of 8 (index 1 of FFF8CDB0; enabled in stock: bit 1 of cal 0x1B97D is clear), on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). table.name: Boost Limit
table.description:
Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run. Stock 211 kPa absolute peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost.
Details: 0x1086F8 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A84F (raw) and FFF8A84E = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, where f is the target's baro/IAT factor: the compensated boost ceiling (read). The torque-model task 0x0C3D14 copies it to FFF8AFAE = A84E << 8 (0x0C3D0C, read). AFAE is the full-load manifold pressure of the throttle/torque model. Target MAP FFF8AF6A = (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this (0x0C2F0C). FFF8AF8A = Throttle Required Area column input AFA8 x this (0x0C3408). The pressure ratio AF6C = AF8A / this (0x0C2F9C) selects the high-pressure spark-compensation filter above 0.85 (all read). Also read by the airflow/torque model 0x111AB8 (role there not decoded). It is not an overboost cut; see Overboost Limit for that. Stock 211 kPa abs peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost. Raise it with Target Boost. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05CFC8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 050B0C. Confidence: read.

On the AT/CVT coding this is the whole requested-torque map for this drive mode (Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default) is then ignored); unused on manual cars. Edit it, and its Monitor copy, when tuning an AT/CVT car.
Details: When used: whenever FFF88ADA bit 7 (manual-transmission coding) is clear, i.e. on the AT/CVT coding. The A/B weight FFF8AE26 (0x0B9C78) starts at 0 and its step cals 0x22FBE/0x22FC0 are 0, so it stays 0 and the output is this table alone; the matching non-AT/CVT table is then ignored (read). FFF88ADA bit 7 is set on the manual coding, so this table is unused on manual cars. Driver-requested torque from rpm and pedal (0x0BB670, read): FFF8AEB4 = A x FFF8AE26/32768 + B x (1 - FFF8AE26/32768), torque above the zero point, into FFF8AEB4; FFF8AE26 ramps between 0 and 32768 under a condition (0x0B9C78). Table B of map set 2 = Drive Mode 1, Default (0x0BDBD8 combines the four sets by the drive-mode byte FFF8A8C1 and per-mode scale cals 0x1FAFE-0x1FB00; SI-Drive positions (inferred 2026-11-02 from the stock maps of the SI-Drive cars LF78001H and LV9N101C, using S# > S > I in requested torque for a given pedal): mode 4 = Sport Sharp (its Forester map reaches full torque by half pedal), mode 2 = Sport, mode 3 = Intelligent (least torque for a given pedal in both images), mode 1 = the default used when no valid SI-Drive request is received, and the only set on cars without SI-Drive (the WRX MT images have identical mode 1-3 maps)). All six tables of sets 1-3 are identical in stock. KEEP Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor) identical (inferred safety copy). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05981C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04D7C0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT, Monitor)
table.description:
Monitor copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT): keep identical to it or expect a throttle plausibility fault. Used only on the AT/CVT coding.
Details: When used: Monitor copy; keep identical. Byte-for-byte copy of Requested Torque (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT) (data and axes) in separate storage, read by a second module (0x1873C4/0x1874BC/0x1875BC/0x1876BC, rpm x FFF88FE2, same A-then-B lookup order and weight structure, into FFF8BBAE/BBB2/BBB6/BBBA). Almost certainly the electronic-throttle torque monitor: change it together with the primary map or expect a throttle/torque plausibility fault (inferred). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05F5E8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 052C90. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 2, Sport)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 4, Sport Sharp)
Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per step everywhere, i.e. no Stage 1 limit.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding; unused in stock (manual coding). AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock, 255 = x1) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Stock 24000 everywhere = 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per 10 ms, i.e. no Stage 1 limit (same as the high-gear cells of the Stage 2 AT/CVT Coding tables). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 0598BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04D860. Confidence: inferred.

Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 0.7-2.2 ft-lb (1-3 Nm) per step in gears 1-2, no limit in higher gears.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 with FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so unused in stock. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. A second shaping path (Path B) exists but is off in stock (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Stock 0.7-2.2 ft-lb (1-3 Nm) per pass in gears 1-2, 74 ft-lb (100 Nm, no limit) in higher gears. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F714. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05995C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 04D900. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 01DEDE by the code that reads it (read). Address 01A99A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:
Overboost limit by rpm, compensated for baro and intake temperature like the boost target. Boost 26.7 kPa over it for 2 s sets the overboost flag, and 33 kPa over it starts the overboost cut (throttle cap, then a full fuel cut once the flag is set). Raise it when raising boost targets (stock 211 kPa absolute peak). Note: the boost-control pressure reading stops at about 269 kPa absolute, so an Overboost Limit above about 236 kPa absolute (269 minus the 33 kPa cut margin) can never trigger the overboost cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768 (read; cal 0x290A8 = 1 would use a fixed value, 0 in stock). Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. The flag makes the state-0x0B cut a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Rev Limit RPM); on its own, outside state 0x0B, it reduces nothing. It also feeds a diagnostic 0x1B8310. Stock 211 kPa abs peak, the same as Boost Limit from 2,000 rpm. Raise it with Target Boost. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05CFD4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 050B18. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 2 Hold MAP

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description:

table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:
Boost above Overboost Limit plus this enters the overboost cut state: the throttle is capped at once, and fuel to all cylinders is cut only if the 2-second overboost flag is also set. Stock 33 kPa.

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
table.description:

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
table.description:

table.name: External Torque Limit Baro Factor (Off in Stock)
External Torque Limit IAT Factor (Off in Stock)
Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (1 Cylinder)
table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Stock 75 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Stock 192 = 75 %. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Stock EGR and non-EGR tables are identical.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description:
Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Stock 1.0 flat. Leave alone.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S1: after combustion-mode change 4 -> 1, while in mode 1, FFF886AB bit 5 set and final timing above the spark target. Stock 1.0 flat. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 059EA0 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: 0x0AFD40 (= LF75404S 0x0C1EA8) has 7 inputs, no TGV-closed flag (2015 param 8, FFF8A881 bit 4, is not passed: caller seg 0x0B0000 line 1534) and reads 5 tables: S2 -> 04DDE4 / 04DDFC (Alt), S1 -> 04DDF0, S3 -> 04DE14 / 04DE08 (Alt) (read); S1 table (read); the automatic port had it by data only. Descriptor 04DDF0. Confidence: inferred.

Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGVs normal, A7E2 bit 0 set. Stock 0.375 to -20 degC, 1.5 at 0-30 degC, 1.9 at 60-80 degC, 0.9 above 90 degC. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, A table (weight w). Stock -11...30 degrees. table.name: EGR Timing Advance (TGV Closed)

FFF8A769 = FFF8A767 when FFF8A775 bit 2 is set (all four injectors in a 2- or 3-injection strategy, 0x0FAABC), else FFF8A763 (0x0DD454, read). It can never lift the fired timing above the Base Timing (EGR Active) maps. Axes rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8ADE4 (400-6400 rpm, 10-240 %; rows above 32768 are padding). Stock up to +13.5 degrees at 800-4800 rpm, 0.39-0.78 g/rev (30-60 % load). Byte-identical to EGR Timing Advance (Multi-Injection, TGV Closed) in stock. TGV Coolant Minimum
table.description:
Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions). Stock 5 degC.
Details: TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum (hysteresis cal 0x37B46 - 16384, stock 409 = 1 C), requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay (05D384, by vehicle speed; stock 1 s at standstill, 2 s from 4 km/h). States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is clear. Stock 18432 = 5 degC. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 037A44 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: CORRECTED (auto 032690 wrong). 0x0F8E10 (pair of 0x10D93C, ratio 0.91), disassembly 0x0F8F4A..0x0F8F5E: one unconditional read MOV.L @(0x0F90E0,PC)=0x00032692, MOVU.W, minus hysteresis W[0x32792] (= ref 0x37B46) when latch FFF853EE is set, compared with coolant param_1 (read). Following cals 0x32694/0x32696/0x32698 sit where ref has 0x37A48/0x37A4A/0x37A4C, so the 2015 LV9N block has one coolant minimum, not two. 0x32690 is not referenced anywhere (no literal in the ROM, no decompiler reference); it holds 0x00C8, the tail of a preceding 0x00C8 run. Address 032692. Confidence: read.

table.description:
How long the brake must be pressed over a held accelerator, by pedal position and speed, before brake override starts cutting the pedal signal (above 7 km/h). Stock 2 s at light pedal, 0.5 s from 60 % pedal. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while the VDC brake-pressure signal is valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4); 05F2E0 (200 = 2 s, flat) replaces it otherwise. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x1832C4 (read, args checked in the assembly): override request FFF8AC91 bit 1 sets when the time FFF8BADA since the brake was applied while the accelerator was already pressed (FFF8AC90 bit 6, 0x1831EC) reaches this(pedal FFF88EE6, speed FFF8AC95), with speed >= cal 0x43472 (7 km/h) and either pedal >= 05F2C0 (1.1 %) or a deceleration-confirmed brake (FFF8AC91 bit 2). FFF8AC91 bit 1 (or bit 0, the brake-switch path 0x183680) sets the active flag FFF8AC8F bit 0 (0x183B68), which starts the pedal-limit ramp. Stock 200 passes (2.0 s) at 11 % pedal; 1.25-1.5 s at 23 %; 0.75-1.0 s at 40 %; 0.5 s from 60 % pedal. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 05F2CC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 052974. Confidence: inferred.

Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 (65535 = no filter in stock) -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V (identical to IAT 2). LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 060850 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0539D4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06B304, read). ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 (no filter in stock) -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. Probably the thermistor of the manifold TMAP sensor (inferred from its use as the manifold air temperature): when fitting a different TMAP / MAP sensor with its own thermistor, change these temperature values. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock identical to IAT 1. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 06085C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0539E0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) a warm-up model from cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2 replaces it. Range faults: P0117 below Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0118 above Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25.7 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V. Change only when fitting a different sensor. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 060874 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0539F8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). Oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (input 7 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed) is filtered by cal 0x56F76 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88AE4 and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC). Output unit 256 x (degC + 50), read: FFF88E24 = (output - 0xA00) x 256 / 205 and OBD PID 0x5C reports FFF88E24 x 205 / 65536 = degC + 40. FFF88E24 / FFF88E26 is the oil temperature of the AVCS and idle tables (oil_temp_obd axis). Range faults: P0197 below Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0198 above Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock identical to the coolant curve. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 060880 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 053A04. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description:
Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling. Identical to A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich) in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while FFF88AFB bit 4 is clear: the A/F signal is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37 (window -800..1000 with hysteresis 333, 0x0843F8, read); gain cal 0x571F0 = 2. Identical to Near Stoich in stock; edit both together. 0x06C1A8 (read): the A/F sensor signal FFF88B2E is looked up here (boot lookup 0x6A0C) into FFF88AF6, the measured lambda of the closed loop (B308 = 43194 x 32768 / FFF88AF6, 0x0FF3CC). Stock lambda 1.00 at signal -25...0. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 06088C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 053A10. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description:
Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain. Shares its axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range) and is identical to it in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while the A/F signal is within about lambda 0.90-1.37 (FFF88AFB bit 4 set, 0x0843F8, read); higher gain cal 0x571F1 = 9 (gain reading inferred). Second A/F sensor table in 0x06C1A8 (read); shares the axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range). Identical to it in stock; edit both together. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 060898 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 053A1C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Stock: full (219) at the lowest input, empty at 2432 and above. LV9N100F: located from LF75404S 0608A4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 053A28. Confidence: read.
