table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 0.7-2.2 ft-lb (1-3 Nm) per step in gears 1-2, no limit in higher gears.
Details: When used: drive mode 3 with FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so unused in stock. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 2. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. A second shaping path (Path B) exists but is off in stock (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Stock 0.7-2.2 ft-lb (1-3 Nm) per pass in gears 1-2, 74 ft-lb (100 Nm, no limit) in higher gears. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F700. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 059948 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 007D78. Confidence: inferred.

Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 01DEDE by the code that reads it (read). Address 02440E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut RPM
table.description:

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:
Overboost limit by rpm, compensated for baro and intake temperature like the boost target. Boost 26.7 kPa over it for 2 s sets the overboost flag, and 33 kPa over it starts the overboost cut (throttle cap, then a full fuel cut once the flag is set). Raise it when raising boost targets (stock 211 kPa absolute peak). Note: the boost-control pressure reading stops at about 269 kPa absolute, so an Overboost Limit above about 236 kPa absolute (269 minus the 33 kPa cut margin) can never trigger the overboost cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768 (read; cal 0x290A8 = 1 would use a fixed value, 0 in stock). Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. The flag makes the state-0x0B cut a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Rev Limit RPM); on its own, outside state 0x0B, it reduces nothing. It also feeds a diagnostic 0x1B8310. Stock 211 kPa abs peak, the same as Boost Limit from 2,000 rpm. Raise it with Target Boost. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05CFD4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00BDC0. Confidence: read.

Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 01DE86 by the code that reads it (read). Address 0243B6. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description:
Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables). Set in stock; cleared, the limiter is probably fuel-cut only.
Details: Set in stock. With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this. Stock 0 kPa.

Stock 0. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 01DEF6 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 024426. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)
table.description:

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the vehicle-speed limiter. Set in stock; leave it set.
Details: Set in stock. Same as Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut for limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed limiter) (0x0DD568, read). Bits 5 and 4 do the same for states 0x19 and 0x1A (not decoded); state 0x1B always uses the normal target. Leave set. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 0239AE by the code that reads it (read). Address 02AC62 bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the rev limiter and overboost cut instead of retarding it. Set in stock; leave it set.
Details: Set in stock (byte 0xF0). In limit state 0x0B (rev limiter, overboost cut) 0x0DD568 sets the spark angle FFF8A76A to the normal spark target FFF8A72A instead of base timing FFF8A645 minus Torque Reduction Spark Retard (asm 0x0DD5F8-0x0DD62A, read), so the limiter does not retard the spark. Cleared, the full cut would ask for about 34 degrees of retard (ratio floor cal 0x2FDE4 = 102, inferred from the table). Leave set. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 0239AE by the code that reads it (read). Address 02AC62 bit 7 (value 128). Confidence: read.

table.name: External Torque Limit Baro Factor (Off in Stock)
External Torque Limit IAT Factor (Off in Stock)
Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (1 Cylinder)
table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Stock 75 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Stock 192 = 75 %. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 023D53 by the code that reads it (read). Address 02B007. Confidence: read.

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (2 Cylinders)
table.description:
Below this share of current torque, two cylinders in four are cut. Also sets the second decel fuel cut stage. Stock 50 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 2 cylinders are cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. The rev limiter and the overboost full cut use a zero cap (ratio 0, 4 cylinders) and do not depend on them. Stock 128 = 50 %. Further gating in 0x0C1AC8 (read): the ratio comparison also runs outside those states while FFF8A63B bit 0 or FFF899EC bit 1 / bit 4 is set; while FFF89BFE bit 2 is set (a fault latch from 0x09FE44, meaning not decoded) the count is instead taken from cals 0x23D58-0x23D5F by rpm FFF8CD62 and speed FFF99835 (not yet defined) and overrides both this ratio and the Fail-Safe Rev Limit; and with engine state FFF99844 = 4, or FFF8A65F bit 7 set while FFF89066 bit 0 is clear, the count is cal 0x38248 (the cylinder count, 4), i.e. all cylinders. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 023D54 by the code that reads it (read). Address 02B008. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Intake-temperature factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp. Has no effect on a stock car because the base step is 0. Stock all 1.0.
Details: 0x0C30F8: FFF8AF7E = cal 0x11ACE x this(IAT) x 05A080(baro) >> 14, the per-pass step of the AF9C throttle offset ramp (0x0C3700). cal 0x11ACE = 0, so inactive in stock; all 1.0. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. Evidence: (from LF9C100P) three look-alike readers 0x0CB4A4/0x0CB4F4/0x0CB544 (= LF75404S 0x0C30F8/0x0C3150/0x0C31A8), told apart by their gain cal (0x11ACE / 0x11AD0 / 0x1080E, same addresses as 2015) and call order, and they keep the 2015 data addresses (read): IAT table of 0x0CB4A4 (cal 0x11ACE), data 0x011ADC as LF75404S 05A074 (read); the automatic port had 0085F0, which is the third reader 0x0CB544 (cal 0x1080E, = 05A0A4). table.name: Throttle Air Spark Compensation Limit
table.description:
Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Stock 1.5x at 22.5 degrees or more up to 3.1x at -15 degrees, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three.
Details: 0x0C37D8 (read): FFF8AFA8 = 32768 x (AF2C/AF64) x min(this(final timing FFF8A642), AF56)/8192; the result indexes Throttle Required Area 05A148. It caps the spark-efficiency air compensation (AF56, normally ~1.0) as a function of the actual final timing; stock 1.50x at >=22.5 deg up to 3.13x at -15 deg, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares its data (0x0107E8) with 05A124 and 05F414 (0x185FFC): editing one edits all three. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05A118 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) twins 0x0CBAD0 (reads 008664) and 0x0CBB70 (reads 008670) share data 0x0107E8; the parent calls 0x0CBB70(FFF8C37C) then 0x0CBAD0(FFF8C37A) as LF75404S calls 0x0C385C(AF2E -> AFAA, 05A124) then 0x0C37D8(AF2C -> AFA8, 05A118), and the 0x0CBAD0 output FFF8C3F6 feeds 0x0CCF50, the Throttle Required Area (008694) reader, as AFA8 feeds 05A148 (read). The automatic port had 008670, the Alt Request twin (same data). Descriptor 008664. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Stock EGR and non-EGR tables are identical.
Details: When used: every pass of the 0x110000 torque module. Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR). Stock: 14-49 ft-lb (19-66 Nm) at zero load, 260-306 ft-lb (352-415 Nm) at 2.81 g/rev (217 % load) from 2400 rpm (119 ft-lb, 162 Nm cap at 800 rpm); identical to the EGR table 05D64C. 0x118318 (DAM 1 set -> FFF8B490) and 0x1186A4 (DAM 0 set -> FFF8B4A2), called from 0x110000 with rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616, TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (read): closed = TGV-closed x (1 - w) + TGV-closed-EGR x w, open = TGV-open x (1 - w) + TGV-open-EGR x w with w = B290/256, result = closed x (1 - B3E8) + open x B3E8, all above the 16000 zero point (read; same blend as the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables in 0x0C0010). 0x10ED6C interpolates the two sets by DAM: FFF8B48A = B490 x DAM + B4A2 x (1 - DAM) with FFF811AE = DAM x 16 (read), and 0x118A40 subtracts (B490 - B4A2) x (1 - DAM) from the torque it reports as FFF8B4B2 (0.1 ft-lb, 0.1 Nm, 10000 = 0) (read). So these are the engine torque the ECU expects from the air charge, at full and at zero knock-learning advance (inferred from the DAM interpolation). They do not set the throttle or boost; they shape the estimated/reported engine torque (inferred). Axes: rpm FFF8CE9C x load % FFF8A616. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05D638 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) CORRECTION of the existing curated_LF9C100P placement (00C530, which is the DAM 0 set). 0x120EB8 is the first call (-> FFF8C96C, the B490/DAM 1 slot of the DAM interpolator 0x118654, identical to LF75404S 0x10ED6C after normalisation); lookup 1 -> &DAT_00C4E0 (LF75404S 05D638). ROM: 00C4E0 16x16 u16 data u16@03EB52; axes identical to LF75404S; data identical to LF75404S (0/256 cells differ), stock min/max 17522/49201 (LF75404S 17522/49201). Descriptor 00C4E0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description:

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, A table (weight w). Stock -11...30 degrees. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05E4BC by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) intake target function 0x15F9C0 (= LF79002P 0x1646AC): each target 2D table plus its own coolant offset x coolant factor 00D3F4, weighted by the barometric blend w (Altitude = w, Sea Level = 1-w); Normal vs High Pedal by the high-pedal flag; TGV-closed set blended by the TGV weight. How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 2 -> 7. p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05C640 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00B3EC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (Cold Idle, Mode 4, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold. No effect on a stock car: the thresholds that enter this mode are 0 in stock, so it never occurs.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. Both cals are 0 in stock, so mode 4 never occurs in stock (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 024AF0 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Data at 02BE84. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version). Probably never used on a stock car: that fallback is switched off by a calibration setting in stock (inferred).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch, gated off in stock by cal 0x59134 bit0 = 0 (my research notes), so never used in stock (inferred from that trace). This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. table.name: CAN Idle Speed Request (Alternate, Off in Stock)

CAN Idle Speed Request Remap (Flag Set, Alternate, Off in Stock)
Idle Base Air (Mode 5)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle (the warm-idle mode on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. At a settled warm idle the TGVs are normally commanded closed, so Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed) is probably the table in use: change both together, and together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) so idle feedback does not have to learn the difference. Stock hot value is about 1.9 % throttle.
Details: When used: idle mode 5, normal idle (the warm-idle mode of a manual car). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant; the TGV-closed set is used while FFF8A881 bit4. Hot stock mode-5 value 1536 (TGV normal) / 1408 (closed) -> ~1.9 % throttle. Change with the idle speed target so the feedback need not learn the difference. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC (lookup 0x7414, read). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 02503E by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) base-air reader 0x0FAEFC (= LF75404S 0x0F0D24): position 15 of its 25 implicit-axis lookups, as in LF75404S, same memory order of the A/B sets (read). Data at 02C3D2. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) and Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Stock hot value slightly below the TGV-open table.

Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC (lookup 0x7414, read). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. table.name: Post-Start Staged Air Start Time

Stock: active only at -40 degC and from 70 degC up (zeros between = Start/End 0, so the staged air is decayed to 0 at once; checked as real data, the five data blocks are contiguous 160-byte arrays with no overlap) - a hot-restart air bump (inferred). table.name: EGR Upstream Pressure Estimate
table.description:
Estimated pressure upstream of the EGR valve (probably exhaust side) by rpm and load. The difference to manifold pressure sets the modelled EGR flow and decides whether EGR may be enabled. Stock about 101 kPa at idle up to 170 kPa at high rpm and load.

Reading it as the exhaust-side (upstream) pressure is inferred; stock 152 (101.3 kPa) at idle up to 255 (170 kPa) at high rpm and load. EGR controller task 0x0F94A8 (read). That this is external EGR is inferred: its commanded output FFF8A81B is the OBD PID 0x2C (Commanded EGR) source and FFF88A1C (actual position) feeds PID 0x2D (EGR error) (0x1717C8, 0x1715F0, read). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05CB3C by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read code, inferred choice) LF9C100P has no single-table counterpart of 0x0FA760: FFF8BC51 (fed to 0x102AC4 = the 0x0F943C counterpart and to 0x104210 param_13, as FFF8A81D in LF75404S) is written by 0x103DC0, which looks up 00B91C (adder), 00B944 (baro multiplier), 00B930, 00B908 in that order (LF75404S: 05CB50, 05CB64, 05CB3C) and returns (00B930 x w + 00B908 x (65536-w)) / 65536 + adder term, w = FFF8C8C4. w is set by 0x1150A0: it ramps to 0xFFFF while FFF8BCBA bit4 is clear and to 0 (floored by table 00C0FC) while it is set. FFF8BCBA bit4 sits in the slot of LF75404S FFF8A881 bit4 (TGV flag, docs Phase7/11) in the calls of 0x1036DC/0x1037B8 (pairs of 0x0FA10C/0x0FA1F8) (read). So 00B930 is the third lookup, as 05CB3C is, and the full-weight table with bit4 clear; 00B908 (the layout placement) is the bit4-set blend partner (inferred). Both 16x16 u8, rpm/load axes 03514E/03516E, stock identical to each other and to LF75404S 05CB3C (152..255). Suggest adding 00B908 as a second, separately named table. Descriptor 00B930. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Minimum coolant temperature for the TGVs to close (probably; part of the TGV close conditions). Stock 5 degC.
Details: TGV request logic 0x10D93C (read): the request byte FFF8A888 is 3 unless all of these hold: coolant FFF88A44 at or above TGV Coolant Minimum (hysteresis cal 0x37B46 - 16384, stock 409 = 1 C), requested torque FFF8AEE2 (0x0BA868, Nm = x/80 - 200) below the rpm-based TGV Torque Threshold (it must fall below the Enter table and then rise above the Exit table to clear), air quantity FFF8B4D6 below TGV Air Quantity Maximum (Enter 0x37A4A, Exit 0x37A48), and FFF8A88D = 0. When they hold, FFF8A888 = 1, or 2 if the intake air temperature FFF88A48 is below TGV IAT Threshold (vehicle speed) or FFF88E28 bit 0/2 is set; FFF8A888 = 2 also while combustion mode FFF8A85C is below cal 0x37B48. State 1 requests TGV close: it runs the timer FFF8B3E0 (0x10C3D0) and FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set once the timer reaches TGV Close Delay (05D384, by vehicle speed; stock 1 s at standstill, 2 s from 4 km/h). States 2 (close blocked: cold intake air, FFF88E28 bit 0/2, or combustion mode below cal 0x37B48) and 3 (close conditions not met) reset the timer, so the TGVs stay open (read). Which threshold pair is used depends on FFF8A8C1 (1, 2, 3 or other) and FFF8A8A2 bit 5 (not identified). Each threshold is table(rpm FFF8CE9C) + TGV Torque Threshold Offset(rpm, FFF88AE6) - 16000, so the offset table is centred on 16000 (0 ft-lb). Used while FFF899D7 bit 0 is clear. Stock 18432 = 5 degC. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 037A44 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x10D93C->0x116F70 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x037A44 (1 reference(s), votes {'040940': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x040940 is accessed as u16. Stock 18432 (LF75404S 18432). Matches the layout address. Address 040940. Confidence: read.

table.description:
How long the brake must be pressed over a held accelerator, by pedal position and speed, before brake override starts cutting the pedal signal (above 7 km/h). Stock 2 s at light pedal, 0.5 s from 60 % pedal. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while the VDC brake-pressure signal is valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4); 05F2E0 (200 = 2 s, flat) replaces it otherwise. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x1832C4 (read, args checked in the assembly): override request FFF8AC91 bit 1 sets when the time FFF8BADA since the brake was applied while the accelerator was already pressed (FFF8AC90 bit 6, 0x1831EC) reaches this(pedal FFF88EE6, speed FFF8AC95), with speed >= cal 0x43472 (7 km/h) and either pedal >= 05F2C0 (1.1 %) or a deceleration-confirmed brake (FFF8AC91 bit 2). FFF8AC91 bit 1 (or bit 0, the brake-switch path 0x183680) sets the active flag FFF8AC8F bit 0 (0x183B68), which starts the pedal-limit ramp. Stock 200 passes (2.0 s) at 11 % pedal; 1.25-1.5 s at 23 %; 0.75-1.0 s at 40 %; 0.5 s from 60 % pedal. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05F2CC by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) brake-override set function 0x1864AC (= LF75404S 0x1832C4) (read): same code (a 2D lookup without arguments, the 2D lookup(param_3, param_4) compared with param_2, a 1D lookup(param_4)); called from 0x184FE8 as callee 36 of 44 (0x8A0 calls not counted), right after the Brake Override Recovery Time reader, as 0x1832C4 is in 0x181B38; its 2D argument table is 00E454. The automatic code pick 00E490 is the 2D table of the next reader 0x18682C (= LF75404S 0x183680, table 05F308, whose stock data are flat 200): the code-identical sibling. stock data equal LF75404S 05F2CC (read). table.description:

table.name: Gear Advice Consumption Map (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Fuel consumption map by torque and rpm (probably g/kWh) for a gear-shift advice function that picks the most economical gear. One table edits all three copies. No effect on a stock car: the gear advice function is switched off by a calibration setting.
Details: When used: never in stock (cal 0x57585 bit 3 clear). Gear advice module 0x116A0C (read; called at seg_0x110000.c:1208 with cal 0x57585 bit 3, which is clear in stock 0x73, so the function returns at once and never reads its tables). With the bit set it takes the current power (torque x rpm / 9549.3), the engine speed in the gear below (FFF8B434, gear FFF8A8BA = gear - 1, 0x114360) and in the gear above (FFF8B436, gear FFF8A8BC = gear + 1, 0x1143CC), looks up the consumption map at the three points and advises the gear with the lowest value (FFF85678 / FFF85679, biases cal 0x36E4E/0x36E50 = 3 %). 'Alternate' tables are used when FFF8A8C3 = 2. Descriptors 05D4D8, 05D504 and 05D518 share this data block (037352): 05D4D8 at the current torque FFF8B468 = DAM-blended torque FFF8B48A - FFF8A8CC x 128 (0x1161DC) and rpm, 05D504 / 05D518 at the torque needed for the same power in the lower / upper gear (read). One entry edits all three. Stock minimum 7703 (241 g/kWh as x/32, inferred) at 2000 rpm / 133 ft-lb (180 Nm); 10000-14000 at light load or high rpm; rows from 280 ft-lb (380 Nm) repeat. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05D4D8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C380. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 (65535 = no filter in stock) -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V (identical to IAT 2). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 060850 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633A4. Confidence: read.

table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06B304, read). ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 (no filter in stock) -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. Probably the thermistor of the manifold TMAP sensor (inferred from its use as the manifold air temperature): when fitting a different TMAP / MAP sensor with its own thermistor, change these temperature values. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock identical to IAT 1. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 06085C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633B0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) a warm-up model from cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2 replaces it. Range faults: P0117 below Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0118 above Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25.7 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V. Change only when fitting a different sensor. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 060874 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633C8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). Oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (input 7 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed) is filtered by cal 0x56F76 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88AE4 and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC). Output unit 256 x (degC + 50), read: FFF88E24 = (output - 0xA00) x 256 / 205 and OBD PID 0x5C reports FFF88E24 x 205 / 65536 = degC + 40. FFF88E24 / FFF88E26 is the oil temperature of the AVCS and idle tables (oil_temp_obd axis). Range faults: P0197 below Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0198 above Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock identical to the coolant curve. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 060880 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633D4. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description:
Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling. Identical to A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich) in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while FFF88AFB bit 4 is clear: the A/F signal is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37 (window -800..1000 with hysteresis 333, 0x0843F8, read); gain cal 0x571F0 = 2. Identical to Near Stoich in stock; edit both together. 0x06C1A8 (read): the A/F sensor signal FFF88B2E is looked up here (boot lookup 0x6A0C) into FFF88AF6, the measured lambda of the closed loop (B308 = 43194 x 32768 / FFF88AF6, 0x0FF3CC). Stock lambda 1.00 at signal -25...0. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 06088C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633E0. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description:
Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain. Shares its axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range) and is identical to it in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while the A/F signal is within about lambda 0.90-1.37 (FFF88AFB bit 4 set, 0x0843F8, read); higher gain cal 0x571F1 = 9 (gain reading inferred). Second A/F sensor table in 0x06C1A8 (read); shares the axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range). Identical to it in stock; edit both together. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 060898 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633EC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Stock: full (219) at the lowest input, empty at 2432 and above. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 0608A4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633F8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06C768, read). ADC channel 9 (0xFFFFE852, untrimmed) -> FFF8939A, filtered by cal 0x590F0 into FFF8939E (cal 0x590EE replaces the input while FFF88BCA bit 2 or 3 is set) and looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF893A0 (degC + 50), read only by the charging-voltage control 0x136CD8 (temperature-compensated voltage targets); the unfiltered value gives FFF893A1, reported by SSM as x - 10 (0x11F0E8, read). Identity (inferred): its companion input ADC channel 4 (FFF89390, 0x06C554) is a linear signal centred on 2.5 V (FFF89396 = 12800 - 0.488 x (sample - 32768); SSM x/128 + 28 puts zero at 2.5 V, about -50 A per volt), i.e. a bidirectional battery current, read by charging control 0x136BC0 and idle 0x0EE338; the two inputs share their filter cal block and their range monitors (FFF88BCA bits 2-5, 0x0715B0-0x07175C) are both enabled by cal 0x57584 bit 4, which is clear in stock (monitors off). A current + temperature pair used only for charging is the battery sensor, so this is battery temperature. Stock: 100 C at 0.32 V, 20 C at 2.37 V, -40 C from 4.71 V (NTC). Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 0608B0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 063404. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.description:
How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active. Stock about 130 s of heating at -40 C to about 90 s at 60 C.
Details: When used: while the engine runs (run state FFF8906B = 3). 0x1028D0 (read; called from 0x101CF0): FFF8A833 bit 7 is set (and held until the run state leaves 3) when the accumulated rear O2 heater drive FFF88E6E > this(coolant at start FFF88A46; the -40 C row is used when the coolant sensor is faulted, FFF88E28 bit 1), or when FFF8881E >= cal 0x4B900 (9437) for cal 0x4B904 (50) passes. Rear O2 identity: the heater output FFF9980E bit 2 is driven by 0x06EC70 for FFF8CE0B of every 24 40-ms passes, and 0x073570 monitors that output against FFF8CE0B into FFF89CB4 bits 0/1, the P0037 / P0038 (heater circuit, bank 1 sensor 2) monitor records (dtc_monitors slots 182 / 180, read). FFF88E6E sums FFF8CE0B every 40 ms (0x06ED92, read), so it is heater energy since start; FFF8CE0B = 0 while the heater is held off (initial delay from 0x608F4, high load, battery out of range; 0x06E7D8, read). FFF8881E = 2 x (ADC channel 11 - ADC channel 25) (0x1E0000 task, read); it is the oxygen-sensor signal that gates Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (0x0CAE40: FFF8881E < cal 0x14F5C, read), so the second path is 'sensor already reads rich' (inferred). FFF8A833 bit 7 feeds the catalyst/rear-O2 module 0x101CF0 (0x1023E0, 0x102B58) and the rear O2 diagnostics 0x1B8890 / 0x1B902C (P0137, result FFF8AD93 bit 7) and 0x123C68 (read). Meaning 'sensor ready / warmed up' inferred. Stock 26250 at -40 C falling to 18125 at 60 C start coolant; at 13.75 V with the default heater stage that is about 130 s and 90 s of heating (inferred, 200 counts/s). Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor being treated as ready. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 05CEB0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00BC9C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0113)
Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0117)
Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)
Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0193)
P0087 Rail Pressure Low Limit
table.description:
Rail pressure floor by rpm for P0087 (rail pressure too low): the code counts a fault when actual pressure stays more than 0.30 MPa (hysteresis cal) below this value for about 10 seconds, i.e. below 0.40 MPa in stock, and recovers when pressure is back at this value. Stock 0.70 MPa at all rpm.
Details: 0x0752A8 (read, boot lookup 0x72AC): the absolute low-pressure test fails while actual rail pressure FFF88884 < this(rpm FFF8CD56) - hysteresis cal 0x574DA for cal 0x574E0 passes -> P0087. Stock 1148 = 0.70 MPa flat. p16 (read): 0x0752A8 (<- 0x0A1D2C <- 0x1DFE3C) runs every 10 ms; 200 passes = 2 s, 1000 passes = 10 s. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 0609C4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0635D0. Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Enable
table.description:
Master switch for EGR (set in stock). Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off variants of base timing, closed loop target and throttle tables become the live ones (inferred).
Details: Set in stock. One of the EGR enable conditions computed by 0x0FAAFC (FFF8A811 bit 0), with coolant, rpm and load windows, engine running and normal combustion mode (read). Clearing it is expected to keep EGR off, so the EGR-off table variants (Base Timing (EGR Off, ...), Closed Loop Target (..., EGR Off), the non-EGR Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables) become the live ones (inferred). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 02F796 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) Caller of 0x104210 sets uStack_38 = (DAT_00037fee & 0x20) and passes it as param_8 (param_3 = 0x37FEF bit6, LF75404S 0x2F797 bit6); 0x103268 (pair of 0x0F9C3C) passes (DAT_00037fee & 0x20) to 0x104744 (pair of 0x0FB088). Stock 0x20 (bit5 set). Address 037FEE bit 5 (value 32). Confidence: read.

table.name: Transmission Coding: From Input Port
table.description:
When set, the manual/automatic coding is read from a hardware input instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT. Clear in all stock images; leave clear.
Details: Clear in all stock images. When set, the transmission coding (FFF886AB bit 7) is taken from a latched input-port bit (FFF80238 bit 7, set once port bit FFF8A2A4 bit 7 is seen) instead of Transmission Coding: Automatic/CVT (read, 0x06A38C). Leave clear. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 02F796 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) (read) 0x06D124 (pair of 0x06A38C): (DAT_00037fee & 0x40) == 0 selects DAT_00037fec & 2, else latched input port, as LF75404S 0x2F796 bit6. Shared byte with EGR Enable (bit5) is correct. Stock byte 0x20 (bit6 clear). Address 037FEE bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B
table.description:
Enables the second (Path B) tip-in torque shaping. Clear in stock, and all Path B tables are 0 and its rpm limit is 0, so setting only this bit does essentially nothing. Leave clear unless you calibrate the whole Path B set.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0x01). The torque module 0x0BE694 passes this bit to the rise shaping 0x0BB958 (BLD.B #6 at 0x0BF3D0, stack argument 11, read), and the torque monitor call passes it to 0x1877B4 (read). When set, Path B of the target-torque rise shaping can act (all "Target Torque Rise ... (Path B, ..., Off in Stock)" tables), and a request below Path B Start Torque passes unshaped. Path B also needs rpm <= cal 0x22A04, which is 0 in stock, so setting only this bit changes nothing but the Start Torque bypass (and Path B tables are all 0 ft-lb in stock, so that bypass never triggers). Leave clear unless the whole Path B set is calibrated. Bit 7 of the same byte is a separate switch passed to another torque routine (seg_0x0B0000.c:9252). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 023704 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) the rise-shaping function 0x0C3FE8 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0BB958; it reads the Path B pedal multiplier table) is called once, with (cal 0x2A9B8 & 0x40) as its only bit-6 cal flag argument, as LF75404S passes cal 0x23704 bit 6 (read); stock byte 0x01 (bit 6 clear). Address 02A9B8 bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Open Loop Fueling: Use Alternate Map
table.description:
When set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate, Off in Stock) probably replaces the normal open loop fueling strategy. Clear in stock; leave clear unless you have filled that table.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0x8F). Passed by the open-loop fueling readers 0x0CE854 and 0x0CE5E8 (read): when set, Primary Open Loop Fueling (Alternate, Off in Stock) is used in place of the base + DAM-scaled knock additive strategy (inferred). Leave clear unless you have filled that table. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 02F79A by the code that reads it (read). Address 037FF2 bit 4 (value 16). Confidence: read.

table.name: VE: Use AVCS-Not-Ready Table
table.description:
When set, Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock) is used while the cams are probably not yet under control. Clear in stock; leave clear.
Details: Clear in stock. 0x11E308 uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock) only when this bit is set and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear (read); FFF8A83B bit 7 = AVCS ready (inferred). Leave clear. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 02C4D0 by the code that reads it (read). Address 034B00 bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing: Pedal-Released Tables Enable
table.description:
Set in stock: with the pedal released, Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed/Open) replaces the normal EGR Active/Off base timing tables. Clear it to use the normal base timing tables off-throttle too.
Details: Set in stock (all images). With this bit set and FFF8A774 bit 0 (pedal released) set, Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed/Open) replaces the EGR Active/Off base timing tables (read, 0x0C2C08). Clear it to use the normal base timing tables with the pedal released. LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 01071E by the code that reads it (read). Address 01071E bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Multi-Injection Allowed During High-Pedal Latch 1
table.description:
Allows double/triple injection while one of the high-pedal latches is set (clear = not allowed; clear in stock). Has no effect on a stock car because the multi-injection windows are disabled, so stock always uses single injection.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0xE0). The multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 (0x10B650) requires the high-pedal latch FFF8A8A3 bit 6 to be clear unless this bit is set (read; the pairing of bit and latch follows the argument order at the call in 0x109008, inferred). Only matters if the double/triple injection windows are opened (they are 65535 in stock, so stock always uses single injection). LF9C000C: located from LF75404S 02996D by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) the multi-injection enable call (counterpart of LF75404S 0x10B650 called from 0x109008) passes bits 0, 1 and 2 of cal 0x31EAD as the three latch-allow arguments, in the same order (read); stock byte 0xE0 as in 2015 (read). Address 031EAD bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: inferred.

table.description:
Allows double/triple injection while a second high-pedal latch is set (clear in stock). Has no effect on a stock car because the multi-injection windows are disabled, so stock always uses single injection.
Details: Clear in stock (byte 0xE0). The multi-injection enable FFF8A775 bit 0 (0x10B650) requires the high-pedal latch FFF8A8A4 bit 6 to be clear unless this bit is set (read; the pairing of bit and latch follows the argument order at the call in 0x109008, inferred). Only matters if the double/triple injection windows are opened (they are 65535 in stock, so stock always uses single injection). Evidence: (from LF9C100P) the multi-injection enable call (counterpart of LF75404S 0x10B650 called from 0x109008) passes bits 0, 1 and 2 of cal 0x31EAD as the three latch-allow arguments, in the same order (read); stock byte 0xE0 as in 2015 (read). Address 031EAD bit 1 (value 2). Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Trim 1
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for cylinder 1 only, by fuel quantity and rpm (128 = no change), applied before the pulse is split into injections. Use it to balance individual cylinders. Stock all 128 (no effect).
Details: Multiplier on injector 1's fuel quantity before the split into injections: 0x0D168C writes FFF8C060 = quantity x this(quantity, rpm) / 128 + the per-cylinder transient (wall-film + throttle-rate) fuel term FFF8C1E4 (0x0F6260; not learned: 0x8000 = none, reset to 0x8000 outside running; adds 4 x (term - 32768) counts) (read). Order 1-4 is the order the code processes FFF8C060-C06C; the transient fuel module's cylinder masks (05C8A0-05C8C4, read in 0x0F5AD0) only fit firing order 1-3-2-4 if slot n is cylinder n+1, so 1-4 is the cylinder number (inferred, strong). All 128 (no change) in stock. Descriptor 05B1FC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 1 (Single Injection)
table.description:
Fuel multiplier for injector 1 when it fires once per cycle, which appears to be the stock case (128 = x1.0). Stock all 128, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: Strategy byte = injections per cycle (FFF8A69E, 0x0CF3EC, read): this one applies with one injection (the stock case). Written to FFF8A6A3 by 0x0CF630 (read). Injector 1's quantity (0x0D168C) is multiplied by this / 128 when that injector's strategy byte FFF8A69F equals 1 (read). The strategy byte is probably the number of injections per cycle (inferred from the split-injection code). All 128 (x1.0) in stock. Descriptor 05ADE8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Per-Injector Fuel Multiplier 2 (Single Injection)

table.name: Base Fuel Quantity Limit

scaling.category: mg fuel per cylinder (stock Injector Scaling)
scaling.units: mg (stoich fuel per cylinder per cycle)

scaling.category: base pulse (0.3 MPa reference, any Injector Scaling)

table.description:
Ceiling on the base fuel quantity, the stoichiometric fuel the ECU calculates from measured air before any enrichment. Its meaning in air depends on Injector Scaling: stock it allows about 5 g of air per revolution, but lowering the injector flow figure (for example for E85) lowers the ceiling. Raise it in proportion when you raise Injector Scaling, or the engine will run lean at high airflow.
Details: When used: always while running (every pass of 0x0B7E00, which computes load and the base fuel quantity, read). Upper limit of the base (stoichiometric) fuel quantity FFF8ADEA. 0x0B8030 (read) computes FFF8ADEA = air quantity FFF8C250 x Injector Scaling x 0.10266 / 14.7 / 4 / rpm x 0.125 (= 0.5587 x Injector Scaling x air per cylinder per cycle in g) and stores min(that, this) (0x0B80FC-0x0B8112: MOVU.W @0x23696, CMP/GE, read). The limited value is what the rest of the fuel path uses: the base pulse 0x0D15EC (FFF8C05C = 16 x FFF8ADEA x trims), before the enrichment/fuel factor 0x0D1528 and the flow compensation and latency 0x0D2BB8; the transient-fuel film model 0x0F5F84; the fuel load FFF8ADEE (0x0B895C); and the fuel-used accumulators 0x06B70E (read). Above the limit the base pulse stops rising with airflow, so the mixture goes lean as air keeps rising; enrichment is applied on top of the limited value and does not lift it (inferred from the order of the calls). The raw unit includes Injector Scaling, so the limit in air terms moves with it: air per revolution at the limit = this x 3.580 / Injector Scaling (raw) g/rev = this x reference injector flow [g/s] x 0.0004704. Shown in g/rev for stock Injector Scaling 2918 (2.61 g/s). Stock 4060 = 4.98 g/rev (2.49 g per cylinder per cycle, about 556 g/s at 6700 rpm), well beyond the stock turbo. With Injector Scaling at 1.74 g/s (fuel added for E85 by lowering the flow figure) the limit drops to 3.32 g/rev; below about 1.73 g/s it falls under the 3.31 g/rev (256 %) ceiling of engine load FFF8ADE4 (0x0B7EFC, read) and becomes the first limit reached. When you raise Injector Scaling raw (lower reference flow), raise this in proportion: new = 4060 x new raw / 2918 keeps 4.98 g/rev (u16, up to 65535). On AT/CVT codings, while FFF886AB bit 5 is set (meaning not decoded), the value is first smoothed by boot filter 0x6CEC with cal 0x23694 (stock 255); the limit applies on either path (read). 4060 in all eight images; the same code in LF78001H 0x0C1770, LF79002P 0x0C83DC, LF79100P 0x0C788C, LF9C100P 0x0C0ED8, LV9N 0x0A6840 (read). Address 023696. Confidence: read.

Stock 15 MPa flat. Descriptor 05EB84. Confidence: read.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling
table.description:
Base open-loop (power enrichment) AFR target by rpm and load, used once the exhaust temperature estimate is high enough. The ECU uses the richer of this and the Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...) group: to lean, edit both; to richen, either. Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor (Outside Closed Loop).
Details: Note: the ECU has a second open-loop fuel path: the four "Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV ..., AVCS ...)" tables 05ABB0..05ABEC, blended by TGV and AVCS (0x0CE5E8 -> FFF8A681); 0x0CEA80 takes the richer of the two (max). To lean the open-loop target edit both sets; richening works with either (read, my research notes). Also see Open Loop Fueling Floor. Base open-loop enrichment target, 0x0CE854. Used only while the exhaust temperature estimate FFF8AFD0 (see Exhaust Temperature Model Map A/B) is >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), or its integral FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8 (65535); otherwise this path contributes 0 (read). While cal 0x2F79A bit 4 is clear (stock; the first argument of 0x0CE854), the additive term (Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive x DAM multiplier) is added, minus Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive x Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128, both all zero in stock (read). The result is rate-limited (FFF84424) into FFF8A682, and FFF8A684 = max(FFF8A682, other enrichments) feeds commanded lambda. Descriptor 05AC6C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling (TGV Closed, AVCS Inactive)
table.description:
Open-loop AFR target for TGVs closed with AVCS not in active control, part of a blend by TGV position and AVCS state, used above Open Loop Delay Load Threshold after a delay. Stock identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling; edit all five together. The ECU uses the richer of the two systems, so leaning needs both.
Details: When used: whenever the open-loop delay has expired (see below); the blend follows TGV position and AVCS state. TGV-closed base, weight 1 - a (AVCS not in active control). 0x0CE5E8 (read; called from 0x0C589C with rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, cal 0x2F79A bit 4, DAM FFF811AE, AVCS weight FFF8A743 and TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8): TGV-closed base = 05ABB0 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABD8 x a/255, TGV-open base = 05ABC4 x (255 - a)/255 + 05ABEC x a/255, where a = FFF8A743 is the AVCS-active weight from 0x0D952C (255 while both cam controllers are in active control, my research notes); blend FFF8A69B = closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + open x FFF8B3E8. With cal 0x2F79A bit 4 clear (stock): FFF8A681 = clamp(blend + Additive x DAM Multiplier(DAM)/128 - 05AC14 x 05AC3C(DAM)/128 (Primary Open Loop Fueling Subtractive (TGV/AVCS Group) x its DAM multiplier; both all zero in stock), 0, 255). With the bit set: Alternate (+ cal 0x13DCD) while DAM16 < cal 0x1391C (16), else blend + cal 0x13DCD. 0x0CEA80 (read) then takes FFF8A681 (only once FFF8AFD6 >= FFF8AFE6, the open-loop delay, and when >= cal 0x13DD0 = 5), scales it by cal 0x237CA/128 (x1.0), rate-limits its rise by 05ACD4(rpm) and sets FFF8A684 = max(that, FFF8A682), FFF8A682 being Primary Open Loop Fueling from 0x0CE854. FFF8A684 is the open-loop enrichment in commanded lambda 256/(256 + B030 + A684 + AFE8) (0x171C88). So the commanded open-loop mixture is the richer of the two systems: to lean the target, lower this group as well as Primary Open Loop Fueling; to richen, raise this group (Primary Open Loop Fueling alone only takes effect while its exhaust-temperature enable holds: 0x0CE854 sets FFF8A683 to 0 unless FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 or FFF8C03C >= cal 0x18DD8, read). Stock: byte-identical to Primary Open Loop Fueling (05AC6C) and to the other three tables of this group (AFR 14.7 down to about 10.7 at high load); edit all five together. Descriptor 05ABB0. Confidence: inferred.

table.description:

table.name: Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive DAM Multiplier
table.description:
Scales Primary Open Loop Fueling Additive by the Dynamic Advance Multiplier (DAM), so the extra fuel is added as knock history lowers DAM. Edit with the (TGV/AVCS Group) copy.

table.name: Injection Timing (Double Injection, 1st, Off in Stock)
table.description:

Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC, stored directly (0x0CFC20: code = 1440 - x, then clamped to 0.5-540 BTDC; read). Same scale as every other Injection Timing / injection-angle table. When used: Angle of the first pulse when two injections per cycle are used, in normal fuel mode (0x0CB394, read). Stock never uses multiple injections: the Double/Triple Injection Quantity Windows are 65535 (read). Descriptor 05AF94. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Injection Angle 2
table.description:
Angle of the second (late, after top dead centre) pulse during stratified catalyst heating, by spark target; negative = after TDC. Stock pinned at the late limit, about 170 degrees after TDC. Has no effect in stock: Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share is 0, so the pulse gets no fuel.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the compression TDC; negative = AFTER that TDC (expansion stroke). This angle is an offset in segment 0, the 180 degrees after firing TDC (0x0CB604 mode 3 uses it with segment 0; the pulse-fit check 0x075D84 places it B064 + 1440 after the first pulse B062, read), so it is shown as -offset/2: clamped to 0 to -179.5 (0x0D0468, read), and -170 to -179.5 act as -169.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock pins at the -179.5 clamp (stored -170 at spark 24 BTDC only): a late expansion-stroke pulse, about 170 degrees ATDC in effect (its quantity is Catalyst Heating Second Injection Share, cal 0x2A3CA, which is 0 in stock, so stock fires no second pulse in this mode). Catalyst-heating mode = FFF8A85C 2 (0x109B4C, read): it maps to fuel mode 3 (0x108B08), in which the ignition target is FFF8A76C (0x0DA51C, read) and the injection angle is FFF8B062 (0x0CB394, read). FFF8B064 = this(FFF8A76C), clamped to 0-359 (0x0D0468, read); used for the second injection's angle by 0x0CB604 (read). Descriptor 05B194. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Normal)
table.description:
Second-pulse injection angle in catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and spark target; compression stroke, limited to 10.5-180 BTDC. Used when the TGVs are not closed. Stock 40 BTDC (100 BTDC at 1350-1450 rpm with late spark); identical to the TGV Closed table.
Details: Units (FU_UNITS): degrees BTDC of the injected cylinder's compression TDC (0 = firing TDC, 180 = intake BDC (start of compression), 360 = gas-exchange TDC, 540 = expansion BDC); larger = earlier. Same scale as every Injection Timing table. Second pulse of the phase 2 split; clamped to 0.5-180 BTDC (code 1080-1439, 0x0D023C, read), i.e. the compression stroke; 0.5-10 BTDC act as 10.5 (0x1DCA04, read). Stock identical to Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle (TGV Closed). Injection angle FFF8B060 from rpm and FFF8A76B (0x0D023C, read), the second-injection angle in fuel mode 2 (0x0CB604, read). table.description:

Details: When used: catalyst-heating phase 2 first pulse while the TGVs are closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 set); then it replaces the TGV Normal adder and 05B0A4 replaces the multiplier (0x0D00A8, read). 0x0D00A8 (called from 0x0C589C with (906B, cal 0x38448 bit 5, rpm FFF8CD54, load FFF8A616, FFF88E28 bit 2, FFF88E2B bit 5, FFF88A9D, IAT FFF88662, coolant FFF88A44, spark target FFF8A76B, TGV closed FFF8A881 bit 4, &FFF8B05E), read): in fuel states 2/3 FFF8B05E = Base(rpm, coolant) + Base Adder(rpm, load) x multiplier(FFF88A9D, IAT)/255 + Base Spark Adder(spark, coolant), clamped to code 720-1079 (180.5-360 BTDC); with FFF88E28 bit 2 or FFF88E2B bit 5 set only the Base is used (read). table.name: Catalyst Heating Phase 2 Injection Angle Adder (TGV Closed)

table.name: Start Split Injection Second Share (Idle)
table.description:
Share of fuel moved into the second (compression-stroke) pulse during the start / catalyst-heating phase 2, by rpm and coolant (0 = single injection). Used with the pedal released and the car stopped. Stock 40 % almost everywhere; the three tables are identical.
Details: When used: fuel mode 2, pedal released and stopped, FFF899D7 bit 0 clear. 0x10A604 (read) writes FFF8A85F = this(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant FFF88A44; coolant at start FFF88A46 instead if cal 0x2996C bit 3, clear in stock) at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8); 0 when FFF8A657 bit 7 or FFF8A857 bit 7, cal 0x2A340 (51) if cal 0x2996C bit 4 (clear). 0x0D0A7C-0x0D0C14 copy A85F into the per-injector split FFF8A6D6...A6D9 when that injector's fuel mode FFF8A858...A85B is 2 (combustion modes 1 and 3, 0x108B08) (read); the second pulse gets A6D6/256 of the quantity (0x0D1FB8) at the Catalyst Heating Phase 2 injection angle B060, and A6D6 = 0 means no second pulse (my research notes) (read). Selection: pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A389 (2 km/h) -> 05D1A0 (05D1C8 if FFF899D7 bit 0), otherwise 05D1B4 (read). Stock 102 (40 % in the second pulse) everywhere except 0 (single injection) at 1200-1600 rpm with coolant at the 40 degC end of the axis (axis -30...40 degC); the three tables are identical. Descriptor 05D1A0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Maximum Time
table.description:
Longest time the stratified catalyst-heating phase may last. Stock 10 s.
Details: Phase FFF8A85C 2 (stratified heating) continues only while its timer FFF853B6 is below this (0x109B4C, read). Stock 1000. p16 (read): timers FFF853B6/BA count 10 ms passes of 0x109B4C (stock 1000 = 10 s). Address 029A4A. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Coolant Minimum
table.description:
Lowest coolant temperature at which stratified catalyst heating is allowed.
Details: Phase FFF8A85C 2 requires coolant FFF8CD65 >= this (0x109B4C, read). Address 029A39. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Coolant Maximum
table.description:
Highest coolant temperature at which stratified catalyst heating is allowed. Stock 75 degC.
Details: Phase FFF8A85C 2 requires coolant FFF8CD65 <= this (0x109B4C, read). Stock 125 = 75 degC. Address 029A38. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Rail Pressure Minimum
table.description:
Minimum rail pressure needed for stratified catalyst heating. Stock 0.5 MPa.
Details: Phase FFF8A85C 2 requires rail pressure FFF88884 >= this (0x109B4C, read). Stock 820 counts = 0.5 MPa. Address 029A3C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Catalyst Heating Readiness Idle Stability Time
table.description:
How long the idle must be steady (pedal released, normal running) before the catalyst-heating readiness flag sets, by rpm change and rpm versus idle target. Its exact role after that is inferred. Stock 80-115 passes when rpm is steady, up to 500 when falling or low.
Details: When used: combustion mode 4 with the pedal released (FFF88C64 bit 5), only because cal 0x2996C bit 2 is set (stock) (0x10AAB0, read). The readiness flag FFF8A856 bit 5 (0x10AAB0 -> abStack, read) additionally needs a pass counter FFF853E6 (reset whenever the conditions drop) to reach this(rpm change FFF8CEA6, rpm - idle target FFF8B236), i.e. the idle has to be steady for this many passes (disassembly 0x10AB72-0x10AB98: R5 = CEA6, R6 = CE9C - B236, read). The other readiness conditions are the coolant window of Catalyst Heating Coolant Minimum/Maximum shrunk by cal 0x29A5C and further cals (my research notes). A856 bit 5 is used by the mode logic 0x109B4C (with a timer from 05D170, 0x109AA8) (read); its exact role there (re-entry of the heating modes) is inferred. Stock 80-115 passes when rpm is steady and at/above target, up to 500 passes when rpm is falling fast or below target. Descriptor 05D204. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Purge Valve Duty
table.description:
Purge valve duty needed for a target purge flow at a given manifold vacuum; higher vacuum needs less duty. Applied above Purge Valve Minimum Duty. Change only for a different purge valve.
Details: When used: every 80 ms pass (0x0D60FC, read): A70A = this(target purge flow FFF8B0C0, manifold vacuum FFF8CDFA). The final duty is A713 + (100 % - A713) x this, with A713 = Purge Valve Minimum Duty (0x0D6118, read), and 0 when this is 0. B0C0 = purge rate x air quantity FFF8B4D6 / 256, in the air-quantity unit (read). Stock: 0 at zero flow; at 1.07 g/s 100 % with no vacuum, 48 % at 6.7 kPa, 16 % at 53 kPa; 100 % from 8.6 g/s. Higher vacuum needs less duty for the same flow. Purge module (inferred: canister purge): 0x0D4E78 (80 ms task 0x1E1560) and 0x0D4C14 (20 ms task 0x1E0AE8) (read). Chain (read): purge rate A70C (limits A6FD/A70F, ramp A709, cut B0A0) -> purge flow B0C0 = A70C x air FFF8B4D6/256 -> valve duty A70A = 05B314(B0C0, vacuum) -> A70B with minimum duty A713 -> A707 -> timer E channel 22 (0x1D98D6); A707 is also checked by the circuit monitor 0x072090 (driver status FFF88BF4 bits 10/11). Fuel: A71A = filtered purge rate x learned concentration FFF81412 (0x0D688C) is subtracted from the fuel factor (0x0D15EC). Descriptor 05B314. Confidence: read.

table.name: Minimum Ignition Timing
table.description:
Lowest timing the ECU will ever fire when Minimum Ignition Timing (Coolant) does not apply. Final timing is never allowed below this. Stock -25 degrees.
Details: 0x0D9E40 (read): the timing floor used outside the coolant-table conditions. Stock -50 = -25 degrees. Address 02FC69. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing IAT Compensation
table.description:
Timing added (negative = retard) for hot intake air, by intake air temperature, scaled by Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier. Applied once the engine is running above about 800 rpm and feeds into base timing. Stock 0 up to 30 C, then retard growing to about -21 degrees at 110 C at full multiplier.
Details: When used: FFF8A782 = rate-limited (cals 0x32DE2/0x32DE4 = 65535, i.e. none) value, enabled once FFF8CD5C >= cal 0x37F9E (800 rpm) in running mode FFF8866C = 3 (0x0E0184, read; cal 0x239AE bit 3 clear, so the knock-limit min() is not applied). FFF8A782 is added to the torque-model base timing FFF8A645 (0x0C2C08, A-D path with FFF8A787; E/F path with FFF8A788; my research notes, Ghidra stack args) and to the timing request FFF8A78A/FFF8B10E -> FFF8A789 (0x0E0A30, register args, read), which becomes the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). It is not a separate term of the final timing sum FFF8A744, but it reaches the fired timing through FFF8A645 (FFF8A645 -> FFF8A76A -> FFF8A76D -> FFF8A74B -> FFF8A744, 0x0DD568 / 0x0DD760 / 0x0DA600 / 0x0D9E40, read). Value = this(IAT FFF88A48) x Base Timing IAT Compensation Multiplier(rpm, load) / 128 (read). Stock 0 up to 30 C, then -6 (40 C) to -42 counts (110 C) = -21 degrees at full multiplier. Descriptor 05BCC8. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Maximum Retard
table.description:
Largest amount of timing feedback knock correction can pull. The live knock retard never goes below minus this value, and it applies to all cylinders at once. Raising it allows more protective retard. Stock about 12 degrees.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). This is the floor: the integrator never goes below minus this value. Stock 34 counts = 11.95 degrees. Address 01C273. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Knock, State 0x0E)

States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold).
