table.name: FLKC Range Boundary Load 1
table.description:
One of the four load boundaries that split fine learning knock correction (FLKC) into load ranges; each learning cell covers one rpm range by one load range. Moving it changes which conditions share a learned correction. Stock boundaries are 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load) (this is boundary 1, stock 31.5 %). Keep them in increasing order.
Details: Fine learning knock correction cells (0x0E1C58, read): the cell FFF8A790 = 5 x rpm range + load range (0...34). Seven rpm ranges are split at the six boundaries 0x1C24A...0x1C254 on FFF8CE9C, five load ranges at the four boundaries 0x1C240...0x1C246 on FFF8ADE4, each with a hysteresis band (0x1C256 rpm, 0x1C248 load). The learned value for the cell is FFF81414[cell] (s16, x 256); 0x0E73CC applies FFF8A7A7 = min(that, KCA Max x (16 - DAM) x 16) / 256, in 0.3516 degree counts; it is not added to the fired timing directly: like KCA it enters the timing request (0x0C13B4 -> FFF8AF22 -> 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568), so fired base timing = min(Base Timing + comps, request + KCA + FLKC), and in limit states 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B through the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088). 0x0DFA88 also sums it into the total knock correction FFF8A77B, whose only consumer (0x0DDBBC -> FFF8A770) is zero in stock (read). A negative learned value therefore retards the spark only where the request side is the lower one (most of the high-load map in stock); where Base Timing is lower it is hidden until it pulls the request below Base Timing. Feedback knock correction is the only knock term added directly (0x0D9E40). load boundary. Stock 0.41 / 0.92 / 1.70 / 3.19 g/rev (31.5 / 71.5 / 131.5 / 246.5 % load). Address 01C240. Confidence: read.

table.name: FBKC Retard Step (Secondary Knock, State 0x0D, Unused in Stock)
table.description:
Timing pulled per event by feedback knock correction when the secondary knock detector fires. Unused in stock because every Secondary Knock Threshold is at maximum, so that detector never triggers. Stock about 1.4 degrees.
Details: Feedback knock correction (0x0E2BE4, read): FFF8A79A is an s8 integrator kept at or below 0 and added directly to the fired timing (x 0.3516 degrees, 0x0D9E40): it is the only knock term of that sum, and FFF8A79A is one value for the whole engine, so a knock event on any cylinder retards all four (the fired timing FFF8A744 is recomputed per event for the next cylinder, but no per-cylinder knock retard exists; read). The state FFF8A79C (set once per combustion event by 0x0E2F94 from that event's knock results FFF8A7AD / FFF8A7B5; FFF8A7C1 is the knock-window-length flag (1 = extended window), used there only to reload per-cylinder hold counters FFF84920...FFF84930 from cal 0x27014 when it changes, purpose inferred) picks the action: states 0x0E, 0x0D, 7 and 6 subtract a step (floor = minus FBKC Maximum Retard); states 0x0C, 2, 0 (outside the rpm window) and the other non-knock states (0x0A outside the window, 0x0B) add the recovery step 0x1C271; 0x10 (inside the rpm window, no knock, fewer than cal 0x1C288 = 100 events since the last knock) holds the correction unchanged; 0x0F (inside the window, no knock, >= 100 events) adds 0x1C270, 8/9 add 0x1C272 (capped at 0); 5 = FFF8A79B x 0x1C26E / 128; 3 and 4 load the fixed values 0x1C26F / 0x1C278; 1 = 0. States (0x0E2F94, read, in priority order): 1 = knock control off (cal 0x56EE7 bit 7); 2 = FFF886AB bit 5 or load FFF8ADE4 <= cal 0x1C27E (0); 3 / 4 = FFF88E29 bit 3 / FFF88E2A bit 6 (fixed -14 counts = -4.9 degrees, inferred knock-sensor fault default); 5 = engine speed above FBKC Window RPM Maximum (hold); inside the rpm window: 6 / 0x0D = knock A (FFF8A7AD, intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold, never in stock) with / without FFF8AA85 bit 0, 7 / 0x0E = knock B (FFF8A7B5, intensity > Knock Threshold, the active one); 0x0F = no knock and FFF8B130 (events since the last knock, 0x0E7C7C) >= cal 0x1C288 (100), 0x10 = no knock, fewer events; 8 / 9 hold; 0x0A / 0x0B / 0x0C other conditions (0x0B: A/F FFF88AF6 above a lambda threshold). Subtracted per pass in state 0x0D. Stock 4 counts = 1.41 degrees. p16 (read): the FBKC logic 0x0E2F94 (0x0E402C <- 0x07D0E0 <- 0x1E1CBC) is crank-synchronous: one pass per combustion event (180 deg CA, dispatched at tooth position 70 via the ATU-J0 software interrupt 0x0A7390), not per time. Address 01C277. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing DAM Blend Alternate (DAM 0) (Off in Stock)
table.description:
Alternate DAM-blended timing offset (DAM 0 side) for base timing. It has no effect on a stock car: it is only used when a calibration switch is set to a specific value, which it is not in stock. 32 = no change. Stock +2 degrees at low rpm, varying to 0 from 4000 rpm; identical to its DAM 1 pair.

table.name: Knock Threshold (Event 1, Short Window)
table.description:
Knock intensity (sum of the three strongest knock-channel ratios to their background, 3.0 = all at background) (by rpm and load) above which a knock event in slot 1 counts as knock and triggers feedback knock retard; used while the nominal (short) knock window is in use. Higher = less sensitive. Warning: the Full / Short Window sets were renamed on 2026-10-30 (earlier names had them swapped). Which cylinder slot 1 is has not been mapped.
Details: Knock decision (0x0E8654 / 0x0E80B4, read): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4) the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot] (output of the signal processing 0x0E51E4) is compared with two thresholds. Knock B, FFF8A7B5 = intensity > Knock Threshold (this family, FFF8C1CC[slot] by 0x0E77E0) or FFF8CDC4[slot] >= cal 0x1BD92 (65535, off); this is the active path in stock and drives FBKC states 7 / 0x0E (retard 0x1C275 / 0x1C274, 4 counts = 1.41 degrees). Knock A, FFF8A7AD = intensity > Secondary Knock Threshold (FFF8C1D4[slot] by 0x0E78E4); all 65535 in stock, so it never fires (states 6 / 0x0D). Each event also sets bits of FFF8A79D (0x10/0x20/0x30/0x40 by slot). Slot vs cylinder number not mapped. Knock Threshold (0x0E77E0, read): looked up by rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500) and load FFF8A616 for each event slot; set A (05C104/118/12C/140) while FFF8A7C1 = 0, i.e. the nominal (short) window; set B (05C154/168/17C/190) while A7C1 = 1, i.e. the extended window (0x0E77E0 at 0x0E7836-0x0E784A; flag polarity read in 0x0E20E0 at 0x0E21AA-0x0E21EC; corrected 2026-10-30, the earlier names had the two sets swapped). A higher value needs a larger knock signal to count as knock (less sensitive). Set A (nominal / short window). Descriptor 05C104. Confidence: read.

table.name: Knock Background Window Step (Event 2, Channel 2)
table.description:
Knock signal processing for event slot 2, channel 2 (probably a frequency band of the knock sensor). For the one event where the knock window switches length, it shifts the channel's background reference so the switch does not read as knock: added when the window lengthens, subtracted when it shortens. Larger = more compensation in both directions (the lengthening event less likely to count as knock, the shortening event more likely). Leave alone unless recalibrating knock detection.
Details: When used: event slot FFF8CDC0 = 2 (Event 2), knock channel 2 of 8 (index 1 of FFF8CDB0; enabled in stock: bit 1 of cal 0x1B97D is clear), on the knock window where FFF8A7C3 changes. Background step for this channel, added to (window extended) or subtracted from (window back to nominal) the channel background FFF8C190[1] for that one event; overlap-flag FFF8A7D3, gain curve cal 0x26F7F. Knock signal processing 0x0E51E4 (read; called once per knock window from 0x0E43B8 with load FFF8A616, after the event chain 0x0E433C): for the event slot FFF8CDC0 (1-4, the slot of the Knock Threshold tables) each of 8 knock channels i gets a reference ref_i = 32 x step_i + g x background_i, and the channel ratio is 256 x FFF8CDB0[i] / (ref_i / 32), i.e. measured / reference with 256 = equal (0x0E51E4 tail, read). Channels with their bit set in cal 0x1B97C..0x1B97F (per slot; stock 0xC1 = channels 1, 7 and 8 off) give 0; a channel flagged in FFF8CEED (driver flag, value at its lower limit, inferred) gives 256. The ratios are sorted and the largest min(cal 0x1B988, 5) = 3 are summed into the knock intensity FFF8C1C0[slot], which 0x0E80B4/0x0E8654 compare with Knock Threshold (read). The measured channels come from the knock sensor ADC: 0x1E7868 DMA-collects 32-sample blocks, 0x1E725A runs FFT-style butterflies, 0x1E73A4 takes sqrt(re^2+im^2) of 8 selected bins (pointer tables 0x34A88/0x34AA8), and 0x1E7724 sums them over the window into FFF8D1D4[8] -> FFF8CDB0[8] (read), so the 8 channels are 8 frequency bins of the knock sensor signal (inferred). background_i is the per-slot channel background FFF8C180.. (slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. (slot 4), a lag filter of the measured channel kept by 0x0E4500 when the event is not knocking, floored at the per-channel rpm curve FFF8C0D8 (0x0E22A4) (read). step_i is this table family: it is non-zero only on the one event where the slot's window-length flag changes (cal 0x28B9E = 0 in stock selects these flags): +table when the flag goes 0 -> 1 (window switched to the extended length) and -table when it goes 1 -> 0 (back to the nominal length); on that event the reference is also floored at 32 x FFF8C0D8[i] (read). The flag is set when the extended knock window is used (0x0E20E0, read: B11A = nominal + Knock Window Length Extension only while timing FFF8A744 <= Knock Window Extension Timing Threshold and the extended window ends before the event angle). The step is skipped (0) and g is changed instead when the slot's overlap flag (FFF8A7D2..D5) changes while the window is nominal: g = gain curve cal (implicit rpm axis, x/32) on 0 -> 1 and min(1024 / gain, cal 0x26FAF = 64) on 1 -> 0, else g = 32 (x1.0) (read). On the event after a flag change 0x0E4500 resets the background almost fully to the new measurement (filter weight 255/256 while FFF8A7BC is set, read), so the step only bridges that single event: a larger value raises that channel's reference when the window lengthens (lower intensity, less likely to count as knock on that event) and lowers it when the window shortens (read). Axes: rpm FFF8CDC2 (x 31.25 + 500, 500-4000 rpm) x load FFF8A616 (read). Stock 4 to 97 (raw); the sibling tables for channels 1, 7 and 8 (masked in stock) are all 0. Descriptor 05BEAC. Confidence: read.

(slot 1) / C190.. / C1A0.. / C1B0.. table.name: Surge Damping Timing Curve (AT/CVT Gear 1)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1). Not used on this manual-transmission calibration, so it has no effect on a stock car. Stock 0, so it has no effect.
Details: When used: AT/CVT only (FFF88ADA bit 7 clear; it is always set on this manual coding), gear FFF88FCE = 1 (0x0DBB20, read: the AT/CVT curve branch, mirrored by the MT branch that reads Surge Damping Timing Curve (Gear 1); the MT coding flag s4 picks the MT curve). Full-scale timing correction (degrees, negative = retard) by the largest throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE since the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 set (0x0DBB20 holds the maximum in FFF8B0F0 and resets it to 0 while the trigger is clear, read), before the phase, coolant, mode and cal factors (read). Surge damping term FFF8A758 (0x0DBB20, called from the 10 ms module 0x0DE0E0; stack args verified with callers.py: s0 = gear FFF88FCE, s4 = MT coding FFF88ADA bit 7, s8 = FFF8B0EE, s12 = rpm FFF8CE9C, s16 = FFF88C64 bit 5, s20 = combustion mode FFF8A85C, read): A758 = Curve(FFF8B0EE) x PhaseFactor(FFF8A75E) x CoolantFactor FFF8A75C x ModeFactor(A85C) x cal factor (MT coding: cal 0x306E5 = 254, or cal 0x306E7 = 128 once FFF88C64 bit 5 has been clear for cal 0x306E8 = 150 passes) / 255^4, in 0.5-degree units, capped at +63.5 degrees, and 0 when the trigger FFF8A7A1 bit 2 is clear or when the current swing count has lasted longer than its time cal 0x306EA..0x306FA (100/20/100/10/100/5/100/100/100 passes of 10 ms for counts 0..8) (read). A758 is added to the final timing sum in 0x0D9E40 (read), so negative values retard. Trigger (read): 0x0DC1E8 counts passes while FFF8A7A1 bit 3 is set, the throttle-flow change FFF8B0EE >= cal 0x3084E (131 = 0.4 % per 20 ms, MT; hysteresis 0x3084C) and FFF8B112 (0x0E0D14 of FFF88A3A) <= cal 0x30842; 0x0E1350 sets FFF8A7A1 bit 2 when that count exceeds a per-gear, per-rpm-band threshold (cals 0x30F62..0x30FAC); it is dropped after cal 0x30850 (90) active passes. FFF8A75E counts rpm swings (0x0DC324, see p17p_surge_phase). FFF88FCE is the gear: on the MT coding 0x08254C copies FFF8A8B6, which 0x11422C derives from the ratio gear FFF8A623 (read). Reading: a timing intervention after a throttle step that retards while rpm swings up and releases while it swings down, i.e. driveline surge (shuffle) damping (inferred from the structure; the stock odd-count-only factors fit it). Stock 0 at every flow change. Descriptor 05B880. Confidence: read.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs closed; identical to the TGV Open table in stock. It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections), and in stock the target is far lower, so raising this map at idle or when coasting does nothing.
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0: pedal-zero flag FFF88C64 bit 5 in engine state 2/3, vehicle speed FFF99835 at or below cal 0x2FDB2 = 200 km/h (inferred); 0x0E127C / 0x09FF9A, read), TGVs closed; enabled by cal 0x1071E bit 0, set in all four images. The TGV Closed and TGV Open tables are identical in stock. Base ignition timing. 0x0C2C08 uses this 16x16 table when cal 0x1071E bit 0 and FFF8A774 bit 0 are both set, and F2 set (F2 = FFF8A881 bit 4). The result is rate-limited (cals 0x1058C / 0x1058E) and the IAT compensation FFF8A782 and Closed-Pedal Timing Coolant Compensation FFF8A788 are added (0x0C2C08) to give base timing FFF8A645, which is only the upper limit of the fired timing: with the pedal released 0x0DD568 sets FFF8A76A = FFF8A645 - Torque Reduction Spark Retard(FFF8AF22 >> 7), where FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4) is the efficiency of the closed-pedal timing request (Closed-Pedal Timing Target + FFF8A788 + FFF8A782 + Post-Start Closed-Pedal Timing Advance, 0x0E0A30) plus KCA + FLKC, so in effect FFF8A76A = min(FFF8A645, that request + KCA + FLKC) (read; min() form computed from the inverse tables). FFF8A76A then goes through 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and 0x0D9E40 to FFF8A744. In stock the request at idle (about 6-8 degrees at 500-900 rpm, warm) is far below this map (19-28 degrees at 400-1000 rpm, 0.13-0.39 g/rev (10-30 % load)), and it stays below it when coasting (17 vs 34 degrees at 2000 rpm), so idle and coast timing are set by Closed-Pedal Timing Target and raising this map there has no effect (computed from stock data); lowering it below the target does take effect. The F2 selector is FFF8A881 bit 4, set by the TGV module 0x10CAE0 (0x10DEFC) - set = TGVs closed (see below). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. Descriptor 05A034. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Start Spark Target Base (Mode 1)
table.description:
Base spark target by rpm and coolant for the cold-start / catalyst-heating mode (pedal released, car stopped, below 4000 rpm); the manual-car set. Torque, run-time and re-entry adders go on top. It feeds the torque model and cold-start monitors; the fired spark probably follows other paths. Stock +17 degrees cold at low rpm, down to about -10 to -12.5 when warm.
Details: When used: set A7E2 bit 0 set, FFF899D7 bit 0 clear (the manual-car case). Base term. Stock +17 deg at 500-800 rpm with coolant up to 20 degC; it falls with rpm and coolant to -12.5 deg (ATDC) from 1075 rpm at 20-30 degC and to -10 deg from 600 rpm when hot (>= 70 degC). 0x108BAC (catalyst-heating module, read) writes FFF8A854, which 0x0C3200 selects as the spark target FFF8A647 in fuel mode FFF8A852 = 2 (combustion mode FFF8A85C 1 or 3, 0x108B08). A647 is the spark the torque model compensates for (0x0C2514, 0x0C1EA8) and the reference of the cold-start retard monitors (0x1CB70C, 0x132568: A72A - A854) (read); the fired spark in this mode follows FFF8A74C/FFF8A76B (0x0DA428), not A854 (read). In combustion mode 1 (A85C < 2), at <= 4000 rpm (cal 0x1CBD8), with the pedal released (FFF886AB bit 5) and speed below cal 0x2A0C1 (2 km/h): A854 = Base(rpm FFF8CD5C, coolant) + Torque Adder(FFF8A85E, coolant) + Run-Time Adder(passes since the engine state became running, coolant) + Re-Entry Adder(passes since mode 1 was re-entered from normal mode 4, coolant), saturated to a byte; the set is chosen by FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (set = the manual tables, clear = the "AT/CVT" tables; always set on the manual coding, Phase 14) and FFF899D7 bit 0 (set = the "Warm-Up Fallback" tables): a once-per-drive warm-up fallback latch set by 0x081EFC only when cal 0x59134 bit 0 is set, which is 0 in stock, so the Warm-Up Fallback tables are never used in stock (read). Otherwise in mode 1 A854 = 05D0BC x 05D0A8 / 256 + FFF8A789 - 32 (both tables 0 in stock, so the normal request); in mode 3 A854 = A72A (normal target) (read). with cal 0x2996C bit 6 set (clear in stock) A854 is forced to cal 0x2A0C0 (0 in stock). Units: A854 is compared with A72A and final timing in 0.5 degree units (inferred). All four sets are identical in stock. Descriptor 05D008. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Boost Limit
table.description:
Boost ceiling by rpm that the torque/throttle model uses as its full-load manifold pressure: the model's target MAP is (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this, and it also scales the throttle-area input. It is not an overboost cut (see Overboost Limit). Raise it together with Target Boost so the model's full-load pressure matches the boost you run. Stock 211 kPa absolute peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost.
Details: 0x1086F8 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A84F (raw) and FFF8A84E = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, where f is the target's baro/IAT factor: the compensated boost ceiling (read). The torque-model task 0x0C3D14 copies it to FFF8AFAE = A84E << 8 (0x0C3D0C, read). AFAE is the full-load manifold pressure of the throttle/torque model. Target MAP FFF8AF6A = (torque request / full-load reference torque) x this (0x0C2F0C). FFF8AF8A = Throttle Required Area column input AFA8 x this (0x0C3408). The pressure ratio AF6C = AF8A / this (0x0C2F9C) selects the high-pressure spark-compensation filter above 0.85 (all read). Also read by the airflow/torque model 0x111AB8 (role there not decoded). It is not an overboost cut; see Overboost Limit for that. Stock 211 kPa abs peak (about 16 psi gauge), matching Target Boost. Raise it with Target Boost. Descriptor 05CFC8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Target Boost IAT Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on Target Boost and Boost Limit by intake air temperature (1.0 = no change). Stock 0.78 at -40 F, 1.05 near 104 F, 0.96 from 140 F.
Details: 0x108778: FFF8B3B2 = 2 x Target Boost Baro Compensation x this x FFF8A84B / 128 (32768 = x1), the factor on the absolute boost target and Boost Limit (read). table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per step everywhere, i.e. no Stage 1 limit.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding; unused in stock (manual coding). AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock, 255 = x1) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Stock 24000 everywhere = 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per 10 ms, i.e. no Stage 1 limit (same as the high-gear cells of the Stage 2 AT/CVT Coding tables). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. Descriptor 0598BC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rev Limit RPM
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Address 01DEDE. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut RPM
table.description:
At or above this rpm, once the rev limit has started, every injector is cut on every firing (a hard fuel cut). Keep it equal to Rev Limit RPM; set higher, the range between them gets only the throttle cap, probably a softer limit. Stock 6700 rpm.
Details: When used: always in stock (vehicle speed never exceeds Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold). Set rpm of the full-cut latch (part 2): at or above it, while state 0x0B is active, the torque cap is zero and all four injectors are cut every combustion event (part 3). On its own it does not start a cut; Rev Limit RPM does. Set above Rev Limit RPM, the range between them gets only the throttle cap (part 5; a soft stage, inferred). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Address 01DE2C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.description:
Overboost limit by rpm, compensated for baro and intake temperature like the boost target. Boost 26.7 kPa over it for 2 s sets the overboost flag, and 33 kPa over it starts the overboost cut (throttle cap, then a full fuel cut once the flag is set). Raise it when raising boost targets (stock 211 kPa absolute peak). Note: the boost-control pressure reading stops at about 269 kPa absolute, so an Overboost Limit above about 236 kPa absolute (269 minus the 33 kPa cut margin) can never trigger the overboost cut.
Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768 (read; cal 0x290A8 = 1 would use a fixed value, 0 in stock). Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. The flag makes the state-0x0B cut a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Rev Limit RPM); on its own, outside state 0x0B, it reduces nothing. It also feeds a diagnostic 0x1B8310. Stock 211 kPa abs peak, the same as Boost Limit from 2,000 rpm. Raise it with Target Boost. Descriptor 05CFD4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP

Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. Address 01DE88. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable
table.description:
Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables). Set in stock; cleared, the limiter is probably fuel-cut only.
Details: Set in stock. With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). Cleared, the rev limiter and the overboost cut become fuel-only: no throttle closing during the cut (inferred). Address 023CEA bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this. Stock 0 kPa.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. The flag forces the zero torque cap in the overboost/rev cut state (0x0BAE98 -> FFF8AE8A, applied in limit state 0x0B; Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) and also feeds 0x1B8310 (0x1B828C / 0x1B83CC, the overboost diagnostic, inferred in my research notes), so this margin also sets how long that monitor sees overboost. Stock 0. Address 01DEF6. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.description:
Boost above Overboost Limit plus this enters the overboost cut state: the throttle is capped at once, and fuel to all cylinders is cut only if the 2-second overboost flag is also set. Stock 33 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Overboost latch FFF84167 (0x0BE140, read): sets when MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit (the baro/IAT-compensated FFF8A851) + this, and releases when MAP < that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). While set (and no higher state) the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0B, the same state as the rev limiter (see Rev Limit RPM). In that state the throttle-side request is capped at once (Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base) by rpm, or the stage tables above 256 kPa abs); fuel is cut on all four cylinders every event only once the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 is also set (MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay, 2.0 s stock) or rpm reaches Rev Limit Full Cut RPM; spark is not retarded. When MAP falls below the release level the state ends and fuel returns even if the flag is still set (inferred from the state gating, read). Stock 8448 = 33 kPa, about 244 kPa abs at the 211 kPa stock limit peak. Address 01DEE6. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)
table.description:
How far boost must fall below the overboost cut level before the overboost cut state ends. Stock 15 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Subtracted from the overboost latch level while the latch FFF84167 is set (0x0BE208-0x0BE222, read): the overboost cut state 0x0B releases when MAP FFF88FF4 < Overboost Limit + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) - this. See Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) for what the state does. Stock 3840 = 15 kPa, so the state releases 18 kPa above the Overboost Limit. Address 01DEE8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.description:
Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing. Stock 255 km/h (no effect in stock).
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed latch, see Vehicle Speed Limit). 0x0C058C (read): latch FFF84188 sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this (minus Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis while above it) and holds until speed is below and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP; while set, FFF8AF1A = zero torque, which in state 0x0C cuts fuel on all four cylinders every event (0x0B9DC8, 0x0C1AC8). Without it state 0x0C reduces nothing. Stock 255 km/h (off). Address 01DEF9. Confidence: read.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit
table.description:
Keeps normal spark timing during the vehicle-speed limiter. Set in stock; leave it set.
Details: Set in stock. Same as Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut for limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed limiter) (0x0DD568, read). Bits 5 and 4 do the same for states 0x19 and 0x1A (not decoded); state 0x1B always uses the normal target. Leave set. Address 0239AE bit 6 (value 64). Confidence: read.

table.name: Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut
table.description:

table.name: Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio (1 Cylinder)
table.description:
When a cut state asks for less torque than this share of the engine's current torque, one cylinder in four is cut. Also sets the first decel fuel cut stage. Stock 75 %.
Details: When used: in the cut limit states (decel fuel cut, rev/overboost/speed cuts). Below this torque ratio at least 1 cylinder is cut. 0x0C1AC8 (read): in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x18 (unless FFF8A638 = 2) and 0x19-0x1B the torque ratio FFF8A64F (capped / unreduced torque, 0x0C4BA0) is compared with four thresholds: cylinders cut FFF8A643 = 0 if the ratio >= the 1-cylinder threshold, 1 if >= the 2-cylinder threshold, 2 if >= the 3-cylinder threshold, 3 if >= the 4-cylinder threshold, else 4 (each threshold minus Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio Hysteresis while it is crossed). Once per event 0x0C4B84 then skips n of every 4 injections. The same four cals set the torque level of each decel fuel cut stage (0x0B9EF0), so changing them also changes the decel cut. table.name: Throttle Offset Step IAT Factor
table.description:
Intake-temperature factor on the step rate of a small throttle offset ramp. Has no effect on a stock car because the base step is 0. Stock all 1.0.
Details: 0x0C30F8: FFF8AF7E = cal 0x11ACE x this(IAT) x 05A080(baro) >> 14, the per-pass step of the AF9C throttle offset ramp (0x0C3700). cal 0x11ACE = 0, so inactive in stock; all 1.0. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). p16 (read): this torque-model function (0x0C3E34 subtree) runs every 10 ms (0x07C408 <- 0x1DFE3C); 'pass' = 10 ms. Descriptor 05A074. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Air Spark Compensation Limit
table.description:
Caps, by actual ignition timing, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded timing. Stock 1.5x at 22.5 degrees or more up to 3.1x at -15 degrees, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares data with two other entries: editing one edits all three.
Details: 0x0C37D8 (read): FFF8AFA8 = 32768 x (AF2C/AF64) x min(this(final timing FFF8A642), AF56)/8192; the result indexes Throttle Required Area 05A148. It caps the spark-efficiency air compensation (AF56, normally ~1.0) as a function of the actual final timing; stock 1.50x at >=22.5 deg up to 3.13x at -15 deg, so it does not bind in normal warm running. Shares its data (0x0107E8) with 05A124 and 05F414 (0x185FFC): editing one edits all three. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Descriptor 05A118. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Stock EGR and non-EGR tables are identical.
Details: When used: every pass of the 0x110000 torque module. Weight (1 - TGV open) x (1 - EGR). Stock: 14-49 ft-lb (19-66 Nm) at zero load, 260-306 ft-lb (352-415 Nm) at 2.81 g/rev (217 % load) from 2400 rpm (119 ft-lb, 162 Nm cap at 800 rpm); identical to the EGR table 05D64C. 0x118318 (DAM 1 set -> FFF8B490) and 0x1186A4 (DAM 0 set -> FFF8B4A2), called from 0x110000 with rpm FFF8CE9C, load FFF8A616, TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8 and EGR realisation FFF8B290 (read): closed = TGV-closed x (1 - w) + TGV-closed-EGR x w, open = TGV-open x (1 - w) + TGV-open-EGR x w with w = B290/256, result = closed x (1 - B3E8) + open x B3E8, all above the 16000 zero point (read; same blend as the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables in 0x0C0010). 0x10ED6C interpolates the two sets by DAM: FFF8B48A = B490 x DAM + B4A2 x (1 - DAM) with FFF811AE = DAM x 16 (read), and 0x118A40 subtracts (B490 - B4A2) x (1 - DAM) from the torque it reports as FFF8B4B2 (0.1 ft-lb, 0.1 Nm, 10000 = 0) (read). So these are the engine torque the ECU expects from the air charge, at full and at zero knock-learning advance (inferred from the DAM interpolation). They do not set the throttle or boost; they shape the estimated/reported engine torque (inferred). Axes: rpm FFF8CE9C x load % FFF8A616. Descriptor 05D638. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Torque Model Filter Multiplier B
table.description:
Torque-model smoothing multiplier by coolant (1.0 = normal; very high values mean no smoothing), used in another phase after a combustion-mode change. Stock 1.0 flat. Leave alone.
Details: 0x0C1EA8 (read): AF4E multiplies the rpm-based filter coefficient AFAC (0x0C38E0) in 0x0C2514 (AF58), 0x0C1854 (predicted air torque AF40) and 0x0C39DC (AF3E): k = AF4E x AFAC/512. 512 = 1.0; values that push k past 65535 mean no lag. Selected in state S1: after combustion-mode change 4 -> 1, while in mode 1, FFF886AB bit 5 set and final timing above the spark target. Stock 1.0 flat. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Descriptor 059EA0. Confidence: inferred.

Selected in state S2: after combustion-mode change 1 -> 3, while spark target - final timing > 4 deg (7 deg with A7E2 bit 0) and FFF886AB bit 5. TGVs normal, A7E2 bit 0 set. table.name: Spark Air Compensation Limiter
table.description:
Limits, by requested amount and coolant, how much the throttle model may add air to make up for retarded spark (TGVs not closed). Large compensation is cut more when cold. Leave alone unless you know the model. On 2017+ ROMs edit the "(Alt)" version instead: this one is unused there in stock.
Details: 0x0C2AD8 (read): A644 = this(AF58, coolant); AF5E = max(1.0, AF58 x A644/256) is the spark compensation actually allowed and is the normal value of the cap AF56 in 0x0C37D8. Stock: 1.0 at AF58 = 1.0, 0.63-0.90 at 1.4-2.0 (0.63-0.80 at 2.0), at 5.0 from 0.37 (cold) to 0.90 (20 degC). Used while TGVs are not forced closed (FFF8A881 bit 4 clear). Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). Descriptor 059FA8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Flow Coefficient (Reverse Flow)
table.description:
Coefficient of the throttle airflow model when the manifold is above the pre-throttle pressure; -1.0 in stock so the modelled flow turns negative. Leave alone.
Details: When used: every model pass while r > 1.0 (manifold above the pre-throttle pressure; the ratio is inverted). 0x11DD04 (read), enabled by FFF8A8FB bit 0 (0x11E43C): modelled throttle flow FFF8C24C [g/min] = (P_up/101325) x Throttle Flow Function(r) x FFF8ADEC (Throttle Area from Throttle Position, 0.05 mm^2) x Throttle Flow Temperature Correction x this x 60000 x 2.98e-15, which feeds the manifold/airflow observer 0x11DB50 / 0x11D938. Stock 192 = -1.0 as a signed byte, so the modelled flow turns negative (out of the manifold) (read). Normally leave alone. Address 02B06D. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. Map A while no open-loop enrichment is active. 0x0C9878 (read): with no open-loop enrichment (FFF8A684 = 0) S = Map A (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier A (No Enrichment)/256 and U = Map B (No Enrichment) x Retard Multiplier B (No Enrichment)/256; with enrichment the (Enriched) tables are used; with FFF8A8A5 bit 4 set (flag from 0x11B2A4 on vehicle speed, pedal and load; not decoded) the (FFF8A8A5 Bit 4) tables. Maps are rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616. FFF8C562 = S filtered (weight 05A578 while FFF8AFCC is rising, 05A5A0 while falling, by rpm x load); FFF8C564 = (U - S + fuel-cut term FFF8B040) filtered (weights 05A680 / 05A6A8 by air quantity FFF8B4D6 x FFF8B066); estimate FFF8AFD0 = FFF8C562 + FFF8C564, so in steady state FFF8AFD0 tends to Map B. 0x0CE854 enables Primary Open Loop Fueling while FFF8AFD0 >= cal 0x18DD4 (39322, hysteresis cal 0x18DD6 = 2185), and 0x0C5880 integrates 05A82C(FFF8AFD0) into FFF8C03C, the second enable path (read). Reading FFF8AFD0 as an exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate is inferred: the enriched maps are lower than the stoichiometric ones, retard raises the value (multiplier 0.75 at 25 degrees advanced to 1.2 at 20 degrees retarded) and the value gates the enrichment. Raising these maps brings Primary Open Loop Fueling in earlier (lower load); lowering them delays it. Descriptor 05A564. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (No Enrichment)
table.description:
Second exhaust/catalyst temperature estimate (inferred), by rpm and load, with no enrichment active. When it gets high enough the ECU skips the delay before open loop fueling. Raising it brings open loop in sooner.
Details: When used: always while running. Map while no open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8A684 = 0). 0x0C965C (read): FFF8AFCE = filtered (Enrichment-dependent Map x Retard Multiplier (05A538 no enrichment / 05A52C enriched / 05A544 with FFF8A8A5 bit 4) / 256), maps on rpm FFF8CD54 x load FFF8A616; filter weight 05A4C8 while FFF8AFCC rises, 05A4F0 (05A504 with FFF8A8A5 bit 4) while it falls, 05A4DC rising with the bit, the previous weight when unchanged. 0x0C95F8: FFF8AFCC = FFF8AFCE filtered by 05A48C(rpm, load). table.name: Exhaust Temperature Estimate 2 Map (Standstill High Load)
table.description:

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor
table.description:
On a hot restart, the A/F sensor exhaust model starts from the pipe temperature stored at engine stop, multiplied by this factor by how much the coolant has dropped since. Stock 1.0 at no drop to 0.7 at 30 C drop. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs (FFF8906B != 3) on a hot restart: coolant at start >= 60 C (50 C to stay, cals 0x4234D/0x4234C) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= 80 C (cal 0x4234F = 130). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water (stock 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.2 kPa at 30 C, 94 kPa at 98 C, in kPa x 8192 - read values); 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x1802F4 (read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature FFF8BAB8 (K x 32) starts at the value stored at the last engine stop FFF815BA (0x1802D4) x this(coolant drop since the engine last ran)/256; on other starts it starts at min(IAT, coolant) - 05F1F0 (0 in stock). FFF8069B is the coolant copied every pass while running (0x06BA46, read). Stock 1.00, 0.90, 0.80, 0.70 at 0, 10, 20, 30 C drop (0-54 F). Descriptor 05F1E4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level. Stock w = 1 at or below 84 kPa (about 5200 ft) and 0 at or above 98 kPa (about 1000 ft), so near sea level only the B tables are used. S = set 1 or set 2, chosen by FFF8A8A4 bit 7 (stack argument +24 from 0x15969C, read). That bit is a high-pedal latch (0x11C15C / 0x10F848, read): it sets when the accelerator FFF88A5E is at or above High Pedal Entry Threshold (90 % stock, by barometric pressure) while vehicle speed is not jumping (under cal 0x35B16... per gear) and some status flags (FFF88A2D bit 0, FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF8A8A2 bit 6) are clear, or when FFF8A8A5 bit 2 or 4 is set; it clears once the pedal is below cal 0x36518 (85 %). So set 1 = normal driving and set 2 = near wide-open pedal (meaning inferred from these conditions). In stock (sea-level B tables), intake set 2 differs from set 1 across the map: about +10...+35 degrees more advance below 1.03 g/rev and about 10...20 degrees less advance at 1.29 g/rev and above from 1200 to 4400 rpm, equal from 5600 rpm; exhaust set 2 differs mainly below 1.03 g/rev; the altitude (A) sets differ only below 0.52 g/rev. The set-3 terms are active because cal 0x3ACF6 = 1 in both images. Set 1, A table (weight w). Stock -11...30 degrees. Descriptor 05E4BC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Speed Target (In Drive, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive with the brake on (pedal released, slow). Never used on a manual car (inferred). Stock 1200 rpm cold to 650 rpm hot, 50 rpm below the warm idle in neutral.
Details: When used: only with the automatic/CVT coding, while the in-Drive idle condition FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant): automatic coding, neutral input clear, pedal released, slow) and afterwards until the in-Drive idle air reduction FFF8B160 has ramped back to its target (FFF8A7E4 bit 2 clear; 0x0F3A40, 0x0F522C with cal 0x23CE9 bit 1 = 1 stock, read). Never on a manual car (inferred from that chain). 0x0F2248 (read): when FFF8A7E4 bit 4 is set, B242 = this(coolant) << 6 (12.5 rpm per count) replaces the idle-mode target chain. Stock 1200 rpm cold -> 650 rpm hot (50 rpm below the Mode 5 warm idle, as expected for an automatic in gear). Descriptor 05C76C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Mode 2 to 7)
table.description:
How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 2 (cold post-start) to mode 7 (warm-up drive-off). Larger = quicker change towards the new idle target; smaller = a gentler fade.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Coolant FFF88A44 axis. Mode 1 -> 1 uses step 0. This table: mode 2 -> 7. p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Descriptor 05C640. Confidence: read.

How fast the idle speed target moves (by coolant) when idle switches from mode 1 (engine stopped) to mode 6 (AT/CVT warm idle). Larger = quicker change. Automatic/CVT only: these modes never occur on a manual car, so this table has no effect there.

Modes 6/8 only occur with the AT/CVT coding: 0x0F2BCC passes A7F6 through when FFF88ADA bit7 is set (manual coding, stock here) and 0x0F354C itself only yields 1-5/7, so this step is never used by this MT calibration (read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. table.name: Idle Speed Target (Cold Idle, Mode 4, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle speed target by coolant for a cold-idle mode used when stopped below a coolant threshold. No effect on a stock car: the thresholds that enter this mode are 0 in stock, so it never occurs.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. Both cals are 0 in stock, so mode 4 never occurs in stock (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F1BCC selects this boot-format table by idle mode FFF8A7F0 = 4 and coolant; the result B238 is ramped (0x0F1D00) and becomes the idle target FFF8B236 through the minimum-speed max() in 0x0F2274 (read). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Data at 024AF0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set (manual-car version). Probably never used on a stock car: that fallback is switched off by a calibration setting in stock (inferred).
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch, gated off in stock by cal 0x59134 bit0 = 0 (my research notes), so never used in stock (inferred from that trace). This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is set, which is always the case with the manual coding (0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Descriptor 05C760. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Target Ramp Rate (Fallback Latch, AT/CVT, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Idle target ramp rate (by coolant) used when a warm-up fallback flag is set, on automatic/CVT cars. Probably never used on a stock car: that fallback is switched off by a calibration setting in stock (inferred), and a manual car uses the other Fallback Latch table.
Details: 0x0F1DD0 (read; selection checked in the disassembly 0x0F1DD0..0x0F2148): the target ramp step B23E is chosen on a change of idle mode FFF8A7F0 (previous -> new) and kept while the mode stays the same; the target B23C (4 x B238) moves toward the new mode's Idle Speed Target by this step every pass (0x0F1D00). Used instead of the mode table when FFF899D7 bit0 rises while the idle mode is unchanged (index 98/99, 0x0F1DD0, read). FFF899D7 bit0 is the warm-up fallback latch, gated off in stock by cal 0x59134 bit0 = 0 (my research notes), so never used in stock (inferred from that trace). This one when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear, which happens only with the AT/CVT coding (AT state FFF8A7DD 0 or 5; 0x0EC7A4/0x0F38B0, read). p16 (read): 0x0F1D00 runs every 10 ms (module 0x0EE338), so rpm/s = shown rpm-per-pass x 100. Descriptor 05C754. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle (the warm-idle mode on a manual car), used while the TGVs are commanded open. At a settled warm idle the TGVs are normally commanded closed, so Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed) is probably the table in use: change both together, and together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) so idle feedback does not have to learn the difference. Stock hot value is about 1.9 % throttle.
Details: When used: idle mode 5, normal idle (the warm-idle mode of a manual car). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant; the TGV-closed set is used while FFF8A881 bit4. Hot stock mode-5 value 1536 (TGV normal) / 1408 (closed) -> ~1.9 % throttle. Change with the idle speed target so the feedback need not learn the difference. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC (lookup 0x7414, read). Data at 02503E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Mode 5, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant for normal warm idle while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with Idle Speed Target (Warm Idle, Mode 5) and Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Stock hot value slightly below the TGV-open table.
Details: When used: idle mode 5, normal idle (the warm-idle mode of a manual car). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant; this TGV-closed table is used while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set. Hot stock mode-5 value 1536 (TGV open) / 1408 (closed) -> ~1.9 % throttle. Change with the idle speed target so the feedback need not learn the difference. Implicit coolant axis -40..110 degC (lookup 0x7414, read). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Data at 024F5E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant right after a cold start (below 75 degC) until the car moves or the engine warms, and while stopped, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. The TGV Closed table is used whenever the TGVs are commanded closed, which is the normal state at low torque, so change both together.
Details: When used: idle mode 1 (engine stopped, or dropped out of the running state) and mode 2 (after a start with coolant below 75 C / 167 F, until the car moves or, once the warm-up flag FFF88EA2 bit 1 has cleared, coolant reaches 50 C / 122 F; held at least 200 time-since-start counts) (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Data at 024FDE. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Post-Start, Modes 1/2, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant right after a cold start (below 75 degC) until the car moves or the engine warms, and while stopped, used while the TGVs are commanded closed (the normal state at low torque, probably including warm idle). Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target and the normal Idle Base Air table for this mode.
Details: When used: idle mode 1 (engine stopped, or dropped out of the running state) and mode 2 (after a start with coolant below 75 C / 167 F, until the car moves or, once the warm-up flag FFF88EA2 bit 1 has cleared, coolant reaches 50 C / 122 F; held at least 200 time-since-start counts) (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Data at 024EFE. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Warm Start, Mode 3)
table.description:
Base (open-loop) idle air by coolant after a hot restart (coolant at or above 75 degC at start) until the car moves, used while the TGVs are commanded open. Change it together with the matching Idle Speed Target so idle feedback does not have to make up the difference. Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Data at 024FFE. Confidence: read.

Details: When used: idle mode 3, after a start with coolant at or above 75 C / 167 F (hot restart). Extra idle air given for the first 0.4 s after the A/C compressor engages (then it fades to the matching A/C Idle Air Steady value), for: A/C load switch off, neutral switch on, car moving above 14 km/h. Raise if idle dips when the A/C kicks in. 0 = no kick. The A/C load switch meaning is inferred.
Details: 0x0EC10C (stock path, cal 0x1D0AE bit0 = 0; call 0x0EF446 in module 0x0EE338, stack args checked) (read): while FFF8A9A2 bit6 (A/C compressor engaged, inferred) the A/C idle air FFF8B1A0 = max(kick part, steady part). For the first 40 passes = 0.4 s (cals 0x35195/0x35194) the kick part is the Initial Kick table, then it falls by 256 raw = 128 base-air units per 10 ms (cals 0x35192/0x35190) toward the Steady table. Selectors (read): FFF88BC6 bit7 = discrete input FFF8A29C bit5 (pin PA8, active low; an A/C load / refrigerant-pressure switch, inferred) debounced 300 x 10 ms = 3.0 s (0x080A64, 0x08058A), FFF88ADA bit6 = discrete input FFF8A29E bit5 (neutral switch, pin PH5, confirmed by its P0851/P0852 monitor 0x06F436), vehicle speed FFF88BE8 (km/h x 17.8) above 14 km/h (cal 0x35196 = 249), held until below 4 km/h (249 - cal 0x35198 178). B1A0 enters the idle air at half weight (0x0EC09C -> 0x0F0AF8), so values are shown in base-air units. Logged as FFF8B4F0. This table: FFF88BC6 bit7 clear, FFF88ADA bit6 set, vehicle moving (>14 km/h). 0 = no kick. p16 (read): A29C.5 = port pin PA8, active low (sampler 0x1D3C9A, 4 ms two-sample filter 0x1D4122, copy 0x1E2F20); 88E2F b1 -> 88BC6 b7 after 300 consecutive 10 ms passes (3.0 s, cals 0x57734/0x57736); also sent on CAN 0x360 byte 6 bit 6 and selects the compressor torque adder (A292 b5) - an A/C load / pressure switch (inferred). 'Neutral Sw' = FFF8A29E b5 = pin PH5, confirmed by its P0851/P0852 monitor 0x06F436. 0x0EC10C runs every 10 ms. Data at 03535A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, Coolant)
table.description:
Idle air taken away, by coolant, while an automatic/CVT car idles in Drive (pedal released, slow) to offset the load of the transmission. Never used on a manual car. Stock large when cold, small when hot.
Details: When used: only while FFF8A7E4 bit 0 is set (0x0F38D0, read): automatic coding (FFF886AB bit 7 clear) and the neutral input FFF88ADA bit 6 clear, accelerator released, speed FFF99835 within cals 0x2583F..0x25841, rpm below cal 0x25842 and below @025886(coolant), no speed-sensor/CAN faults; so never on a manual car (read). 0x0EAA40 (read): FFF8B162 = this(coolant) + Idle Air Reduction In Drive (RPM Error)(rpm - target rpm FFF8B236, coolant) + a ramp term (cals 0x25838..0x2583C), >= 0, capped by @025846(coolant); FFF8B160 follows it at cal 0x25834/0x25836 (86) per pass and is subtracted at half weight from the idle air FFF8B200 (0x0F0AF8, read). Stock raw 22528 cold to 768 hot (11264..384 in the idle-air unit). Descriptor 05C210. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Reduction In Drive (AT/CVT, RPM Error)
table.description:
Correction to Idle Air Reduction In Drive by rpm error (actual minus target) and coolant, for automatic/CVT cars idling in Drive. Never used on a manual car. Stock 0 at no error.
Details: When used: see Idle Air Reduction In Drive (Coolant) (automatic coding only). 0x0EAA40 (read): added to the coolant term with the rpm error FFF8CE9C - FFF8B236 (s16, rpm x 5.12) and coolant FFF88A44 as axes. Stock 0 at no error, about +-1000 base-air units (as shown; +-2000 raw) per 50 rpm cold, about +-300 (as shown) hot. Descriptor 05C21C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward (AT/CVT, State 0/5)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT version of Idle Air Target-Change Feed-Forward, used in two transmission states only: extra or less idle air applied immediately when the idle speed target changes, by the size of the step.
Details: 0x0ECA08 (read; call 0x0ECA88/0x0ECA94 R5 checked): while FFF88A26 bit0 (idle, inferred), engine running (FFF88A27 bit0 clear) and FFF99835 below cal 0x259C8 (255, i.e. always), B1AE = this(new target - ramped target = B236 - B23C/4, capped at cal 0x259CA = 1000 rpm); B1AE enters the idle air at half weight. A positive step (target raised) adds air ahead of the ramp. Used when FFF8A7E2 bit0 is clear (bit0 = FFF8A7DD in 1..4 or 6, 0x0F38B0). Stock -947..+847 base-air units over -200..+200 rpm. Descriptor 05C394. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4. No effect on a stock car: the thresholds that enter mode 4 are 0 in stock, so it never occurs.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. Both cals are 0 in stock, so mode 4 never occurs in stock (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is clear (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). Data at 02501E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Base Air (Cold Idle, Mode 4, TGV Closed, Off in Stock)
table.description:
Base idle air by coolant for the cold-idle mode 4 with the TGVs commanded closed. No effect on a stock car: the thresholds that enter mode 4 are 0 in stock, so it never occurs.
Details: When used: idle mode 4, entered from mode 5 when stopped with coolant below cal 0x24E94 for cal 0x24E96 passes. Both cals are 0 in stock, so mode 4 never occurs in stock (read, 0x0F354C). 0x0F0D24: base idle air B20C by idle mode FFF8A7F0 and coolant, this table while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGV close command) is set (read). Scale as Idle Base Air (Mode 5). Raise it with this mode's idle speed target so the feedback need not cover the difference (inferred). Implicit coolant axis -40..110 C in 10 C steps (lookup 0x7414). FFF8A881 bit 4 is the normal TGV-close command (0x10DEFC, set mainly by the timed close request FFF8A883 bit 5 from 0x10E180 when requested torque, coolant and air flow are below the TGV thresholds; the same bit selects every TGV-closed table), not a forced or fault state (read). At a settled warm idle the request conditions hold, so the TGVs are normally commanded closed and the TGV Closed table is probably the one in use (inferred). Data at 024F3E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Positive)
table.description:
Limit on a positive idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. Stock 1.0 at the idle opening, falling to 0.1 from about 35 %. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred).
Details: When used: every 10 ms pass while running and the carry-over at hand-over B178 is positive. Input FFF88A3C, throttle opening above the idle opening (0x08015C, read; % scale inferred). Stock 1.0 with the throttle at the idle opening, 0.5 at about 12 %, 0.3 at 24 %, 0.1 from about 35 %. 0x0EAC1C (read; called from the 10 ms idle module 0x0EE338 with FFF8906B, B180, A7E0 bit 4, FFF8CEA6, FFF88A3C): in the pass where idle speed feedback switches off (FFF8A7E0 bit 4 falls), the feedback air B180 is added to the carry-over FFF8B174 (clamped -2375..4751 by cals 0x25730/0x25732) and copied to B178. B174 then enters the idle air at half weight next to B180 (B1FE = (2 x B200 + B180 + B174) x F/64, 0x0F0A90) and decays every pass: a positive carry-over falls by Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Positive) and may not exceed B178 x Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Positive)/255; a negative one rises by the (Negative) decay and may not go below B178 x the (Negative) limit/255 (read). So the air the feedback had added when the driver leaves idle is kept and released gradually (dashpot-like, inferred). Engine state 3 only. Descriptor 05C248. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Negative)
table.description:
Limit on a negative idle-feedback carry-over, as a fraction by throttle opening above idle. Stock 1.0 at the idle opening, 0 from about 24 %, so a negative carry-over is removed once the throttle opens. The carried-over air keeps the air idle feedback had added when leaving idle and releases it gradually (dashpot-like, inferred).
Details: When used: every 10 ms pass while running and the carry-over at hand-over B178 is negative. Input FFF88A3C (as the Positive limit). Stock 1.0 at the idle opening, 0.5 at about 12 %, 0 from about 24 % (a negative carry-over is removed once the throttle opens). 0x0EAC1C (read; called from the 10 ms idle module 0x0EE338 with FFF8906B, B180, A7E0 bit 4, FFF8CEA6, FFF88A3C): in the pass where idle speed feedback switches off (FFF8A7E0 bit 4 falls), the feedback air B180 is added to the carry-over FFF8B174 (clamped -2375..4751 by cals 0x25730/0x25732) and copied to B178. B174 then enters the idle air at half weight next to B180 (B1FE = (2 x B200 + B180 + B174) x F/64, 0x0F0A90) and decays every pass: a positive carry-over falls by Idle Feedback Carry-Over Decay (Positive) and may not exceed B178 x Idle Feedback Carry-Over Limit (Positive)/255; a negative one rises by the (Negative) decay and may not go below B178 x the (Negative) limit/255 (read). So the air the feedback had added when the driver leaves idle is kept and released gradually (dashpot-like, inferred). Engine state 3 only. Descriptor 05C254. Confidence: read.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as stopped in gear for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car. Stock 200 rpm cold to 60 rpm warm, always met from 100 degC.
Details: When used: AT/CVT codings, standstill in gear. Input FFF88A44 (coolant, read in the disassembly by the same R5). Stock 200 rpm to 0 degC, 150 at 10, 80 at 20-60, 70 at 70, 60 at 80-90 degC, -6400 (always met) from 100 degC. 0x0EC7A4 (read; called from 0x0EE338 with FFF886AB bit 7, neutral FFF88ADA bit 6, CAN fault FFF88E2B bit 1, FFF8A7E2 bit 1, FFF8B140, coolant FFF88A44, time since start FFF88A76, speed FFF99835): on the manual coding FFF8A7DD is always 1, so these tables are AT/CVT only. FFF8B140 = engine rpm FFF8CD54 - FFF888AC x 128/25 (0x0E9EE8, read); FFF888AC comes from the TCM frame 0x148 (signals_rates_can.md, read), so B140 is the torque-converter slip in rpm (inferred). State 4 (stopped in gear) needs slip >= Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear) (hysteresis cal 0x25648), state 6 (neutral/park) needs slip > Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral) (hysteresis cal 0x25646) and FFF88A76 > cal 0x25642 (read). FFF8A7DD selects the idle table sets named "(AT/CVT, State ...)" through FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (0x0F38B0). Descriptor 05C35C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral, AT/CVT)
table.description:
Automatic/CVT only: converter slip, by coolant, needed for the ECU to treat the car as in neutral/park for idle control (probably torque-converter slip). Never used on a manual car. Stock 500-700 rpm cold to 200 rpm from 90 degC.
Details: When used: AT/CVT codings, in neutral/park. Input FFF88A44 (coolant). Stock 500 rpm to -10 degC, 700 at 0-20, 600 at 30-40, 550 at 50, 500 at 60, 400 at 70, 300 at 80, 200 rpm from 90 degC. 0x0EC7A4 (read; called from 0x0EE338 with FFF886AB bit 7, neutral FFF88ADA bit 6, CAN fault FFF88E2B bit 1, FFF8A7E2 bit 1, FFF8B140, coolant FFF88A44, time since start FFF88A76, speed FFF99835): on the manual coding FFF8A7DD is always 1, so these tables are AT/CVT only. FFF8B140 = engine rpm FFF8CD54 - FFF888AC x 128/25 (0x0E9EE8, read); FFF888AC comes from the TCM frame 0x148 (signals_rates_can.md, read), so B140 is the torque-converter slip in rpm (inferred). State 4 (stopped in gear) needs slip >= Idle Converter Slip Threshold (In Gear) (hysteresis cal 0x25648), state 6 (neutral/park) needs slip > Idle Converter Slip Threshold (Neutral) (hysteresis cal 0x25646) and FFF88A76 > cal 0x25642 (read). FFF8A7DD selects the idle table sets named "(AT/CVT, State ...)" through FFF8A7E2 bit 0 (0x0F38B0). Descriptor 05C368. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Minimum
table.description:
EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or above this. Stock -50 degC, i.e. no limit; warm-up is handled by EGR Target Rate Coolant Multiplier instead.
Details: 0x0FAAFC: EGR enable needs coolant FFF8CD65 (degC + 50) >= this (minus cal 0x2C4D6 = 5 once met) (read). Stock 0 (-50 degC, i.e. no limit; warm-up is handled by EGR Target Rate Coolant Multiplier). Address 02C4D5. Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Enable Coolant Maximum
table.description:
EGR is only enabled when coolant is at or below this. Stock 200 degC, i.e. no limit.
Details: 0x0FAAFC: EGR enable needs coolant FFF8CD65 <= this (plus cal 0x2C4D8 = 5 once met) (read). Stock 250 (200 degC, no limit). Address 02C4D7. Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Enable RPM Minimum
table.description:
EGR is only enabled when rpm is at or above this. Stock 0, i.e. no limit.
Details: 0x0FAAFC: EGR enable needs rpm FFF8CE9C >= this (minus cal 0x2C4DC once met) (read). Stock 0. Address 02C4DA. Confidence: read.

table.name: EGR Enable Load Minimum
